````txt
\title{Probing heavy Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator through vector boson fusion processes in proton-proton collisions at \texorpdfstring{$\sqrt{s}~=~13~\TeV$}{sqrt(s) = 13 TeV}}
\date{\today}
\abstract{The first search exploiting the vector boson fusion process to probe heavy Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator at the LHC is presented. The search is performed in the same-sign dimuon final state using a proton-proton collision dataset recorded at $\sqrt{s}=13\TeV$, collected with the CMS detector and corresponding to a total integrated luminosity of 138\fbinv. The results are found to agree with the predictions of the standard model. For heavy Majorana neutrinos, constraints on the squared mixing element between the muon and the heavy neutrino are derived in the heavy neutrino mass range $50\GeV$--$25\TeV$; for masses above 650\GeV these are the most stringent constraints from searches at the LHC to date. A first test of the Weinberg operator at colliders provides an observed upper limit at 95\% confidence level on the effective $\PGm\PGm$ Majorana neutrino mass of 10.8\GeV.}
\hypersetup{
pdfauthor={CMS Collaboration},
pdftitle={Probing Majorana neutrinos and Weinberg operator in di-muon channel through vector boson fusion processes in proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV},
pdfsubject={CMS},
pdfkeywords={CMS, Majorana neutrino, Weinberg operator, vector boson fusion}}
\maketitle
Despite the enormous success of the standard model (SM) of particle physics over the last fifty years, the observation of neutrino oscillations~\cite{SNO:2002tuh,Super-Kamiokande:2005mbp} has confirmed that at least two SM neutrinos have small, but nonzero, masses. This provides a compelling hint of physics beyond the SM. Efforts to determine each neutrino mass are being pursued by many experiments within different research fields, including cosmology and tritium beta decay~\cite{Loureiro:2018pdz,eBOSS:2020yzd,KATRIN:2021uub}, and various theoretical explanations of these observations have been proposed~\cite{seesaw1,seesaw2,seesaw3,seesaw4,Weinberg79,Das:2015toa,Das:2016hof,Das:2017nvm}.
A natural formalism for generating neutrino masses is through a dimension-five operator, proposed by Weinberg~\cite{Weinberg79}, which extends the SM Lagrangian with
\begin{linenomath}
\begin{equation}
\lag_5 = \frac{\mathrm{C}_5^{\ell\ell'}}{\Lambda} \big[\Phi\!~\cdot~\! \overline{L}^c_{\ell }\big] \big[L_{\ell'}\!\!~\cdot~\!\Phi\big],
\label{eqn:Lag_5}
\end{equation}
\end{linenomath}
where $\ell ,~\ell'$ are the flavors of the leptons, which can be electrons, muons, or taus; $\Lambda$ is the scale at which the particles responsible for neutrino masses become relevant degrees of freedom; $\mathrm{C}_5^{\ell\ell'}$ is a flavor-dependent Wilson coefficient; $L_\ell=(\nu_\ell,\ell)$ is the left-handed lepton doublet; and $\Phi$ is the SM Higgs doublet with a vacuum expectation value $v=\sqrt{2}\langle\Phi\rangle\approx246\GeV$. This operator, known as the Weinberg operator, generates the Majorana neutrino masses as
\begin{linenomath}
\begin{equation}
m_{\ell\ell'} = C_5^{\ell\ell'} v^2/\Lambda,
\label{eqn:Majorana_N_mass}
\end{equation}
\end{linenomath}
and introduces lepton number violation (LNV), as the Majorana neutrino is its own antiparticle. The LNV processes have been tested extensively in searches for neutrinoless double beta decays of heavy nuclei. These experiments search for events with two same-sign (SS) charge electrons and the absence of neutrinos in the final state, and set stringent upper limits on the associated Majorana neutrino mass ($ \abs{m_{ee}}$) at 90\% confidence level (\CL) in the ranges 61--165\unit{meV}~\cite{KamLAND-Zen:2016pfg} and 79--180\unit{meV}~\cite{Agostini:2020xta}.
Since muons and tau leptons are much heavier than electrons, SS final states involving these heavier leptons are kinematically forbidden in low-energy nuclear experiments and can only be studied at colliders~\cite{Fuks:2020zbm}. As the study of tau leptons is experimentally more challenging, the final state with SS muons is investigated in this search. The observed upper limit on the effective $\PGm\PGm$ Majorana neutrino mass ($\abs{m_{\PGm\PGm}}$), translated from the searches for LNV decays of charged kaons at the NA62 experiment~\cite{NA62:2019eax}, is around 55\GeV at 90\% \CL~\cite{Fuks:2020zbm}.
The Weinberg operator can be realized in the context of ``seesaw'' models~\cite{seesaw1,seesaw2,seesaw3,seesaw4}, assuming the existence of hypothetical heavy states, for example a heavy Majorana neutrino ($\mathit{N}$) in the type-I seesaw model. The small mass of the SM neutrinos can thus be explained by a suppression due to the high mass of new particles, because $ m_\nu\sim y_\nu^2v^2/ \mN$. In this expression, $m_\nu$ is the SM neutrino mass, $ \mN$ is the mass of the heavy Majorana neutrino, and $y_\nu$ is the Yukawa coupling. This ability to explain the small mass of the SM neutrinos motivates the search for heavy Majorana neutrinos. Heavy Majorana neutrinos can only couple to the SM through mixing with SM neutrinos, which is characterized by the mixing element, $\Vln$, between a SM neutrino in its left-handed interaction state and a \hmn in its mass eigenstate. The searches that have set limits on $\Vln$ were based on the production of a \hmn through either quark-antiquark annihilation or $W\PGg$, with different analysis strategies based on various decay modes, such as many leptons in the final state~\cite{Sirunyan:2018mtv,Aad:2019kiz,Sirunyan:2019bgz}, and in final states containing LNV lepton pairs~\cite{Sirunyan:2018xiv,Aaboud:2018spl}. For $ \mN$ at a few \GeVns{}, the constraints on $\abs{\Vln}^{2}$, where $\ell=\left\{e, \Pgm \right\}$, are around $10^{-7}$--$10^{-5}$, while at around 1\TeV, the constraints approach unity.
This Letter reports the first search probing Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator in vector boson fusion (VBF) processes~\cite{Fuks:2020zbm,Fuks:2020att} at the CERN LHC, studying events with SS muon pairs.
As shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:diagram} by the two representative Feynman diagrams, in the $t$ channel, SS $W$ boson pairs may convert to SS lepton pairs via a \TeVns{}-scale Majorana neutrino or through a Weinberg operator process. Because the cross section of $t$-channel processes is less sensitive to the mass of the intermediate particle compared with $s$-channel quark-antiquark annihilation processes, the VBF process can complement searches for heavy Majorana neutrinos at the \TeVns{} mass scale as its cross section decreases more slowly with increasing $N$ mass compared with the values from $s$-channel production. Although the various seesaw mechanisms can be considered as realizations of the Weinberg operator, an alternative implementation is considered in this Letter, as shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:diagram} (right). The two VBF processes considered in this work differ primarily in that the Majorana process is assumed to be mediated by a heavy $t$-channel neutrino whereas the Weinberg operator process is mediated by a lighter $t$-channel neutrino.
\begin{figure}[h!]\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.40\linewidth]{Figure_001-a.pdf}
\hspace{13pt}
\includegraphics[width=0.40\linewidth]{Figure_001-b.pdf}
\caption{Example Feynman diagrams of VBF processes with heavy Majorana neutrino production (left) and processes mediated by the Weinberg operator (right) at the LHC.}\label{fig:diagram}
\end{figure}
This analysis is based on proton-proton ($pp$) collision data collected at $\sqrt{s} = 13\TeV$ by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC during 2016--2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $138\fbinv$.
Tabulated results are provided in the HEPData record for this analysis~\cite{hepdata}.
The CMS apparatus~\cite{CMS:2008xjf} is a multipurpose, nearly hermetic detector, designed to trigger on~\cite{CMS:2020cmk,CMS:2016ngn}
and identify electrons, muons, photons, and hadrons~\cite{CMS:2020uim,CMS:2018rym,CMS:2014pgm}. A global ``particle-flow'' algorithm~\cite{CMS:2017yfk} aims to reconstruct all individual particles in an event, combining information provided by the all-silicon inner tracker and by the crystal electromagnetic and brass-scintillator hadron calorimeters, operating inside a 3.8\unit{T} superconducting solenoid, with data from gas-ionization muon detectors embedded in the flux-return yoke outside the solenoid. The reconstructed particles are used to build charged leptons, jets, and missing transverse momentum ($\pTvecmiss$)~\cite{CMS:2018jrd,CMS:2016lmd,CMS:2019ctu}.
Samples of signal events are simulated with next-to-leading order (NLO) precision using the \MGvATNLO 2.6.5 generator~\cite{Alwall:2014hca}, based on model implementations from Refs.~\cite{Fuks:2020zbm,Alva:2014gxa,Degrande:2016aje,Fuks:2020att}. For the heavy Majorana neutrino, we assume only one heavy state and scan its mass in a range from 50\GeV to 25\TeV. The process induced by the Weinberg operator is simulated using a novel approach, established in Ref.~\cite{Fuks:2020zbm}, which approximates the internal neutrino lines and vertex insertion with an effective light Majorana neutrino. The Wilson coefficient $\mathrm{C}_5^{\ell\ell'}$ is set to 1, and the energy scale $\Lambda$ to 200\TeV. The production cross sections scale with $\Vln ^{2} \Vlnprime^{2}$ and $\abs{\mathrm{C}_5^{\ell\ell'}/\Lambda }^{2}$ for the VBF processes with heavy Majorana neutrinos~\cite{Fuks:2020att} and the Weinberg operator~\cite{Fuks:2020zbm}, respectively. Since the kinematic shape of the signal is independent of $\abs{ \Vmn }$, we set $\abs{ \Vmn } = 1$ for the signal simulation to ensure efficient generation of signal events.
The SM electroweak $\WW$ and $W^{\pm} Z$ processes, where both bosons decay leptonically, are simulated using \MGvATNLO 2.4.2~\cite{Alwall:2014hca} at leading order (LO) with six electroweak $\left[ \mathcal{O}(\alpha^6) \right]$ and zero quantum chromodynamics (QCD) vertices. The QCD-induced $\WW$ process is also simulated using \MGvATNLO 2.4.2 at LO. Contributions with an initial-state $b$ quark are excluded from the electroweak $W^{\pm} Z$ simulation because they are included in the production of a $Z$ boson in association with a single top quark, known as the $tZq$ process, which is simulated at NLO using \MGvATNLO 2.3.3.
The $ZZ \to 4 \ell$ and $gg \to ZZ$ processes are simulated with the $\POWHEG$ v2~\cite{Nason:2013ydw} and $\MCFM$ 7.0.1~\cite{Campbell:2011bn} generators, respectively. The production of $\TTBar W^{\pm}$, $\TTBar Z$, and triple vector boson ($VVV$) background events is simulated at NLO in QCD using the \MGvATNLO 2.2.2 (2.4.2) generator~\cite{Alwall:2014hca,MadGraph,Frederix:2012ps} for the samples corresponding to the 2016 (2017--2018) data-taking period. The production of $\WW$ events through double-parton scattering is generated at LO using \PYTHIA 8.226 (8.230)~\cite{Sjostrand:2014zea} for 2016 (2017--2018).
The simulated samples for the 2016 (2017--2018) data-taking period use the NNPDF 3.0 (3.1) parton distribution functions~\cite{Ball:2014uwa,Ball:2017nwa}, and are interfaced with \PYTHIA to model the fragmentation and hadronization of partons in the initial and final states, along with the underlying event. The CUETP8M1 (CP5) tune~\cite{Khachatryan:2015pea,Sirunyan:2019dfx} is used in the simulation for the 2016 (2017--2018) data-taking period. In LO (NLO) simulations performed with \MGvATNLO, jets are matched to the parton shower produced by \PYTHIA 8.2 following the MLM~\cite{Alwall:2007fs} (FxFx~\cite{Frederix:2012ps}) prescription. The interactions of all final-state particles with the CMS detector are simulated using \GEANTfour~\cite{Agostinelli:2002hh}. Simulated events are mixed with the contribution of particles from additional $pp$ interactions within the same or nearby bunch crossings (pileup); the pileup distribution in the simulated samples matches that observed in data.
Collision events are collected using single-muon triggers~\cite{CMS:2016ngn} that require the presence of an isolated muon with transverse momentum $\pT > 24$ or 27\GeV, depending on the data-taking period. In addition, a set of dimuon triggers~\cite{CMS:2016ngn} with lower $\pT$ thresholds is used to ensure a trigger efficiency above 90\% for events with muons. Depending on the subsequent off-line selection, the dimuon triggers increase the event acceptance by up to 4\%. The primary vertex (PV) is taken to be the vertex corresponding to the hardest scattering in the event, evaluated using tracking information alone, as described in Section 9.4.1 of Ref.~\cite{CMS-TDR-15-02}.
The jets are clustered using the anti-\kt algorithm~\cite{Cacciari:2011ma,Cacciari:2008gp} with a distance parameter of 0.4, with the tracks assigned to the candidate vertices as inputs. To mitigate the impact from pileup, tracks identified to be originating from pileup vertices are discarded and calorimeter energies are corrected to account for charged and neutral particles originating from those vertices. The $\pTvecmiss$ is then defined as the negative vector $\pT$ sum of all reconstructed particles in an event. Its magnitude is referred to as $\pTmiss$. Jets arising from $b$ quark hadronization and decay ($b$ jets) are identified using a deep neural network algorithm, termed \textsc{DeepCSV}, whose inputs are tracks displaced from the primary interaction vertex, details of secondary vertices, and the kinematical variables of jets~\cite{Sirunyan:2017ezt}. To classify jets as $b$ tagged, we use a requirement on the score of the \textsc{DeepCSV} algorithm for which the $b$ jet identification efficiency ranges from 65 to 75\% and the rate at which gluon or light-flavor jets are misidentified as $b$ jets is around 1\%. The fraction of jets originating from the hadronization of $c$ quarks that are incorrectly identified as $b$ jets is about 10\%.
Starting from the constituents of reconstructed jets, hadronically decaying $\tau$ leptons are identified via the ``hadrons-plus-strips'' algorithm~\cite{CMS:2018jrd}.
The final states analyzed contain two well-identified SS muons with $\pT > 30\GeV$ and pseudorapidity $\abs{\eta} < 2.4$, and at least two jets with $\pT > 30\GeV$ and $\abs{\eta} < 4.7$. The two selected jets with the largest $\pT$ are considered as the VBF jet candidates, which must satisfy a large pseudorapidity separation $\abs{\Delta\eta_{jj}} > 2.5$ and a large dijet invariant mass $m_{jj} > 750 \GeV$. Events produced via VBF are expected to contain rapidity gaps between the muons and the VBF jets. To utilize this signature, we require max$\left ( \mathcal{Z}_{\ell} \right ) < 0.75$, where $\mathcal{Z}_{\ell}$ is the Zeppenfeld variable~\cite{zepp1996} of a lepton $\ell$: $\mathcal{Z}_{\ell} = \abs{ \eta_{\ell} -(\eta_{j1}+\eta_{j2})/2 }/ \abs{ \Delta \eta_{jj} }$, where $\eta_{\ell}$ is the pseudorapidity of the lepton, and $\eta_{j1}$ and $\eta_{j2}$ are of the two VBF jets. Events with an additional loosely identified muon (electron) with $\pT > 10 \GeV$ and $\abs{\eta} < 2.5 (2.4)$ or an identified hadronically decaying tau lepton with $\pT > 20 \GeV$ and $\abs{\eta}<2.3$ are rejected to suppress backgrounds such as $W^{\pm} Z$ production. Because the signal processes do not produce final state neutrinos other than those produced in hadron decays, $\pTmiss$ is a useful discriminant to separate the signal and backgrounds. For the analysis targeting processes with heavy Majorana neutrinos, the azimuthal separation variable $\dphill$ is better for improving the sensitivity to the signal than $\pTmiss$ because the two muons in the final state tend to be more back-to-back than in background processes~\cite{Fuks:2020att}. However, $\pTmiss$ is more discriminating than azimuthal separation for the Weinberg operator process because of the different event topology resulting from the discrepancy between the two $t$-channel propagators. To separate the signal and the SM electroweak $\WW$ events, signal regions (SRs) for the \hmn and Weinberg operator analyses are defined in bins of $\dphill$ and $\pTmiss$, respectively. For the \hmn analysis, we define a high-$\dphill$ bin ($\dphill > 2$) and a low-$\dphill$ bin ($\dphill < 2$) in the SR. For the Weinberg operator analysis, a low-$\pTmiss$ bin ($<~$50\GeV) and a high-$\pTmiss$ bin ($>~$50\GeV) are defined in the SR.
The background from opposite-sign dilepton events where one of the lepton charges is misidentified is negligible for events with muon pairs~\cite{CMS:2009fdy,CMS:2019ied}. The so-called nonprompt-lepton backgrounds, originating from leptonic decays of heavy quarks or hadrons misidentified as leptons, are suppressed by identification and isolation requirements.
Events from a $\TTBar$ pair where only one $W$ boson decays leptonically are the main source of nonprompt-lepton backgrounds. To reduce this contribution, events with at least one $b$-tagged jet with $\pT > 20\GeV$ and $\abs{\eta}<2.4$ are rejected. The remaining contribution of the nonprompt-lepton background is estimated directly from a data sample by applying weights to events containing muon candidates that fail the nominal selection criteria while passing a less stringent isolation requirement. These weights, called fake-lepton factors, are obtained from the probability of a jet being misidentified as a lepton and the efficiency of correctly reconstructing and identifying a lepton. More details about this method are given in Refs.~\cite{Sirunyan:2018egh,CMS:2020dvg}.
To constrain the reducible background contributions, which include $W^{\pm} Z$ production and backgrounds from nonprompt leptons, several control regions (CRs) in data are used. These CRs are defined to select samples of events enriched in those background processes, following the procedure described in Refs.~\cite{Sirunyan:2017ret,Sirunyan:2020gyx,Sirunyan:2020gvn}.
A $WZ$ CR, requiring the presence of three muons in an event, is used to estimate $W^{\pm} Z$ background contributions. The opposite-sign dimuon combination with invariant mass closest to the $Z$ boson mass ($m_{Z}$) is considered as the $Z$ boson decay product, whereas the remaining muon is assumed to originate from the decay of the $W$ boson. The selection criteria defining the SR and the $WZ$ CR are summarized in Table~\ref{tab:regions}.
To select event samples enriched in nonprompt leptons, a $b$-tagged CR is defined by using the same selection as for the SR, however requiring the presence of a $b$-tagged jet. Similarly, the $WZb$ CR is defined by requiring the same selection as for the WZ CR, but requiring at least one $b$-tagged jet. The dominant backgrounds in the SR are SM electroweak $\WW$ production and the contribution from nonprompt leptons.
\begin{table*}[htbp]
\centering
\topcaption{Signal region and $WZ$ control region definitions. The signal region is binned differently for the heavy Majorana neutrino and Weinberg operator analyses. A $b$-tagged CR is defined by using the same selection as for the SR, however requiring the presence of a $b$-tagged jet. A $WZb$ CR is defined by requiring the same selection as for the $WZ$ CR, but requiring at least one $b$-tagged jet.}
\begin{scotch}{l c c}
Variable & SR & $WZ$ CR \\
\hline
Number of leptons & Exactly 2 same-sign muons & Exactly 3 muons \\
Lepton $\pT$ & $>~$30/30~\GeV & $>~$25/25/10~\GeV \\
Lepton \abs{\eta} & $<~$2.4 & $<~$2.4 \\
Jet $\pT$ & $>~$30~\GeV & $>~$30~\GeV \\
Jet \abs{\eta} & $<~$4.7 & $<~$4.7 \\
Dilepton mass $m_{\ell \ell}$ & $>~$20~\GeV & \NA \\
$\abs{m_{\ell \ell}-m_{Z}}$ & \NA & $<~$15~\GeV (for one $\PGmp\PGmm$ pair) \\
Trilepton mass $m_{\ell \ell \ell}$ & \NA & $>~$100~\GeV \\
Max $\left ( \mathcal{Z}_{\ell} \right )$ & $<~$0.75 & $<~$1.0 \\
$\pTmiss$ & \NA & $>~$30~\GeV \\
$b$-tagged jet veto & Required & Required \\
Hadronic $\tau$ veto & Required & Required \\
$\mjj$ & $>~$750~\GeV & $>~$750~\GeV \\
$\abs{\Delta\eta_{jj}}$ & $>~$2.5 & $>~$2.5 \\
\end{scotch}
\label{tab:regions}
\end{table*}
The discriminating variable used to search for a signal for both analyses is $\hT/\pT^{\PGm_1}$. Here, $\hT$ is the scalar sum of jet $\pT$ for all jets with $\pT>30\GeV$ and $\abs{\eta} < 4.7$, $\PGm_1$ indicates the highest $\pT$ muon.
This discriminating variable measures the amount of hadronic activity relative to leptonic activity in a given event, and is sensitive to the color structure of the hard scattering processes as discussed in Ref.~\cite{Fuks:2020zbm}. As hadronic activity is typically suppressed in VBF production processes, $\hT/\pT^{\PGm_1}$ tends to be smaller for signal events than for background events~\cite{Fuks:2020zbm,Fuks:2020att}.
The statistical analysis is performed with a profile likelihood ratio test statistic in which systematic uncertainties are modeled as constrained nuisance parameters. Limits are set using the modified frequentist \CLs criterion~\cite{CLS2,CLS1}, and the asymptotic approximation~\cite{Cowan:2010js} is used in the limit setting procedure. The integrated luminosities of the 2016, 2017, and 2018 data-taking periods are individually known with uncertainties in the range 1.2--2.5\%~\cite{CMS:2021xjt,CMS:2018elu,CMS:2019jhq}, while the uncertainty in the total integrated luminosity in 2016--2018 is 1.6\%. The simulation of pileup events assumes a total inelastic $pp$ cross section of 69.2\unit{mb}, with an associated uncertainty of 5\%~\cite{ATLAS:2016pu,Sirunyan:2018nqx}, which has an impact of approximately 1\% on the expected signal and background yields. Discrepancies in the lepton reconstruction and identification efficiencies between data and simulation are corrected for by applying scale factors to all simulated samples, and the associated uncertainty is around 2\%. Uncertainties in both the muon momentum scale and resolution individually amount to about 0.2\%. The simulated muon momentum resolution is corrected by applying a 15\% Gaussian smearing to muons with $\pT > 200\GeV$~\cite{CMS:2019ied}.
The resolution uncertainty and the momentum scale uncertainty for high-$\pT$ muons are less than 1\%. The uncertainty in the calibration of the jet energy scale (JES) directly affects the acceptance of the jet multiplicity requirement and the $\pTmiss$ measurement. These effects are estimated by shifting the JES in the simulation up and down by 1 standard deviation. The uncertainty in the JES is 2\%--5\%, depending on the jet $\pT$ and $\eta$~\cite{CMS:2016lmd,CMS-DP-2020-019}. Uncertainties in the $b$ tagging algorithm are introduced by various sources~\cite{Sirunyan:2017ezt}, and the overall impact on the simulated samples is less than 1\%. Theoretical uncertainties arising from the choice of the renormalization and factorization scales are estimated by varying these scales independently up and down by a factor of 2 from their nominal values, excluding the two extreme variations~\cite{Biedermann:2017bss}. The largest cross section variations from this procedure are taken as the uncertainty~\cite{Ballestrero:2018anz}, which is about 6\%, and which is applied to both the signal and the SM electroweak $\WW$ processes. The parton distribution function uncertainty of the signal and the SM electroweak $\WW$ processes is evaluated according to the procedure described in Ref.~\cite{PDFLHC}, and is found to be about 1\%. These uncertainties are not applied to the subdominant $\WZ$ background, where they are not significant compared to other uncertainties considered. For the nonprompt-lepton background prediction, systematic uncertainties arise from the limited size of the sample used to measure the efficiency and from the difference in the flavor composition of the jets that are misidentified as leptons between the measured sample and the signal region, estimated to amount to at most 5 and 7\%, respectively. An additional normalization uncertainty of 30\% is assigned to the nonprompt-lepton background, based on studies of simulated events~\cite{CMS:2020dvg}.
The statistical uncertainty in the signal and background templates is introduced as a systematic uncertainty via the Barlow-Beeston-lite approach~\cite{Barlow:1993dm}. This is the systematic uncertainty that has the largest impact on the results derived from the simultaneous fits described below. Uncertainties related to pileup, theoretical calculations, and the muon trigger and identification are correlated across the three data-taking years. The luminosity and $b$ tagging uncertainties are partially correlated through some of the individual uncertainty sources, and the remaining uncertainties are uncorrelated across the three datasets. The total uncertainties on the results are dominated by the statistical uncertainties.
Two separate fits are performed, based on the SR and the $b$-tagged, $WZ$, and $WZb$ CRs: one for the heavy Majorana neutrino analysis using $\dphill$ bins in the SR, and a second for the Weinberg operator analysis with the $\pTmiss$ bins in the SR. The normalization factors for the $\WW$, $\WZ$, and $tZq$ background processes, affecting both the SRs and CRs, are included as free parameters in the fit together with the signal strength. The predicted yields are shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:signal_region} with their best fit normalizations from the simultaneous fits for the background-only hypothesis, \ie assuming no contributions from processes involving heavy Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator. The bin boundaries are chosen to optimize the signal sensitivity while leaving the major background contributions in each bin at a reasonable level.
\begin{figure*}[htb!]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=1\textwidth]{Figure_002.pdf}
\caption{The $\hT/\pT^{\PGm_{1}}$ distribution in the SRs and CRs. The horizontal axis indicates the bin width. The predicted yields of the backgrounds are shown with their best fit normalizations from the simultaneous fits for the background-only hypothesis. The lines indicate the scaled expected distributions of the \hmn process with $\mN = 750\GeV$ (solid red line), 1.5\TeV (dashed red line), 5.0\TeV (dotted red line), and of the \WO process (dash-dotted green line). The \hmn processes are characterized by the azimuthal separation variable $\dphill$, while the \WO process features in low missing transverse momentum.}
\label{fig:signal_region}
\end{figure*}
The data are found to be consistent with the background expectation. Using the relationship between the cross section and the mixing elements for the \hmn analysis, upper limits at the 95\% \CL are derived on $\abs{ \Vmn }^{2}$ as shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:upper_limits}. These results surpass those obtained in previous searches by the ATLAS and CMS Collaborations~\cite{Sirunyan:2018mtv,Sirunyan:2018xiv,Aad:2019kiz} for $\mN \gtrsim 650\GeV$, and set the first direct limits for $\mN > 2 \TeV$. Previous upper limits on the mixing elements from the CMS Collaboration~\cite{Sirunyan:2018mtv,Sirunyan:2018xiv} are plotted in Fig.~\ref{fig:upper_limits} for comparison. These limits on $\abs{ \Vmn }^{2}$ approach unity at around 1\TeV. As the mixing element describes the oscillation probability between the SM neutrinos and the heavy Majorana neutrino, results with $\abs{ \Vmn }^{2} > 1$ are not physically meaningful.
Equation~(\ref{eqn:Majorana_N_mass}) is used to convert the limit on $\abs{\mathrm{C}_5^{\ell\ell'}/\Lambda }^{2}$ extracted from the Weinberg operator analysis into a limit on $\abs{m_{\PGm\PGm}}$. The observed (expected) 95\% \CL upper limit on $\abs{m_{\PGm\PGm}}$ is found to be $10.8 ~ (12.8)\GeV$. This is the first upper limit from a collider experiment, and it improves upon a previous limit set in Ref.~\cite{Fuks:2020zbm} using the results from the NA62 experiment~\cite{NA62:2019eax}.
\ifthenelse{\boolean{cms@external}}{\clearpage}{}
\begin{figure}[htbp!]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.50\textwidth]{Figure_003.pdf}
\caption{Upper limits on the heavy neutrino mixing element $\abs{ \Vmn }^{2}$ at the 95\% C.L. as a function of the heavy neutrino mass $\mN$. The black dashed curve shows the expected upper limit, with the 1 and 2 standard deviation bands are indicated in lime green and light yellow, respectively. The solid black curve is the observed upper limit. The red dashed curve indicates observed upper limits from Ref.~\cite{Sirunyan:2018mtv}, while the blue dashed curve shows the observed upper limits from Ref.~\cite{Sirunyan:2018xiv}. The result from Ref.~\cite{Aad:2019kiz} is not shown since it focuses on low $\mN$. Starting from $\mN$ around 650\GeV, the analysis presented in this Letter improves upon the upper limits from those references.}
\label{fig:upper_limits}
\end{figure}
In summary, this Letter presents the first search for Majorana neutrinos at several \TeVns{} and a first probe of the Weinberg operator at the LHC. These achievements were made possible by considering for the first time vector boson fusion processes resulting in a same-sign dimuon final state. The results are consistent with the predictions from the standard model.
For heavy Majorana neutrinos, upper limits on the mixing element $\abs{ \Vmn }^{2}$ are set for the mass range $50\GeV < \mN < 25\TeV$ and the best sensitivity is reached for $\mN \gtrsim 650\GeV$. The phase space explored exceeds the center-of-mass energy of the LHC, improving previous limits for direct production of Majorana neutrinos. The highest mass for which $\abs{\Vmn}^{2}=1$ is excluded is around 23\TeV. The observed (expected) 95\% confidence level upper limit on the effective $\PGm\PGm$ Majorana mass associated with the Weinberg operator is 10.8 (12.8)\GeV, exceeding the current best limit from high intensity Kaon experiments.
````

````yaml
    mass relation, and scaling of relevant couplings if needed.
  detected_text_priorities:

    to 138 fb^{-1}.
  - Identify the final state as same-sign dimuons in vector boson fusion processes.
  - Explain that the search targets lepton-number violation through heavy Majorana
    neutrinos and the Weinberg operator.
  - 'Report only grounded results: agreement with Standard Model predictions, constraints
    on the muon-heavy-neutrino mixing element over 50 GeV to 25 TeV, and the 95% CL
    observed upp...'
  - Define specialized quantities such as V_{mu N}, m_N, C5/Lambda, and m_{mumu} when
    used.
  - Use concise language for backgrounds and simulation, avoiding excessive generator
    details unless they support the poster narrative.
  typography_rules:
  - 'Preserve HEP notation: √s, pT, pTmiss, mN, VμN, Δφμμ, mjj, HT/pT(μ1), CLs.'
  - Use compact fact badges for √s = 13 TeV, 138 fb⁻¹, CMS, same-sign μμ, and VBF.
  - Keep bullets short enough for a professional audience to scan from a distance.
  color_material_rules:

    and uncertainty bands retain plot-native styling.
  - Signal hypotheses are visually separated from SM backgrounds by stable accent
    colors and line styles.
  - Decorative geometry remains abstract and must not resemble unverified data.

- id: 3
  title: Regions, backgrounds, and fit observables
  layout: middle full-width strategy band with wide post-fit distribution figure and
    side notes
  text:
  - title: Analysis strategy
    body:
    - Two signal interpretations use the same HT/pT(μ1) discriminant, with different
      SR binning chosen for the heavy-neutrino and Weinberg-operator topologies.
    bullets:
    - 'Heavy Majorana neutrino SR: Δφμμ > 2 and Δφμμ < 2 bins.'
    - 'Weinberg-operator SR: pTmiss < 50 GeV and pTmiss > 50 GeV bins.'
    - 'Control regions: WZ, b-tagged, and WZb samples constrain reducible backgrounds.'
    - 'Dominant SR backgrounds: SM electroweak W±W± production and nonprompt leptons.'
  - title: Statistical model
    body: []
    bullets:
    - Profile-likelihood ratio with constrained nuisance parameters.
    - Modified frequentist CLs with asymptotic approximation.
    - WW, WZ, and tZq normalization factors float with signal strength.
    - 'Largest impact: statistical uncertainty in signal/background templates; total
      uncertainties are statistically dominated.'
  flowchart:
  - 'SR bins: HMN Δφμμ<2/>2; Weinberg pTmiss<50/>50 GeV'
  - 'CRs: 3μ WZ; b-tagged SR; WZb with ≥1 b-tagged jet'
  - 'Fit observable: HT/pT(μ1) in SRs and CRs'
  - Profile likelihood CLs; WW/WZ/tZq norms float; nuisance constraints
  caption: Post-fit HT/pT(μ1) distributions compare data, SM backgrounds, and scaled
    signal hypotheses across signal and control regions.
- id: 4
  title: Headline constraints at 95% confidence level
  layout: central hero result card with largest square limit plot and prominent result
    callouts
  text:
  - title: Heavy Majorana neutrino limits
    body:
    - The data agree with Standard Model predictions, leading to upper limits on |VμN|²
      over mN = 50 GeV–25 TeV.
    bullets:
    - For mN ≳ 650 GeV, the constraints are the most stringent from LHC searches reported
      in the paper.
    - The analysis sets first direct limits for mN > 2 TeV in this VBF approach.
    - Limits with |VμN|² > 1 are not physically meaningful and are interpreted accordingly.
  - title: Weinberg-operator result
    body: []
    bullets:
    - 'Observed 95% CL upper limit: |mμμ| < 10.8 GeV.'
    - 'Expected 95% CL upper limit: |mμμ| < 12.8 GeV.'
    - This is the first collider test of the μμ Weinberg-operator scenario reported
      by the analysis.
  caption: Observed and expected 95% CL upper limits on |VμN|² as a function of heavy-neutrino
    mass mN, compared with earlier CMS limits shown in the paper.
- id: 5
  title: Interpretation and scope
  layout: lower full-width summary strip with compact cards and no additional figures
  text:
  - title: What is constrained
    body:
    - This VBF same-sign dimuon search probes LNV in the muon channel without observing
      a deviation from the Standard Model.
    bullets:
    - 'Heavy-neutrino interpretation: one heavy state coupled through the muon mixing
      element VμN.'
    - 'Signal mass scan: mN from 50 GeV to 25 TeV.'
    - 'Weinberg interpretation: limit expressed through |C5μμ/Λ|² and converted to
      |mμμ|.'
    - Results are specific to the collider μμ channel and should not be conflated
      with ee neutrinoless double beta decay limits.
````

````yaml
meta:
  title: Probing Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator through VBF at √s =
    13 TeV
  authors: CMS Collaboration
  audience: High-energy physics conference audience
  one_sentence_takeaway: A CMS search in 138 fb⁻¹ of pp collisions at √s = 13 TeV
    finds no deviation from Standard Model predictions and sets 95% CL constraints
    on same-sign dimuon VBF lepton-number violation through heavy Majorana neutrinos
    and the Weinberg operator.
core_message: Same-sign μμ production in a VBF topology provides a collider test of
  lepton-number violation in the muon channel; CMS data agree with SM backgrounds,
  yielding limits on |V_{μN}|² for m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV and an observed 95% CL limit
  |m_{μμ}| < 10.8 GeV for the Weinberg-operator interpretation.
sections:
- id: 1
  title: 'Physics target: LNV in VBF same-sign dimuons'
  role: motivation
  synopsis: Same-sign W bosons in VBF can probe lepton-number violation through either
    a heavy t-channel Majorana neutrino N or the dimension-five Weinberg operator.
    The final state is two same-sign muons plus two VBF jets, targeting a μμ collider
    channel not accessible to low-energy ee-focused LNV searches.
  key_claims:
  - The search targets LNV in VBF pp processes producing same-sign μμ pairs.
  - 'Heavy Majorana neutrino interpretation: a single heavy state N coupled through
    V_{μN}, scanned over m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV.'
  - 'Weinberg operator: C5^{μμ}/Λ generates an effective μμ Majorana mass m_{μμ} =
    C5^{μμ}v²/Λ.'
  - VBF t-channel production complements other LHC heavy-neutrino searches at TeV-scale
    masses.
  text_budget: title + one-sentence motivation + 4 short bullets + 2 equation chips
  preferred_visual: Two adjacent Feynman diagrams with compact equation chips for
    L_5 and m_{μμ}; use CMS-style particle labels and high-contrast signal coloring.
  visual_keywords:
  - Feynman diagram
  - VBF
  - same-sign W bosons
  - heavy Majorana neutrino
  - Weinberg operator
  - LNV
  - m_{μμ}
  - V_{μN}
- id: 2
  title: Dataset, objects, and VBF event selection
  role: dataset
  synopsis: The analysis uses CMS pp collision data collected in 2016–2018 at √s =
    13 TeV, corresponding to 138 fb⁻¹. Events are selected with exactly two same-sign
    muons and at least two high-mass, well-separated VBF jets, with lepton, b-jet,
    and τ vetoes to suppress backgrounds.
  key_claims:
  - 'Dataset: CMS pp collisions at √s = 13 TeV with integrated luminosity 138 fb⁻¹.'
  - 'Triggers: isolated single-muon p_T > 24 or 27 GeV; dimuon triggers improve acceptance
    by up to 4%.'
  - 'Signal-region muons: exactly two same-sign μ with p_T > 30 GeV, |η| < 2.4, and
    m_{μμ} > 20 GeV.'
  - 'VBF jets: at least two jets with p_T > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7; m_{jj} > 750 GeV
    and |Δη_{jj}| > 2.5.'
  - 'VBF topology requirement: max(Z_ℓ) < 0.75; additional loose leptons, hadronic
    τ candidates, and b-tagged jets are vetoed.'
  text_budget: fact badges + 5 compact selection bullets
  preferred_visual: 'Compact HEP selection-flow schematic with concrete thresholds:
    138 fb⁻¹ √s=13 TeV → 2 SS μ → ≥2 VBF jets → topology/vetoes.'
  visual_keywords:
  - 138 fb⁻¹
  - √s = 13 TeV
  - same-sign dimuons
  - p_T > 30 GeV
  - m_{jj} > 750 GeV
  - '|Δη_{jj}| > 2.5'
  - Zeppenfeld variable
  - b veto
- id: 3
  title: Regions, backgrounds, and fit observables
  role: method
  synopsis: 'Two signal interpretations share the H_T/p_T(μ₁) discriminant but use
    interpretation-specific SR binning: Δφ_{μμ} for heavy Majorana neutrinos and p_T^{miss}
    for the Weinberg operator. A simultaneous fit includes SRs and CRs enriched in
    WZ and nonprompt-lepton backgrounds.'
  key_claims:
  - Heavy Majorana neutrino SRs are split into Δφ_{μμ} > 2 and Δφ_{μμ} < 2 bins.
  - Weinberg-operator SRs are split into p_T^{miss} < 50 GeV and p_T^{miss} > 50 GeV
    bins.
  - Control regions include a 3μ WZ CR, a b-tagged CR, and a WZb CR with at least
    one b-tagged jet.
  - Dominant SR backgrounds are SM electroweak W^{±}W^{±} production and nonprompt
    leptons.
  - 'Fit observable: H_T/p_T(μ₁), where H_T is the scalar sum of jet p_T for jets
    with p_T > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7.'
  text_budget: section title + 2 mini-blocks, each with 3–4 bullets
  preferred_visual: Wide post-fit H_T/p_T(μ₁) distribution panel across SR/CR bins,
    plus a small region/fit schematic with paper-specific labels.
  visual_keywords:
  - H_T/p_T(μ₁)
  - SR
  - CR
  - Δφ_{μμ}
  - p_T^{miss}
  - WZ CR
  - b-tagged CR
  - WZb CR
- id: 4
  title: Headline constraints at 95% confidence level
  role: result
  synopsis: The observed data are consistent with Standard Model predictions. The
    analysis sets 95% CL upper limits on |V_{μN}|² versus m_N and an observed 95%
    CL upper limit |m_{μμ}| < 10.8 GeV for the Weinberg-operator interpretation.
  key_claims:
  - No deviation from Standard Model expectations is observed.
  - Heavy-neutrino limits constrain |V_{μN}|² over m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV.
  - For m_N ≳ 650 GeV, the constraints are reported as the most stringent from LHC
    searches to date in the paper.
  - The analysis sets first direct limits for m_N > 2 TeV in this VBF heavy-neutrino
    approach.
  - Values with |V_{μN}|² > 1 are not physically meaningful and should be interpreted
    accordingly.
  text_budget: large result callout + 4 bullets + one small Weinberg result badge
  preferred_visual: 'Hero square limit plot: observed and expected 95% CL upper limits
    on |V_{μN}|² vs m_N, with uncertainty bands and previous CMS comparison curves;
    include log-scale axes if shown in source figure.'
  visual_keywords:
  - 95% CL
  - observed limit
  - expected limit
  - '|V_{μN}|²'
  - m_N
  - 50 GeV–25 TeV
  - 650 GeV
  - 2 TeV
- id: 5
  title: Interpretation and scope
  role: interpretation
  synopsis: This VBF same-sign dimuon search probes LNV in the muon channel and reports
    constraints under specific heavy-neutrino and Weinberg-operator assumptions. The
    results should be read as collider μμ constraints, not as evidence for LNV or
    as direct ee neutrinoless-double-beta-decay comparisons.
  key_claims:
  - The search finds agreement with SM predictions, not discovery or evidence of LNV.
  - Heavy-neutrino interpretation assumes one heavy state coupled through V_{μN}.
  - The heavy-neutrino mass scan is limited to m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV.
  - The Weinberg interpretation constrains |C5^{μμ}/Λ|² and converts it to |m_{μμ}|
    using m_{μμ}=C5^{μμ}v²/Λ.
  - The μμ collider result complements, but should not be conflated with, ee-focused
    low-energy LNV probes.
  text_budget: one-sentence takeaway + 4 compact scope bullets
  preferred_visual: Summary strip with definition cards for V_{μN}, m_N, C5^{μμ}/Λ,
    and m_{μμ}; no new quantitative plots.
  visual_keywords:
  - scope
  - muon channel
  - no deviation
  - one heavy state
  - C5^{μμ}/Λ
  - m_{μμ}
  - collider LNV
````

````yaml
  options:

  - Only photon triggers; no dimuon triggers
  - Single-electron triggers pT > 30 GeV; dimuon triggers add 20% acceptance
  - No trigger information is reported
  answer: Single-muon triggers requiring isolated muons with pT > 24 or 27 GeV are
    used; dimuon triggers improve event acceptance by up to 4%.
  poster_priority: should
  source_evidence: “Collision events are collected using single-muon triggers… pT
    > 24 or 27 GeV… the dimuon triggers increase the event acceptance by up to 4%.”
  target_section: 2
  recommended_copy: Single-μ triggers; dimuon triggers add ≤4%
  linked_assets: []
- id: Q05
  aspect: object_selection
  question: What are the signal-region muon requirements?
  options:
  - Exactly two same-sign μ with pT > 30 GeV, |η| < 2.4, and mμμ > 20 GeV
  - At least three μ with pT > 10 GeV and |η| < 3.0
  - Two opposite-sign μ with mμμ near mZ
  - Exactly two electrons with pT > 30 GeV
  answer: Exactly two same-sign muons with pT > 30 GeV and |η| < 2.4; the SR also
    requires mμμ > 20 GeV.
  poster_priority: must
  source_evidence: '“The final states analyzed contain two well-identified SS muons
    with pT > 30 GeV and pseudorapidity |η| < 2.4…” and Table: “Dilepton mass mℓℓ
    > 20 GeV.”'
  target_section: 2
  recommended_copy: '2 SS μ: pT > 30 GeV, |η| < 2.4'
  linked_assets: []
- id: Q06
  aspect: vbf_selection
  question: Which VBF jet and topology requirements define the signal region?
  options:
  - ≥2 jets pT > 30 GeV, |η| < 4.7; mjj > 750 GeV; |Δηjj| > 2.5; max(Zℓ) < 0.75
  - ≥1 jet pT > 100 GeV with no η requirement
  - Exactly two b-tagged jets with mjj near 125 GeV
  - No explicit VBF jet selection is used
  answer: At least two jets with pT > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7; VBF candidates must satisfy
    mjj > 750 GeV, |Δηjj| > 2.5, and max(Zℓ) < 0.75.
  poster_priority: must
  source_evidence: “at least two jets with pT > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7… |Δηjj| > 2.5
    and… mjj > 750 GeV… require max(Zℓ) < 0.75.”
  target_section: 2
  recommended_copy: 'VBF: mjj > 750 GeV, |Δηjj| > 2.5'
  linked_assets: []
- id: Q07
  aspect: region_definitions
  question: How are the signal regions split for the two interpretations?
  options:
  - 'Heavy N: Δφμμ > 2 and < 2; Weinberg: pTmiss < 50 GeV and > 50 GeV'
  - Both analyses use only mμμ bins
  - 'Heavy N: b-tag bins; Weinberg: electron-count bins'
  - No SR binning is reported
  answer: The heavy Majorana neutrino SR is split by Δφμμ > 2 and Δφμμ < 2; the Weinberg-operator
    SR is split by pTmiss < 50 GeV and pTmiss > 50 GeV.
  poster_priority: must
  source_evidence: “For the hmn analysis, we define a high-Δφll bin (Δφll > 2) and
    a low-Δφll bin (Δφll < 2)… For the Weinberg operator analysis, a low-pTmiss bin
    (< 50 GeV) and a high-pTmiss bin (> 50 GeV) are defined.”
  target_section: 3
  recommended_copy: 'SR splits: Δφμμ for N, pTmiss for Weinberg'
  linked_assets:
  - Figure_002.png
- id: Q08
  aspect: backgrounds_and_control_regions
  question: Which backgrounds dominate the SR, and which control regions help constrain
    reducible backgrounds?
  options:
  - Dominant SR backgrounds are electroweak W±W± and nonprompt leptons; CRs include
    WZ, b-tagged, and WZb samples
  - Dominant SR backgrounds are γγ and QCD multijet only
  - Only tt̄Z is considered, with no CRs
  - Backgrounds are ignored in the fit
  answer: Dominant SR backgrounds are SM electroweak W±W± production and nonprompt
    leptons; WZ, b-tagged, and WZb control regions constrain reducible backgrounds.
  poster_priority: must
  source_evidence: “The dominant backgrounds in the SR are SM electroweak WW production
    and the contribution from nonprompt leptons.” and “A WZ CR… b-tagged CR… WZb CR…”
  target_section: 3
  recommended_copy: 'Dominant: EW W±W± and nonprompt leptons'
  linked_assets:
  - Figure_002.png
- id: Q09
  aspect: fit_observable
  question: What discriminating variable is fitted in the SRs and CRs, and what does
    it measure?
  options:
  - HT/pT(μ1), hadronic activity relative to leading-muon pT
  - mjj only, the invariant mass of VBF jets
  - pTmiss only, missing transverse momentum
  - mμμ only, dimuon invariant mass
  answer: The fitted discriminant is HT/pT(μ1), measuring hadronic activity relative
    to the leading muon pT; HT is the scalar sum of jet pT for jets with pT > 30 GeV
    and |η| < 4.7.
  poster_priority: must
  source_evidence: “The discriminating variable used to search for a signal for both
    analyses is HT/pT^{μ1}. Here, HT is the scalar sum of jet pT for all jets with
    pT > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7…”
  target_section: 3
  recommended_copy: 'Fit observable: HT/pT(μ1)'
  linked_assets:
  - Figure_002.png
- id: Q10
  aspect: statistical_interpretation
  question: Which statistical method is used to set limits?
  options:
  - Profile likelihood with constrained nuisance parameters and modified frequentist
    CLs
  - Simple event counting with no uncertainties
  - Bayesian posterior sampling only
  - A neural-network classifier without a likelihood fit
  answer: Limits are set using a profile-likelihood ratio test statistic with constrained
    nuisance parameters and the modified frequentist CLs criterion with asymptotic
    approximation.
  poster_priority: must
  source_evidence: “The statistical analysis is performed with a profile likelihood
    ratio test statistic in which systematic uncertainties are modeled as constrained
    nuisance parameters. Limits are set using the modified frequentist CLs criterion…
    and the asymptotic approximation…”
  target_section: 3
  recommended_copy: Profile likelihood + CLs at 95% CL
  linked_assets:
  - Figure_002.png
  - Figure_003.png
- id: Q11
  aspect: heavy_neutrino_result
  question: What does the analysis conclude for the heavy Majorana neutrino mixing
    element |VμN|²?
  options:
  - Data agree with SM predictions; 95% CL upper limits constrain |VμN|² over mN =
    50 GeV–25 TeV
  - A heavy neutrino is discovered at 1 TeV
  - Limits are set only below 10 GeV
  - Only electron-channel mixing is constrained
  answer: The data agree with SM predictions, and 95% CL upper limits are derived
    on |VμN|² for mN = 50 GeV–25 TeV; for mN ≳ 650 GeV they surpass previous LHC constraints
    cited in the paper.
  poster_priority: must
  source_evidence: “The results are found to agree with the predictions of the standard
    model… constraints… in the heavy neutrino mass range 50 GeV–25 TeV; for masses
    above 650 GeV these are the most stringent constraints from searches at the LHC
    to date.”
  target_section: 4
  recommended_copy: '|VμN|² limits for mN = 50 GeV–25 TeV'
  linked_assets:
  - Figure_003.png
- id: Q12
  aspect: weinberg_operator_result_and_scope
  question: What 95% CL upper limit is reported for the Weinberg-operator effective
    μμ Majorana mass, and how should its scope be stated?
  options:
  - Observed |mμμ| < 10.8 GeV; expected |mμμ| < 12.8 GeV, in the collider μμ channel
  - Observed |mee| < 10.8 meV from neutrinoless double beta decay
  - Observed |mμμ| > 10.8 GeV as evidence for LNV
  - No numerical Weinberg-operator limit is reported
  answer: The observed 95% CL upper limit is |mμμ| < 10.8 GeV, with an expected limit
    of |mμμ| < 12.8 GeV; it is a collider μμ-channel Weinberg-operator interpretation,
    not evidence for LNV.
  poster_priority: must
  source_evidence: “The observed (expected) 95% CL upper limit on |mμμ| is found to
    be 10.8 (12.8) GeV. This is the first upper limit from a collider experiment…”
    and “The data are found to be consistent with the background expectation.”
  target_section: 4
  recommended_copy: Observed |mμμ| < 10.8 GeV at 95% CL
  linked_assets: []
coverage_notes:
- The 12 items cover motivation, final state, dataset, trigger, object/VBF selection,
  SR binning, backgrounds/CRs, fit observable, statistical method, heavy-neutrino
  limits, Weinberg-operator limit, and interpretation scope.
- Central poster facts are marked as must except the trigger detail, which is useful
  but secondary.
- All numerical values are grounded in the provided excerpt or poster specification;
  no event yields, p-values, efficiencies beyond stated trigger acceptance, or unprovided
  exclusions are introduced.
````

````yaml
  must_units:
  - s2_title
  - s2_badge_data
  - s2_badge_energy
  - s2_badge_lumi
  - s2_selection_mu
  - s2_selection_jets
  - s2_selection_vbf
  target_density: badge row + concrete selection-flow nodes
- section: 3
  role: strategy_fit
  must_units:
  - s3_title
  - fig02_head
  - s3_fitobs
  - s3_ht_def
  - s3_sr_split
  - s3_hmn_bins
  - s3_wo_bins
  - s3_crs
  target_density: wide figure headline + SR/CR matrix + fit/stat chips
- section: 4
  role: results
  must_units:
  - s4_title
  - fig01_head
  - s4_no_dev
  - s4_hmn_limit
  - s4_lhc_strong
  - s4_weinberg_obs
  - s4_weinberg_exp
  target_density: hero limit plot with large result callouts and short caveats
- section: 5
  role: interpretation_scope
  must_units:
  - s5_title
  - s5_conclusion
  - s5_scope_hmn
  - s5_scope_wo
  - s5_scope_channel
  target_density: compact conclusion strip with definition/scope cards
coverage_notes:
- Must-priority quiz coverage includes mechanisms, topology, dataset, object/VBF cuts,
  SR splits, dominant backgrounds/CRs, fit observable, CLs method, heavy-neutrino
  limits, Weinberg limit, and interpretation scope.
- Trigger acceptance is included as should-priority density because Q04 is secondary.
- All numerical claims are grounded in the provided analysis text or selected figure
  captions; no event yields, p-values, efficiencies beyond the stated trigger gain,
  or unreported exclusions are introduced.
````

````yaml
  \ This provides a compelling hint of physics beyond the SM. Efforts to determine\
  \ each neutrino mass are being pursued by many experiments within different research\
  \ fields, including cosmology and tritium beta decay~\\\\cite{Loureiro:2018pdz,eBOSS:2020yzd,KATRIN:2021uub},\

  nA natural formalism for generating neutrino masses is through a dimension-five\
  \ operator, proposed by Weinberg~\\\\cite{Weinberg79}, which extends the SM Lagrangian\

  \\overline{L}^c_{\\\\ell }\\\\big] \\\\big[L_{\\\\ell'}\\\\!\\\\!~\\\\cdot~\\\\\
  !\\\\Phi\\\\big],\\n\\\\label{eqn:Lag_5}\\n\\\\end{equation}\\n\\\\end{linenomath}\\\

  \ neutrino masses become relevant degrees of freedom; $\\\\mathrm{C}_5^{\\\\ell\\\
  \\ell'}$ is a flavor-dependent Wilson coefficient; $L_\\\\ell=(\\\\nu_\\\\ell,\\\
  \\ell)$ is the left-handed lepton doublet; and $\\\\Phi$ is the SM Higgs doublet\
  \ with a vacuum expectation value $v=\\\\sqrt{2}\\\\langle\\\\Phi\\\\rangle\\\\\

  \\ell\\\\ell'} = C_5^{\\\\ell\\\\ell'} v^2/\\\\Lambda,\\n\\\\label{eqn:Majorana_N_mass}\\\
  n\\\\end{equation}\\n\\\\end{linenomath}\\nand introduces lepton number violation\

  \ and the absence of neutrinos in the final state, and set stringent upper limits\

  \ and 79--180\\\\unit{meV}~\\\\cite{Agostini:2020xta}.\\nSince muons and tau leptons\
  \ are much heavier than electrons, SS final states involving these heavier leptons\
  \ are kinematically forbidden in low-energy nuclear experiments and can only be\
  \ studied at colliders~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm}. As the study of tau leptons is experimentally\
  \ more challenging, the final state with SS muons is investigated in this search.\

  \ ($\\\\abs{m_{\\\\PGm\\\\PGm}}$), translated from the searches for LNV decays of\
  \ charged kaons at the NA62 experiment~\\\\cite{NA62:2019eax}, is around 55\\\\\
  GeV at 90\\\\% \\\\CL~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm}.\\nThe Weinberg operator can be realized\

  \ assuming the existence of hypothetical heavy states, for example a heavy Majorana\

  \ of the SM neutrinos motivates the search for heavy Majorana neutrinos. Heavy Majorana\

  \ set limits on $\\\\Vln$ were based on the production of a \\\\hmn through either\
  \ quark-antiquark annihilation or $W\\\\PGg$, with different analysis strategies\
  \ based on various decay modes, such as many leptons in the final state~\\\\cite{Sirunyan:2018mtv,Aad:2019kiz,Sirunyan:2019bgz},\
  \ and in final states containing LNV lepton pairs~\\\\cite{Sirunyan:2018xiv,Aaboud:2018spl}.\
  \ For $ \\\\mN$ at a few \\\\GeVns{}, the constraints on $\\\\abs{\\\\Vln}^{2}$,\
  \ where $\\\\ell=\\\\left\\\\{e, \\\\Pgm \\\\right\\\\}$, are around $10^{-7}$--$10^{-5}$,\
  \ while at around 1\\\\TeV, the constraints approach unity.\\nThis Letter reports\
  \ the first search probing Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator in vector\
  \ boson fusion (VBF) processes~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm,Fuks:2020att} at the CERN LHC,\
  \ studying events with SS muon pairs.\\nAs shown in Fig.~\\\\ref{fig:diagram} by\
  \ the two representative Feynman diagrams, in the $t$ channel, SS $W$ boson pairs\
  \ may convert to SS lepton pairs via a \\\\TeVns{}-scale Majorana neutrino or through\
  \ a Weinberg operator process. Because the cross section of $t$-channel processes\
  \ is less sensitive to the mass of the intermediate particle compared with $s$-channel\
  \ quark-antiquark annihilation processes, the VBF process can complement searches\
  \ for heavy Majorana neutrinos at the \\\\TeVns{} mass scale as its cross section\
  \ decreases more slowly with increasing $N$ mass compared with the values from $s$-channel\
  \ production. Although the various seesaw mechanisms can be considered as realizations\
  \ of the Weinberg operator, an alternative implementation is considered in this\
  \ Letter, as shown in Fig.~\\\\ref{fig:diagram} (right). The two VBF processes considered\
  \ in this work differ primarily in that the Majorana process is assumed to be mediated\
  \ by a heavy $t$-channel neutrino whereas the Weinberg operator process is mediated\
  \ by a lighter $t$-channel neutrino.\\n\\\\begin{figure}[h!]\\\\centering\\n\\\\\
  includegraphics[width=0.40\\\\linewidth]{Figure_001-a.pdf}\\n\\\\hspace{13pt}\\\
  n\\\\includegraphics[width=0.40\\\\linewidth]{Figure_001-b.pdf}\\n\\\\caption{Example\
  \ Feynman diagrams of VBF processes with heavy Majorana neutrino production (left)\
  \ and processes mediated by the Weinberg operator (right) at the LHC.}\\\\label{fig:diagram}\\\
  n\\\\end{figure}\\nThis analysis is based on proton-proton ($pp$) collision data\
  \ collected at $\\\\sqrt{s} = 13\\\\TeV$ by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC during\
  \ 2016--2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $138\\\\fbinv$.\\nTabulated\
  \ results are provided in the HEPData record for this analysis~\\\\cite{hepdata}.\\\
  nThe CMS apparatus~\\\\cite{CMS:2008xjf} is a multipurpose, nearly hermetic detector,\
  \ designed to trigger on~\\\\cite{CMS:2020cmk,CMS:2016ngn}\\nand identify electrons,\
  \ muons, photons, and hadrons~\\\\cite{CMS:2020uim,CMS:2018rym,CMS:2014pgm}. A global\
  \ ``particle-flow'' algorithm~\\\\cite{CMS:2017yfk} aims to reconstruct all individual\
  \ particles in an event, combining information provided by the all-silicon inner\
  \ tracker and by the crystal electromagnetic and brass-scintillator hadron calorimeters,\
  \ operating inside a 3.8\\\\unit{T} superconducting solenoid, with data from gas-ionization\
  \ muon detectors embedded in the flux-return yoke outside the solenoid. The reconstructed\
  \ particles are used to build charged leptons, jets, and missing transverse momentum\
  \ ($\\\\pTvecmiss$)~\\\\cite{CMS:2018jrd,CMS:2016lmd,CMS:2019ctu}.\\nSamples of\
  \ signal events are simulated with next-to-leading order (NLO) precision using the\
  \ \\\\MGvATNLO 2.6.5 generator~\\\\cite{Alwall:2014hca}, based on model implementations\
  \ from Refs.~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm,Alva:2014gxa,Degrande:2016aje,Fuks:2020att}.\
  \ For the heavy Majorana neutrino, we assume only one heavy state and scan its mass\
  \ in a range from 50\\\\GeV to 25\\\\TeV. The process induced by the Weinberg operator\
  \ is simulated using a novel approach, established in Ref.~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm},\
  \ which approximates the internal neutrino lines and vertex insertion with an effective\
  \ light Majorana neutrino. The Wilson coefficient $\\\\mathrm{C}_5^{\\\\ell\\\\\
  ell'}$ is set to 1, and the energy scale $\\\\Lambda$ to 200\\\\TeV. The production\
  \ cross sections scale with $\\\\Vln ^{2} \\\\Vlnprime^{2}$ and $\\\\abs{\\\\mathrm{C}_5^{\\\
  \\ell\\\\ell'}/\\\\Lambda }^{2}$ for the VBF processes with heavy Majorana neutrinos~\\\
  \\cite{Fuks:2020att} and the Weinberg operator~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm}, respectively.\
  \ Since the kinematic shape of the signal is independent of $\\\\abs{ \\\\Vmn }$,\
  \ we set $\\\\abs{ \\\\Vmn } = 1$ for the signal simulation to ensure efficient\
  \ generation of signal events.\\nThe SM electroweak $\\\\WW$ and $W^{\\\\pm} Z$\
  \ processes, where both bosons decay leptonically, are simulated using \\\\MGvATNLO\
  \ 2.4.2~\\\\cite{Alwall:2014hca} at leading order (LO) with six electroweak $\\\\\
  left[ \\\\mathcal{O}(\\\\alpha^6) \\\\right]$ and zero quantum chromodynamics (QCD)\
  \ vertices. The QCD-induced $\\\\WW$ process is also simulated using \\\\MGvATNLO\
  \ 2.4.2 at LO. Contributions with an initial-state $b$ quark are excluded from the\
  \ electroweak $W^{\\\\pm} Z$ simulation because they are included in the production\
  \ of a $Z$ boson in association with a single top quark, known as the $tZq$ process,\
  \ which is simulated at NLO using \\\\MGvATNLO 2.3.3.\\nThe $ZZ \\\\to 4 \\\\ell$\
  \ and $gg \\\\to ZZ$ processes are simulated with the $\\\\POWHEG$ v2~\\\\cite{Nason:2013ydw}\
  \ and $\\\\MCFM$ 7.0.1~\\\\cite{Campbell:2011bn} generators, respectively. The production\
  \ of $\\\\TTBar W^{\\\\pm}$, $\\\\TTBar Z$, and triple vector boson ($VVV$) background\
  \ events is simulated at NLO in QCD using the \\\\MGvATNLO 2.2.2 (2.4.2) generator~\\\
  \\cite{Alwall:2014hca,MadGraph,Frederix:2012ps} for the samples corresponding to\
  \ the 2016 (2017--2018) data-taking period. The production of $\\\\WW$ events through\
  \ double-parton scattering is generated at LO using \\\\PYTHIA 8.226 (8.230)~\\\\\
  cite{Sjostrand:2014zea} for 2016 (2017--2018).\\nThe simulated samples for the 2016\
  \ (2017--2018) data-taking period use the NNPDF 3.0 (3.1) parton distribution functions~\\\
  \\cite{Ball:2014uwa,Ball:2017nwa}, and are interfaced with \\\\PYTHIA to model the\
  \ fragmentation and hadronization of partons in the initial and final states, along\
  \ with the underlying event. The CUETP8M1 (CP5) tune~\\\\cite{Khachatryan:2015pea,Sirunyan:2019dfx}\
  \ is used in the simulation for the 2016 (2017--2018) data-taking period. In LO\
  \ (NLO) simulations performed with \\\\MGvATNLO, jets are matched to the parton\
  \ shower produced by \\\\PYTHIA 8.2 following the MLM~\\\\cite{Alwall:2007fs} (FxFx~\\\
  \\cite{Frederix:2012ps}) prescription. The interactions of all final-state particles\
  \ with the CMS detector are simulated using \\\\GEANTfour~\\\\cite{Agostinelli:2002hh}.\
  \ Simulated events are mixed with the contribution of particles from additional\
  \ $pp$ interactions within the same or nearby bunch crossings (pileup); the pileup\
  \ distribution in the simulated samples matches that observed in data.\\nCollision\
  \ events are collected using single-muon triggers~\\\\cite{CMS:2016ngn} that require\
  \ the presence of an isolated muon with transverse momentum $\\\\pT > 24$ or 27\\\
  \\GeV, depending on the data-taking period. In addition, a set of dimuon triggers~\\\
  \\cite{CMS:2016ngn} with lower $\\\\pT$ thresholds is used to ensure a trigger efficiency\
  \ above 90\\\\% for events with muons. Depending on the subsequent off-line selection,\
  \ the dimuon triggers increase the event acceptance by up to 4\\\\%. The primary\
  \ vertex (PV) is taken to be the vertex corresponding to the hardest scattering\
  \ in the event, evaluated using tracking information alone, as described in Section\
  \ 9.4.1 of Ref.~\\\\cite{CMS-TDR-15-02}.\\nThe jets are clustered using the anti-\\\
  \\kt algorithm~\\\\cite{Cacciari:2011ma,Cacciari:2008gp} with a distance parameter\
  \ of 0.4, with the tracks assigned to the candidate vertices as inputs. To mitigate\
  \ the impact from pileup, tracks identified to be originating from pileup vertices\
  \ are discarded and calorimeter energies are corrected to account for charged and\

  \ defined as the negative vector $\\\\pT$ sum of all reconstructed particles in\
  \ an event. Its magnitude is referred to as $\\\\pTmiss$. Jets arising from $b$\
  \ quark hadronization and decay ($b$ jets) are identified using a deep neural network\
  \ algorithm, termed \\\\textsc{DeepCSV}, whose inputs are tracks displaced from\
  \ the primary interaction vertex, details of secondary vertices, and the kinematical\

  \ we use a requirement on the score of the \\\\textsc{DeepCSV} algorithm for which\
  \ the $b$ jet identification efficiency ranges from 65 to 75\\\\% and the rate at\
  \ which gluon or light-flavor jets are misidentified as $b$ jets is around 1\\\\\
  %. The fraction of jets originating from the hadronization of $c$ quarks that are\
  \ incorrectly identified as $b$ jets is about 10\\\\%.\\nStarting from the constituents\
  \ of reconstructed jets, hadronically decaying $\\\\tau$ leptons are identified\
  \ via the ``hadrons-plus-strips'' algorithm~\\\\cite{CMS:2018jrd}.\\nThe final states\
  \ analyzed contain two well-identified SS muons with $\\\\pT > 30\\\\GeV$ and pseudorapidity\
  \ $\\\\abs{\\\\eta} < 2.4$, and at least two jets with $\\\\pT > 30\\\\GeV$ and\
  \ $\\\\abs{\\\\eta} < 4.7$. The two selected jets with the largest $\\\\pT$ are\
  \ considered as the VBF jet candidates, which must satisfy a large pseudorapidity\
  \ separation $\\\\abs{\\\\Delta\\\\eta_{jj}} > 2.5$ and a large dijet invariant\
  \ mass $m_{jj} > 750 \\\\GeV$. Events produced via VBF are expected to contain rapidity\
  \ gaps between the muons and the VBF jets. To utilize this signature, we require\
  \ max$\\\\left ( \\\\mathcal{Z}_{\\\\ell} \\\\right ) < 0.75$, where $\\\\mathcal{Z}_{\\\
  \\ell}$ is the Zeppenfeld variable~\\\\cite{zepp1996} of a lepton $\\\\ell$: $\\\
  \\mathcal{Z}_{\\\\ell} = \\\\abs{ \\\\eta_{\\\\ell} -(\\\\eta_{j1}+\\\\eta_{j2})/2\
  \ }/ \\\\\\n... [truncated]\"\n}"

result:

        corresponding to... $138\fbinv$"'
    - label: Single-muon triggers pT>24 or 27 GeV; dimuon triggers add up to 4% acceptance

    - label: '>=2 jets: pT>30 GeV, |eta|<4.7; leading-pT pair defines VBF candidates'
````

````yaml
  text:

    - 'Majorana-neutrino hypothesis: heavy t-channel N with mass mN.'

    a heavy Majorana neutrino and by the Weinberg operator.

      to 138 fb⁻¹.
    bullets:
    - 'Triggers: single-muon pT > 24 or 27 GeV, with dimuon triggers improving acceptance

      SR binning chosen for the heavy-neutrino and Weinberg-operator topologies.

    - 'Heavy Majorana neutrino SR: Δφμμ > 2 and Δφμμ < 2 bins.'

  for mN ≳ 650 GeV as stated in the analysis.
````
