````yaml
storyboard:
  meta:
    title: Probing Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator through VBF at √s
      = 13 TeV
    authors: CMS Collaboration
    audience: High-energy physics conference audience
    one_sentence_takeaway: A CMS search in 138 fb⁻¹ of pp collisions at √s = 13 TeV
      finds no deviation from Standard Model predictions and sets 95% CL constraints
      on same-sign dimuon VBF lepton-number violation through heavy Majorana neutrinos
      and the Weinberg operator.
  core_message: Same-sign μμ production in a VBF topology provides a collider test
    of lepton-number violation in the muon channel; CMS data agree with SM backgrounds,
    yielding limits on |V_{μN}|² for m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV and an observed 95% CL limit
    |m_{μμ}| < 10.8 GeV for the Weinberg-operator interpretation.
  sections:
  - id: 1
    title: 'Physics target: LNV in VBF same-sign dimuons'
    role: motivation
    synopsis: Same-sign W bosons in VBF can probe lepton-number violation through
      either a heavy t-channel Majorana neutrino N or the dimension-five Weinberg
      operator. The final state is two same-sign muons plus two VBF jets, targeting
      a μμ collider channel not accessible to low-energy ee-focused LNV searches.
    key_claims:
    - The search targets LNV in VBF pp processes producing same-sign μμ pairs.
    - 'Heavy Majorana neutrino interpretation: a single heavy state N coupled through
      V_{μN}, scanned over m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV.'
    - 'Weinberg operator: C5^{μμ}/Λ generates an effective μμ Majorana mass m_{μμ}
      = C5^{μμ}v²/Λ.'
    - VBF t-channel production complements other LHC heavy-neutrino searches at TeV-scale
      masses.
    text_budget: title + one-sentence motivation + 4 short bullets + 2 equation chips
    preferred_visual: Two adjacent Feynman diagrams with compact equation chips for
      L_5 and m_{μμ}; use CMS-style particle labels and high-contrast signal coloring.
    visual_keywords:
    - Feynman diagram
    - VBF
    - same-sign W bosons
    - heavy Majorana neutrino
    - Weinberg operator
    - LNV
    - m_{μμ}
    - V_{μN}
  - id: 2
    title: Dataset, objects, and VBF event selection
    role: dataset
    synopsis: The analysis uses CMS pp collision data collected in 2016–2018 at √s
      = 13 TeV, corresponding to 138 fb⁻¹. Events are selected with exactly two same-sign
      muons and at least two high-mass, well-separated VBF jets, with lepton, b-jet,
      and τ vetoes to suppress backgrounds.
    key_claims:
    - 'Dataset: CMS pp collisions at √s = 13 TeV with integrated luminosity 138 fb⁻¹.'
    - 'Triggers: isolated single-muon p_T > 24 or 27 GeV; dimuon triggers improve
      acceptance by up to 4%.'
    - 'Signal-region muons: exactly two same-sign μ with p_T > 30 GeV, |η| < 2.4,
      and m_{μμ} > 20 GeV.'
    - 'VBF jets: at least two jets with p_T > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7; m_{jj} > 750 GeV
      and |Δη_{jj}| > 2.5.'
    - 'VBF topology requirement: max(Z_ℓ) < 0.75; additional loose leptons, hadronic
      τ candidates, and b-tagged jets are vetoed.'
    text_budget: fact badges + 5 compact selection bullets
    preferred_visual: 'Compact HEP selection-flow schematic with concrete thresholds:
      138 fb⁻¹ √s=13 TeV → 2 SS μ → ≥2 VBF jets → topology/vetoes.'
    visual_keywords:
    - 138 fb⁻¹
    - √s = 13 TeV
    - same-sign dimuons
    - p_T > 30 GeV
    - m_{jj} > 750 GeV
    - '|Δη_{jj}| > 2.5'
    - Zeppenfeld variable
    - b veto
  - id: 3
    title: Regions, backgrounds, and fit observables
    role: method
    synopsis: 'Two signal interpretations share the H_T/p_T(μ₁) discriminant but use
      interpretation-specific SR binning: Δφ_{μμ} for heavy Majorana neutrinos and
      p_T^{miss} for the Weinberg operator. A simultaneous fit includes SRs and CRs
      enriched in WZ and nonprompt-lepton backgrounds.'
    key_claims:
    - Heavy Majorana neutrino SRs are split into Δφ_{μμ} > 2 and Δφ_{μμ} < 2 bins.
    - Weinberg-operator SRs are split into p_T^{miss} < 50 GeV and p_T^{miss} > 50
      GeV bins.
    - Control regions include a 3μ WZ CR, a b-tagged CR, and a WZb CR with at least
      one b-tagged jet.
    - Dominant SR backgrounds are SM electroweak W^{±}W^{±} production and nonprompt
      leptons.
    - 'Fit observable: H_T/p_T(μ₁), where H_T is the scalar sum of jet p_T for jets
      with p_T > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7.'
    text_budget: section title + 2 mini-blocks, each with 3–4 bullets
    preferred_visual: Wide post-fit H_T/p_T(μ₁) distribution panel across SR/CR bins,
      plus a small region/fit schematic with paper-specific labels.
    visual_keywords:
    - H_T/p_T(μ₁)
    - SR
    - CR
    - Δφ_{μμ}
    - p_T^{miss}
    - WZ CR
    - b-tagged CR
    - WZb CR
  - id: 4
    title: Headline constraints at 95% confidence level
    role: result
    synopsis: The observed data are consistent with Standard Model predictions. The
      analysis sets 95% CL upper limits on |V_{μN}|² versus m_N and an observed 95%
      CL upper limit |m_{μμ}| < 10.8 GeV for the Weinberg-operator interpretation.
    key_claims:
    - No deviation from Standard Model expectations is observed.
    - Heavy-neutrino limits constrain |V_{μN}|² over m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV.
    - For m_N ≳ 650 GeV, the constraints are reported as the most stringent from LHC
      searches to date in the paper.
    - The analysis sets first direct limits for m_N > 2 TeV in this VBF heavy-neutrino
      approach.
    - Values with |V_{μN}|² > 1 are not physically meaningful and should be interpreted
      accordingly.
    text_budget: large result callout + 4 bullets + one small Weinberg result badge
    preferred_visual: 'Hero square limit plot: observed and expected 95% CL upper
      limits on |V_{μN}|² vs m_N, with uncertainty bands and previous CMS comparison
      curves; include log-scale axes if shown in source figure.'
    visual_keywords:
    - 95% CL
    - observed limit
    - expected limit
    - '|V_{μN}|²'
    - m_N
    - 50 GeV–25 TeV
    - 650 GeV
    - 2 TeV
  - id: 5
    title: Interpretation and scope
    role: interpretation
    synopsis: This VBF same-sign dimuon search probes LNV in the muon channel and
      reports constraints under specific heavy-neutrino and Weinberg-operator assumptions.
      The results should be read as collider μμ constraints, not as evidence for LNV
      or as direct ee neutrinoless-double-beta-decay comparisons.
    key_claims:
    - The search finds agreement with SM predictions, not discovery or evidence of
      LNV.
    - Heavy-neutrino interpretation assumes one heavy state coupled through V_{μN}.
    - The heavy-neutrino mass scan is limited to m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV.
    - The Weinberg interpretation constrains |C5^{μμ}/Λ|² and converts it to |m_{μμ}|
      using m_{μμ}=C5^{μμ}v²/Λ.
    - The μμ collider result complements, but should not be conflated with, ee-focused
      low-energy LNV probes.
    text_budget: one-sentence takeaway + 4 compact scope bullets
    preferred_visual: Summary strip with definition cards for V_{μN}, m_N, C5^{μμ}/Λ,
      and m_{μμ}; no new quantitative plots.
    visual_keywords:
    - scope
    - muon channel
    - no deviation
    - one heavy state
    - C5^{μμ}/Λ
    - m_{μμ}
    - collider LNV
  visual_assets:
  - asset: Figure_001-a.png
    caption: Example VBF Feynman diagram for same-sign dimuon production mediated
      by a heavy Majorana neutrino.
    figure_type: feynman_diagram
    relevance: Introduces the heavy-N signal topology and motivates the same-sign
      μμ + VBF jets final state.
    target_section: 1
    role: motivation_visual
  - asset: Figure_001-b.png
    caption: Example VBF Feynman diagram for same-sign dimuon production mediated
      by the Weinberg operator.
    figure_type: feynman_diagram
    relevance: Pairs with the heavy-neutrino diagram to show the second LNV interpretation
      and supports the equation-chip explanation.
    target_section: 1
    role: motivation_visual
  - asset: Figure_002.png
    caption: Post-fit H_T/p_T(μ₁) distributions in SRs and CRs with SM backgrounds
      and scaled signal hypotheses.
    figure_type: post_fit_distribution
    relevance: Shows the discriminant used in the simultaneous fits and the agreement
      of data with background expectations.
    target_section: 3
    role: method_and_validation_visual
  - asset: Figure_003.png
    caption: Observed and expected 95% CL upper limits on |V_{μN}|² as a function
      of heavy-neutrino mass m_N.
    figure_type: limit_curve
    relevance: Central quantitative result for the heavy Majorana neutrino interpretation,
      including expected bands and prior CMS comparisons.
    target_section: 4
    role: hero_result_visual
  layout_tree:
    reading_order:
    - 1
    - 2
    - 3
    - 4
    - 5
    hero_section: 4
    hero_visual_role: Observed and expected 95% CL |V_{μN}|² limit curve versus m_N,
      paired with a prominent Weinberg-operator |m_{μμ}| limit callout.
    layout_intent: Lead with the LNV physics question and Feynman diagrams, anchor
      the upper-right with dataset and concrete VBF selection, use the middle band
      for region/fit strategy and post-fit distributions, then center the poster on
      the limit results and close with scope and interpretation.
    section_grouping:
    - 'Motivation and signal hypotheses: Section 1'
    - 'CMS dataset and event topology: Section 2'
    - 'Analysis strategy, backgrounds, and statistical model: Section 3'
    - 'Headline constraints: Section 4'
    - 'Interpretation boundaries and takeaways: Section 5'
  information_plan:
    density_target: 'High-density HEP conference poster: preserve concrete thresholds,
      SR/CR definitions, fit observable, statistical method, and grounded numerical
      limits while keeping each block scannable.'
    data_badges:
    - √s = 13 TeV
    - 138 fb⁻¹
    - CMS 2016–2018
    - same-sign μμ + VBF jets
    - m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV
    - 95% CL
    - observed |m_{μμ}| < 10.8 GeV
    - expected |m_{μμ}| < 12.8 GeV
    display_facts:
    - 'Final state: exactly two same-sign μ plus at least two VBF jets.'
    - 'Muon selection: p_T > 30 GeV and |η| < 2.4.'
    - 'Jet selection: p_T > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7.'
    - 'VBF topology: m_{jj} > 750 GeV, |Δη_{jj}| > 2.5, max(Z_ℓ) < 0.75.'
    - 'HMN SR split: Δφ_{μμ} > 2 and Δφ_{μμ} < 2.'
    - 'Weinberg SR split: p_T^{miss} < 50 GeV and p_T^{miss} > 50 GeV.'
    - 'Fit observable: H_T/p_T(μ₁).'
    - 'Dominant SR backgrounds: SM electroweak W^{±}W^{±} and nonprompt leptons.'
    - 'Statistical method: profile likelihood with constrained nuisance parameters;
      modified frequentist CL_s with asymptotic approximation.'
    - Data agree with SM predictions.
    must_answer_questions:
    - What lepton-number-violating processes are tested in the same-sign dimuon VBF
      channel?
    - What CMS dataset, collision energy, and integrated luminosity are used?
    - What object and VBF topology requirements define the signal region?
    - How do the heavy-neutrino and Weinberg-operator SR binnings differ?
    - Which backgrounds dominate, and how are control regions used?
    - What discriminant and statistical method are used to set limits?
    - What are the headline 95% CL constraints on |V_{μN}|² and |m_{μμ}|?
    - What assumptions and scope limits should readers keep in mind when interpreting
      the results?
    visual_story_units:
    - 'Side-by-side Feynman diagrams: heavy N vs Weinberg operator VBF LNV.'
    - Selection thresholds as concrete badges and a compact region-flow schematic.
    - Post-fit H_T/p_T(μ₁) distribution showing data-background agreement and signal
      hypotheses.
    - Observed/expected |V_{μN}|² limit curve vs m_N with uncertainty bands.
    - Definition/scope strip clarifying V_{μN}, m_N, C5^{μμ}/Λ, m_{μμ}, and μμ collider
      context.
  qa_questions:
  - What is the LNV final state targeted by this CMS VBF search?
  - What are the values of √s and integrated luminosity used in the analysis?
  - Which thresholds define the same-sign dimuon and VBF jet selection?
  - Which variables split the signal regions for the heavy-neutrino and Weinberg-operator
    interpretations?
  - What is H_T/p_T(μ₁), and why is it used as the fit observable?
  - Which control regions constrain WZ and nonprompt-lepton backgrounds?
  - What does the analysis conclude about agreement with the Standard Model?
  - What are the stated 95% CL limits on |V_{μN}|² over m_N and on |m_{μμ}| for the
    Weinberg operator?
physics_quiz:
  quiz_items:
  - id: Q01
    aspect: physics_motivation
    question: What lepton-number-violating mechanisms are tested in the VBF same-sign
      dimuon channel?
    options:
    - Heavy Majorana neutrino exchange and the Weinberg operator
    - Higgs-pair production and supersymmetric sleptons
    - Dark photons and axionlike particles
    - Only Standard Model WZ production
    answer: Heavy Majorana neutrino exchange and the dimension-five Weinberg operator.
    poster_priority: must
    source_evidence: “The first search exploiting the vector boson fusion process
      to probe heavy Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator at the LHC is presented.”
    target_section: 1
    recommended_copy: VBF tests heavy N and the Weinberg operator
    linked_assets:
    - Figure_001-a.png
    - Figure_001-b.png
  - id: Q02
    aspect: signal_topology
    question: What final state defines the core collider signature of the search?
    options:
    - Two same-sign muons plus two VBF jets
    - Two opposite-sign electrons plus missing energy
    - Four photons in a VBF topology
    - A single muon plus b-tagged jets
    answer: Two same-sign muons plus at least two VBF jets in pp collisions.
    poster_priority: must
    source_evidence: '“The final states analyzed contain two well-identified SS muons…
      and at least two jets…” and poster text: “Final state: two same-sign muons plus
      two VBF jets.”'
    target_section: 1
    recommended_copy: Same-sign μμ + VBF jets
    linked_assets:
    - Figure_001-a.png
    - Figure_001-b.png
  - id: Q03
    aspect: dataset_channel
    question: What collision energy and integrated luminosity are used?
    options:
    - √s = 13 TeV, 138 fb⁻¹
    - √s = 8 TeV, 20 fb⁻¹
    - √s = 14 TeV, 300 fb⁻¹
    - √s = 13.6 TeV, 35 fb⁻¹
    answer: CMS pp collision data at √s = 13 TeV corresponding to 138 fb⁻¹, collected
      during 2016–2018.
    poster_priority: must
    source_evidence: “This analysis is based on proton-proton (pp) collision data
      collected at √s = 13 TeV… during 2016–2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity
      of 138 fb⁻¹.”
    target_section: 2
    recommended_copy: 'CMS 2016–2018: 138 fb⁻¹ at √s = 13 TeV'
    linked_assets: []
  - id: Q04
    aspect: trigger_and_acceptance
    question: Which triggers are used, and what acceptance gain do dimuon triggers
      provide?
    options:
    - Single-muon triggers pT > 24 or 27 GeV; dimuon triggers add up to 4% acceptance
    - Only photon triggers; no dimuon triggers
    - Single-electron triggers pT > 30 GeV; dimuon triggers add 20% acceptance
    - No trigger information is reported
    answer: Single-muon triggers requiring isolated muons with pT > 24 or 27 GeV are
      used; dimuon triggers improve event acceptance by up to 4%.
    poster_priority: should
    source_evidence: “Collision events are collected using single-muon triggers… pT
      > 24 or 27 GeV… the dimuon triggers increase the event acceptance by up to 4%.”
    target_section: 2
    recommended_copy: Single-μ triggers; dimuon triggers add ≤4%
    linked_assets: []
  - id: Q05
    aspect: object_selection
    question: What are the signal-region muon requirements?
    options:
    - Exactly two same-sign μ with pT > 30 GeV, |η| < 2.4, and mμμ > 20 GeV
    - At least three μ with pT > 10 GeV and |η| < 3.0
    - Two opposite-sign μ with mμμ near mZ
    - Exactly two electrons with pT > 30 GeV
    answer: Exactly two same-sign muons with pT > 30 GeV and |η| < 2.4; the SR also
      requires mμμ > 20 GeV.
    poster_priority: must
    source_evidence: '“The final states analyzed contain two well-identified SS muons
      with pT > 30 GeV and pseudorapidity |η| < 2.4…” and Table: “Dilepton mass mℓℓ
      > 20 GeV.”'
    target_section: 2
    recommended_copy: '2 SS μ: pT > 30 GeV, |η| < 2.4'
    linked_assets: []
  - id: Q06
    aspect: vbf_selection
    question: Which VBF jet and topology requirements define the signal region?
    options:
    - ≥2 jets pT > 30 GeV, |η| < 4.7; mjj > 750 GeV; |Δηjj| > 2.5; max(Zℓ) < 0.75
    - ≥1 jet pT > 100 GeV with no η requirement
    - Exactly two b-tagged jets with mjj near 125 GeV
    - No explicit VBF jet selection is used
    answer: At least two jets with pT > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7; VBF candidates must
      satisfy mjj > 750 GeV, |Δηjj| > 2.5, and max(Zℓ) < 0.75.
    poster_priority: must
    source_evidence: “at least two jets with pT > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7… |Δηjj| > 2.5
      and… mjj > 750 GeV… require max(Zℓ) < 0.75.”
    target_section: 2
    recommended_copy: 'VBF: mjj > 750 GeV, |Δηjj| > 2.5'
    linked_assets: []
  - id: Q07
    aspect: region_definitions
    question: How are the signal regions split for the two interpretations?
    options:
    - 'Heavy N: Δφμμ > 2 and < 2; Weinberg: pTmiss < 50 GeV and > 50 GeV'
    - Both analyses use only mμμ bins
    - 'Heavy N: b-tag bins; Weinberg: electron-count bins'
    - No SR binning is reported
    answer: The heavy Majorana neutrino SR is split by Δφμμ > 2 and Δφμμ < 2; the
      Weinberg-operator SR is split by pTmiss < 50 GeV and pTmiss > 50 GeV.
    poster_priority: must
    source_evidence: “For the hmn analysis, we define a high-Δφll bin (Δφll > 2) and
      a low-Δφll bin (Δφll < 2)… For the Weinberg operator analysis, a low-pTmiss
      bin (< 50 GeV) and a high-pTmiss bin (> 50 GeV) are defined.”
    target_section: 3
    recommended_copy: 'SR splits: Δφμμ for N, pTmiss for Weinberg'
    linked_assets:
    - Figure_002.png
  - id: Q08
    aspect: backgrounds_and_control_regions
    question: Which backgrounds dominate the SR, and which control regions help constrain
      reducible backgrounds?
    options:
    - Dominant SR backgrounds are electroweak W±W± and nonprompt leptons; CRs include
      WZ, b-tagged, and WZb samples
    - Dominant SR backgrounds are γγ and QCD multijet only
    - Only tt̄Z is considered, with no CRs
    - Backgrounds are ignored in the fit
    answer: Dominant SR backgrounds are SM electroweak W±W± production and nonprompt
      leptons; WZ, b-tagged, and WZb control regions constrain reducible backgrounds.
    poster_priority: must
    source_evidence: “The dominant backgrounds in the SR are SM electroweak WW production
      and the contribution from nonprompt leptons.” and “A WZ CR… b-tagged CR… WZb
      CR…”
    target_section: 3
    recommended_copy: 'Dominant: EW W±W± and nonprompt leptons'
    linked_assets:
    - Figure_002.png
  - id: Q09
    aspect: fit_observable
    question: What discriminating variable is fitted in the SRs and CRs, and what
      does it measure?
    options:
    - HT/pT(μ1), hadronic activity relative to leading-muon pT
    - mjj only, the invariant mass of VBF jets
    - pTmiss only, missing transverse momentum
    - mμμ only, dimuon invariant mass
    answer: The fitted discriminant is HT/pT(μ1), measuring hadronic activity relative
      to the leading muon pT; HT is the scalar sum of jet pT for jets with pT > 30
      GeV and |η| < 4.7.
    poster_priority: must
    source_evidence: “The discriminating variable used to search for a signal for
      both analyses is HT/pT^{μ1}. Here, HT is the scalar sum of jet pT for all jets
      with pT > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7…”
    target_section: 3
    recommended_copy: 'Fit observable: HT/pT(μ1)'
    linked_assets:
    - Figure_002.png
  - id: Q10
    aspect: statistical_interpretation
    question: Which statistical method is used to set limits?
    options:
    - Profile likelihood with constrained nuisance parameters and modified frequentist
      CLs
    - Simple event counting with no uncertainties
    - Bayesian posterior sampling only
    - A neural-network classifier without a likelihood fit
    answer: Limits are set using a profile-likelihood ratio test statistic with constrained
      nuisance parameters and the modified frequentist CLs criterion with asymptotic
      approximation.
    poster_priority: must
    source_evidence: “The statistical analysis is performed with a profile likelihood
      ratio test statistic in which systematic uncertainties are modeled as constrained
      nuisance parameters. Limits are set using the modified frequentist CLs criterion…
      and the asymptotic approximation…”
    target_section: 3
    recommended_copy: Profile likelihood + CLs at 95% CL
    linked_assets:
    - Figure_002.png
    - Figure_003.png
  - id: Q11
    aspect: heavy_neutrino_result
    question: What does the analysis conclude for the heavy Majorana neutrino mixing
      element |VμN|²?
    options:
    - Data agree with SM predictions; 95% CL upper limits constrain |VμN|² over mN
      = 50 GeV–25 TeV
    - A heavy neutrino is discovered at 1 TeV
    - Limits are set only below 10 GeV
    - Only electron-channel mixing is constrained
    answer: The data agree with SM predictions, and 95% CL upper limits are derived
      on |VμN|² for mN = 50 GeV–25 TeV; for mN ≳ 650 GeV they surpass previous LHC
      constraints cited in the paper.
    poster_priority: must
    source_evidence: “The results are found to agree with the predictions of the standard
      model… constraints… in the heavy neutrino mass range 50 GeV–25 TeV; for masses
      above 650 GeV these are the most stringent constraints from searches at the
      LHC to date.”
    target_section: 4
    recommended_copy: '|VμN|² limits for mN = 50 GeV–25 TeV'
    linked_assets:
    - Figure_003.png
  - id: Q12
    aspect: weinberg_operator_result_and_scope
    question: What 95% CL upper limit is reported for the Weinberg-operator effective
      μμ Majorana mass, and how should its scope be stated?
    options:
    - Observed |mμμ| < 10.8 GeV; expected |mμμ| < 12.8 GeV, in the collider μμ channel
    - Observed |mee| < 10.8 meV from neutrinoless double beta decay
    - Observed |mμμ| > 10.8 GeV as evidence for LNV
    - No numerical Weinberg-operator limit is reported
    answer: The observed 95% CL upper limit is |mμμ| < 10.8 GeV, with an expected
      limit of |mμμ| < 12.8 GeV; it is a collider μμ-channel Weinberg-operator interpretation,
      not evidence for LNV.
    poster_priority: must
    source_evidence: “The observed (expected) 95% CL upper limit on |mμμ| is found
      to be 10.8 (12.8) GeV. This is the first upper limit from a collider experiment…”
      and “The data are found to be consistent with the background expectation.”
    target_section: 4
    recommended_copy: Observed |mμμ| < 10.8 GeV at 95% CL
    linked_assets: []
  coverage_notes:
  - The 12 items cover motivation, final state, dataset, trigger, object/VBF selection,
    SR binning, backgrounds/CRs, fit observable, statistical method, heavy-neutrino
    limits, Weinberg-operator limit, and interpretation scope.
  - Central poster facts are marked as must except the trigger detail, which is useful
    but secondary.
  - All numerical values are grounded in the provided excerpt or poster specification;
    no event yields, p-values, efficiencies beyond stated trigger acceptance, or unprovided
    exclusions are introduced.
domain_profile:
  domain_label: high_energy_particle_physics_collider_neutrino_search
  domain_profile: hep
  confidence: 0.99
  arxiv_categories:
  - hep-ex
  rationale: The paper is a CMS Collaboration search in proton-proton collisions at
    the CERN LHC at sqrt(s)=13 TeV, probing heavy Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg
    operator via vector boson fusion in same-sign dimuon final states. The excerpt
    contains HEP-specific terminology and methods including integrated luminosity,
    Feynman diagrams, VBF, lepton-number violation, Wilson coefficients, detector
    reconstr...
  visual_grammar:
  - Use a collider-physics visual style with clean axes, compact legends, and explicit
    units such as GeV, TeV, fb^{-1}, and confidence level.
  - Prioritize Feynman diagrams, event-selection flow, signal-versus-background distributions,
    and limit curves over decorative visuals.
  - Use CMS/LHC-appropriate terminology and notation consistently, including pp collisions,
    sqrt(s), pT, missing transverse momentum, same-sign dimuons, VBF jets, and integrated
    lum...
  - Distinguish signal hypotheses from Standard Model backgrounds with stable, high-contrast
    colors and clear line styles.
  - When showing constraints, emphasize log-scale axes where appropriate for masses,
    cross sections, or mixing elements.
  figure_types:
  - Feynman diagrams for heavy Majorana neutrino and Weinberg-operator VBF proces...
  - Kinematic distributions for same-sign dimuon and VBF event variables, such as...
  - Observed and expected upper-limit curves with uncertainty bands for heavy-neu...
  - Signal and background composition plots for selected event regions.
  - Compact analysis schematic showing pp collisions, VBF topology, two same-sign...
  layout_priorities:
  - 'Lead with the physics question: lepton-number violation, Majorana neutrinos,
    and collider tests of the Weinberg operator.'
  - Place the Feynman diagrams near the motivation section to make the signal topology
    immediately understandable.
  - Use a central results panel for observed/expected limits and the key quantitative
    outcome stated in the abstract.
  - Separate detector/data, event selection, backgrounds, and statistical interpretation
    into concise blocks.
  - Reserve space for collision energy and luminosity, since sqrt(s)=13 TeV and 138
    fb^{-1} are essential context.
  - Use equation snippets sparingly, highlighting only the Weinberg operator, Majorana
    mass relation, and scaling of relevant couplings if needed.
  text_priorities:
  - State that the analysis uses CMS pp collision data at sqrt(s)=13 TeV corresponding
    to 138 fb^{-1}.
  - Identify the final state as same-sign dimuons in vector boson fusion processes.
  - Explain that the search targets lepton-number violation through heavy Majorana
    neutrinos and the Weinberg operator.
  - 'Report only grounded results: agreement with Standard Model predictions, constraints
    on the muon-heavy-neutrino mixing element over 50 GeV to 25 TeV, and the 95% CL
    observed upp...'
  - Define specialized quantities such as V_{mu N}, m_N, C5/Lambda, and m_{mumu} when
    used.
  - Use concise language for backgrounds and simulation, avoiding excessive generator
    details unless they support the poster narrative.
  cautionary_rules:
  - Do not imply discovery, evidence for new physics, or observed lepton-number violation;
    the results agree with Standard Model predictions.
  - Do not generalize the limits beyond the stated heavy-neutrino mass range or beyond
    the muon-channel assumptions provided.
  - Do not invent numerical exclusions, p-values, event yields, efficiencies, or background
    compositions not present in the supplied text.
  - Avoid presenting the Weinberg-operator limit as directly comparable to neutrinoless
    double beta decay limits without explaining the different lepton flavor and collider
    context.
  - Keep confidence-level terminology precise, especially for observed versus expected
    limits.
  - Use HEP notation accurately and avoid replacing physics symbols with ambiguous
    prose when equations or standard variables are clearer.
  suggested_style: a_polished_cms_style_collider_physics_poster_with_a_strong_left_to_right_narrative_motivation_and_signal_diagrams_dataset_and_event_topology_analysis_strategy_then_constraints_and_takeaways_use_a_restrained_color_palette_high_contrast_plots_compact_equations_and_prominently_displayed_units_and_confidence_levels
````

#### prompt — `prompts/poster_prompt.txt` (present, 61575 bytes, sha256=e05ac17c3598…)

````txt
Create a complete vertical academic conference poster as one finished design.

Topic: CMS search for lepton-number violation in same-sign dimuon vector boson fusion processes.
Audience: high-energy physics conference audience.
Overall style: premium domain-adaptive scientific conference poster, modern editorial design, artistic but readable, not a collage.

TITLE SPELLING LOCK:
- Render the top main title exactly as: "Probing Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator through VBF at √s = 13 TeV".
- Do not paraphrase, abbreviate, or visually autocorrect any title word. The word 'for' must be spelled f-o-r, never 'fon'.
- Keep Greek letters unambiguous in the title; if γ would look like Latin y, use clearer glyph spacing rather than a corrupted y.

PLACEHOLDER GEOMETRY PRIORITY (highest priority; outranks art, symmetry, text density, and decoration):
- The visible dashed rectangle for every [FIG NN] placeholder must match its listed width/height aspect ratio. This is the most important instruction in the whole prompt.
- Generation order: first reserve and draw the blank [FIG NN] placeholder rectangles as hard geometric anchors on light mats; only then arrange text, flowcharts, badges, and decoration around those anchors.
- Do not stretch a placeholder to fill a card. If a card is too wide, shorten the dashed rectangle or make the card taller; compute height = width / listed ratio before rendering.
- If a placeholder shape conflicts with prose, flowcharts, badges, cards, or background art, reconstruct the surrounding text/design: reflow copy into compact legible tiers, merge labels, move badges/ornaments, and preserve the information target; never distort the placeholder.
- The light figure mat/card immediately behind a placeholder must support the same shape; do not hide a wrong large card by drawing a smaller correct-looking dashed inset.
- A generated template with an incorrect placeholder shape will be rejected before real-figure insertion.
- [FIG 01]: width/height ≈ 1.00; aspect "1:1 square"; label "95% CL limits on |VμN|² versus mN"; true square; width and height should look equal.
- [FIG 02]: width/height ≈ 2.50; aspect "2.5:1 wide"; label "Post-fit H_T/p_T(μ1) distributions in SRs and CRs"; substantial wide panel with width:height about 2.5:1; not 3.5:1, 4:1, or a thin ribbon.
- [FIG 03]: width/height ≈ 1.20; aspect "1.2:1"; label "VBF heavy Majorana neutrino diagram"; near-square panel with width:height about 1.20:1; only slightly wider than tall, not a 1.5:1 landscape card or banner.
- [FIG 04]: width/height ≈ 1.20; aspect "1.2:1"; label "VBF Weinberg-operator diagram"; near-square panel with width:height about 1.20:1; only slightly wider than tall, not a 1.5:1 landscape card or banner.
- Ruler check before rendering: 2.5:1 is 2.5× wider than tall, so height is 40% of its width; 1.22:1 is only slightly wider than tall; 1:1.47 is portrait with width about 68% of height; 1:1.99 is portrait with width about 50% of height.
- Wide placeholders need enough height to remain readable; portrait placeholders need enough vertical space; near-square placeholders must not become banners.

POSITIVE ART DIRECTION:
- Art direction: Editorial scientific-magazine design with layered abstract geometry and luminous gradients. Use atmospheric depth, subtle glow, frosted-glass surfaces, and carefully balanced negative space. Create a cover-story feeling: authoritative, beautiful, contemporary, and clearly scientific. Let abstract scientific forms sweep across the canvas to connect sections without becoming fake data. Use refined typography, micro-shadows, metallic accents, and soft depth cues to avoid a PPT-like template. Decorative artwork remains abstract; real plots, diagrams, tables, and images appear only in placeholders.
- Layout rhythm: Editorial scientific-poster rhythm with a strong header and a clear diagonal or Z-shaped scan path. Anchor one hero result in the visual center of gravity, with supporting method and context modules around it. Use section ribbons, numbered tabs, circular callouts, pill headers, wide bands, tall sidebars, and staggered panels. Break the grid intentionally while keeping alignment disciplined and readable. Vary card proportions and scale so the poster has hierarchy rather than a uniform matrix of boxes. Generous gutters and overlapping translucent connector elements should create flow without clutter.
- Background texture: Soft abstract scientific network and field texture behind content cards, kept low contrast and atmospheric. Use faint radial gradients, subtle particle trails, ghosted geometric forms, and margin-only network hints. Texture should add depth and motion while never reading as a plot, table, equation, or data visualization. Keep card interiors calm enough for text and placeholders to stay legible. Let color temperature shift gently across the poster to support the reading path.
- Typography: Modern editorial sans-serif system: Helvetica/Inter/Source-Sans-like, with a bold condensed title, crisp section headers, compact readable bullets, and restrained scientific notation. Use two weights and one accent style rather than many decorative fonts. Create hierarchy through scale, weight, color, spacing, and numbered tabs.
- Color/material palette: Premium HEP palette: deep indigo and graphite margins, CMS-like blue accent, muted teal/green for Weinberg-operator elements, warm amber for uncertainty-band highlights, and warm-white content cards. Text cards and figure cards remain light and calm; dark surfaces are reserved for the header, margins, frames, or accent rails.
- Figure-card surface: Every scientific figure placeholder sits on a warm-white, pearl, or very pale blue paper-like card with subtle shadow and fine outline. Plots and Feynman diagrams are never placed on dark navy, black, purple, or saturated blocks.
- Start from a beautiful editorial composition, not from a slide deck or wireframe.
- Use abstract, non-data artwork outside placeholders: gradients, light trails, field-appropriate geometry, atmospheric glow, soft depth, and subtle material texture.
- Decorative icons/badges outside placeholders must be generic only (stars, checks, arrows, abstract circles). Do not put physics symbols, particle labels, equations, ΔL=2, μ/ν/q/W/N, axes, vertices, or event-display schematics in decorative badges.
- Flowcharts, summary pills, and callout badges must not turn scientific shorthand into icons. Use plain words in normal text (for example 'dimuon' or 'muon-sector limit'), never standalone μμ/ν/W/N/ΔL/equation badges or pictograms.
- Give the poster varied visual mass: one dominant hero region, secondary supporting modules, small badges, shaped callouts, and breathing room.
- Section blocks may be rounded rectangles, capsules, circular badges, vertical sidebars, L-shaped wraps, staggered panels, or translucent overlays when this improves hierarchy.
- Keep every scientific figure placeholder itself a clean rectangle on a light paper-like figure card, but make the surrounding poster expressive and premium.
- Use official-looking identity as plain text badges only; do not hallucinate complex collaboration or institute logos unless explicitly supplied as assets.

NARRATIVE STORYBOARD (internal design brief; do not render this heading or the word storyboard):
- Core message to make visually obvious: Same-sign dimuon production in a VBF topology provides a collider test of lepton-number violation in the muon channel; CMS data agree with SM backgrounds, yielding limits on muon-heavy-neutrino mixing squared for m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV and an observed 95% CL limit |m_{dimuon}| < 10.8 GeV for the Weinberg-operator interpretation.
- Reading order should follow section ids: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
- Hero section id: 4; hero visual role: Observed and expected 95% CL |V_{μN}|² limit curve versus m_N, paired with a prominent Weinberg-operator |m_{μμ}| limit callout..
- Layout intent: Lead with the LNV physics question and Feynman diagrams, anchor the upper-right with dataset and concrete VBF selection, use the middle band for region/fit strategy and post-fit distributions, then center the poster on the limit results and close with scope and interpretation.
- Section 1: role=motivation; text budget=title + one-sentence motivation + 4 short bullets + 2 equation chips; preferred visual=Two adjacent Feynman diagrams with compact equation chips for L_5 and m_{dimuon}; use CMS-style particle labels and high-contrast signal coloring.; key claims=The search targets LNV in VBF pp processes producing same-sign dimuon pairs.; Heavy Majorana neutrino interpretation: a single heavy state N coupled through V_{μN}, scanned over m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV.; Weinberg operator: C5^{dimuon}/Λ generates an effective dimuon Majorana mass m_{dimuon} = C5^{dimuon}v²/Λ.
- Section 2: role=dataset; text budget=fact badges + 5 compact selection bullets; preferred visual=Compact HEP selection-flow schematic with concrete thresholds: 138 fb⁻¹ √s=13 TeV → 2 SS μ → ≥2 VBF jets → topology/vetoes.; key claims=Dataset: CMS pp collisions at √s = 13 TeV with integrated luminosity 138 fb⁻¹.; Triggers: isolated single-muon p_T > 24 or 27 GeV; dimuon triggers improve acceptance by up to 4%.; Signal-region muons: exactly two same-sign μ with p_T > 30 GeV, |η| < 2.4, and m_{dimuon} > 20 GeV.
- Section 3: role=method; text budget=section title + 2 mini-blocks, each with 3–4 bullets; preferred visual=Wide post-fit H_T/p_T(μ₁) distribution panel across SR/CR bins, plus a small region/fit schematic with paper-specific labels.; key claims=Heavy Majorana neutrino SRs are split into Δφ_{dimuon} > 2 and Δφ_{dimuon} < 2 bins.; Weinberg-operator SRs are split into p_T^{miss} < 50 GeV and p_T^{miss} > 50 GeV bins.; Control regions include a 3μ WZ CR, a b-tagged CR, and a WZb CR with at least one b-tagged jet.
- Section 4: role=result; text budget=large result callout + 4 bullets + one small Weinberg result badge; preferred visual=Hero square limit plot: observed and expected 95% CL upper limits on muon-heavy-neutrino mixing squared vs m_N, with uncertainty bands and previous CMS comparison curves; include log-scale axes if shown in source figure.; key claims=No deviation from Standard Model expectations is observed.; Heavy-neutrino limits constrain muon-heavy-neutrino mixing squared over m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV.; For m_N ≳ 650 GeV, the constraints are reported as the most stringent from LHC searches to date in the paper.
- Section 5: role=interpretation; text budget=one-sentence takeaway + 4 compact scope bullets; preferred visual=Summary strip with definition cards for V_{μN}, m_N, C5^{dimuon}/Λ, and m_{dimuon}; no new quantitative plots.; key claims=The search finds agreement with SM predictions, not discovery or evidence of LNV.; Heavy-neutrino interpretation assumes one heavy state coupled through V_{μN}.; The heavy-neutrino mass scan is limited to m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV.
- Use this storyboard only to guide hierarchy, reading path, and text compression; render only the public section text specified below.
- Storyboard science terms are semantic guidance only: never render them as standalone icons, circular badges, particle-symbol marks, fake diagrams, or flowchart pictograms outside [FIG NN] placeholders.

Prefer short claims and fact chips over paragraphs; reconstruct lower-priority facts into compact legible chips before changing placeholder geometry..

PHYSICS QUIZ COVERAGE TARGET (internal; do not render this heading, Q IDs, questions, or answers verbatim unless also present in COPY DECK):
- These questions define what a viewer should be able to understand after reading the poster.
- Use them to prioritize public copy and figure hierarchy. Do not draw quiz cards, exam questions, answer keys, or Q-number labels.
- priority=must, aspect=physics_motivation: viewer question "What lepton-number-violating mechanisms are tested in the VBF same-sign dimuon channel?"; expected answer target "Heavy Majorana neutrino exchange and the dimension-five Weinberg operator.".
- priority=must, aspect=signal_topology: viewer question "What final state defines the core collider signature of the search?"; expected answer target "Two same-sign muons plus at least two VBF jets in pp collisions.".
- priority=must, aspect=dataset_channel: viewer question "What collision energy and integrated luminosity are used?"; expected answer target "CMS pp collision data at √s = 13 TeV corresponding to 138 fb⁻¹, collected during 2016–2018.".
- priority=should, aspect=trigger_and_acceptance: viewer question "Which triggers are used, and what acceptance gain do dimuon triggers provide?"; expected answer target "Single-muon triggers requiring isolated muons with pT > 24 or 27 GeV are used; dimuon triggers improve event acceptance by up to 4%.".
- priority=must, aspect=object_selection: viewer question "What are the signal-region muon requirements?"; expected answer target "Exactly two same-sign muons with pT > 30 GeV and |η| < 2.4; the SR also requires mdimuon > 20 GeV.".
- priority=must, aspect=vbf_selection: viewer question "Which VBF jet and topology requirements define the signal region?"; expected answer target "At least two jets with pT > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7; VBF candidates must satisfy mjj > 750 GeV, |Δηjj| > 2.5, and max(Zℓ) < 0.75.".
- priority=must, aspect=region_definitions: viewer question "How are the signal regions split for the two interpretations?"; expected answer target "The heavy Majorana neutrino SR is split by Δφdimuon > 2 and Δφdimuon < 2; the Weinberg-operator SR is split by pTmiss < 50 GeV and pTmiss > 50 GeV.".
- priority=must, aspect=backgrounds_and_control_regions: viewer question "Which backgrounds dominate the SR, and which control regions help constrain reducible backgrounds?"; expected answer target "Dominant SR backgrounds are SM electroweak W±W± production and nonprompt leptons; WZ, b-tagged, and WZb control regions constrain reducible backgrounds.".
- priority=must, aspect=fit_observable: viewer question "What discriminating variable is fitted in the SRs and CRs, and what does it measure?"; expected answer target "The fitted discriminant is HT/pT(μ1), measuring hadronic activity relative to the leading muon pT; HT is the scalar sum of jet pT for jets with pT > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7.".
- priority=must, aspect=statistical_interpretation: viewer question "Which statistical method is used to set limits?"; expected answer target "Limits are set using a profile-likelihood ratio test statistic with constrained nuisance parameters and the modified frequentist CLs criterion with asymptotic approximation.".
- priority=must, aspect=heavy_neutrino_result: viewer question "What does the analysis conclude for the heavy Majorana neutrino mixing element muon-heavy-neutrino mixing squared?"; expected answer target "The data agree with SM predictions, and 95% CL upper limits are derived on muon-heavy-neutrino mixing squared for mN = 50 GeV–25 TeV; for mN ≳ 650 GeV they surpass previous LHC constraints cited in the paper.".
- priority=must, aspect=weinberg_operator_result_and_scope: viewer question "What 95% CL upper limit is reported for the Weinberg-operator effective dimuon Majorana mass, and how should its scope be stated?"; expected answer target "The observed 95% CL upper limit is |mdimuon| < 10.8 GeV, with an expected limit of |mdimuon| < 12.8 GeV; it is a collider dimuon-channel Weinberg-operator interpretation, not evidence for LNV.".

HEP POSTER DESIGN GRAMMAR:
- Use a CERN/LHCC-style scientific story spine: motivation → dataset/selection → strategy/background → key result → interpretation/summary.
- Use colored section ribbons or numbered tabs so the viewer can scan the poster from 2 meters away.
- Create one dominant hero region for the headline result; do not divide the body into many equal tiny boxes.
- Cards/blocks do not need to be square: use wide bands, tall sidebars, pill headers, circular callouts, curved connectors, and staggered panels when it improves hierarchy.
- Let 40-55% of the body be reserved for figure placeholders; HEP posters are figure-led, not paragraph-led.
- Use small badges for dataset, collision energy, luminosity, channel, or experiment only when present in the supplied text; never invent numbers.

TEXT DENSITY AND READABILITY:
- Compress prose into poster bullets: short noun phrases, ideally under 11 words each.
- Maintain Paper2Poster-style information richness through smaller but still legible text tiers, not by removing whitespace or shrinking figure placeholders.
- Use three text scales: large must-level claims, compact body bullets for specialist detail, and micro-badges for optional should/could facts.
- Preserve the current generous editorial whitespace; add information by making copy shorter and typesetting secondary facts smaller, not by packing cards edge-to-edge.
- Avoid microscopic paragraphs, footnote blocks, dense equations, and reference lists in the rendered poster.
- Prefer 2-5 bullets/fact chips per non-hero card and at most one short sentence per text block; preserve meaning without adding new science.
- Use public fact chips and numeric badges for explicitly grounded dataset/result facts; do not invent numbers.
- If text competes with a result figure, reconstruct the text layout: split it into shorter legible chips/sidebars and preserve the information target while enlarging/preserving the figure placeholder.

FIGURE-LED COMPOSITION:
- Allocate the largest placeholder to the main result/limit/cross-section/significance plot.
- Every placeholder rectangle must match its selected source image aspect ratio; enlarge or reshape the surrounding block instead of stretching the placeholder.
- Method, detector, topology, or control-region placeholders should support the story, not dominate it unless the paper is instrumentation-focused.
- Dense multi-panel HEP plots need large absolute area; preserve their native wide/tall ratio rather than forcing a square slot.
- For wide post-fit/distribution plots, reserve enough vertical height for axes and legends; reduce nearby flowchart/text space before making the plot hard to read.
- For professional HEP readers, dataset and strategy cards should show analysis-specific SR/CR, fit, and uncertainty details rather than a generic data-processing pipeline.
- All figure-containing cards must use a light paper/lab-white surface around the placeholder; dark or saturated fills may be outer accents only.

FIGURE CARD SURFACE POLICY (mandatory for visual integration):
- Mandatory: every [FIG NN] placeholder sits inside a light neutral figure card or mat (warm white, pearl, very pale blue, or very pale gray), never inside a dark navy/purple/black content block.
- The placeholder rectangle and its immediate surrounding card surface should read as one clean paper-like area, so a future white-background plot blends naturally instead of looking pasted onto a dark sticker.
- Dark cinematic backgrounds, detector rings, beamline glow, and saturated accent colors may frame figure cards from the outside, appear in margins, headers, side rails, numbered tabs, or corner ornaments, but must not fill the main figure card.
- For a hero result, create drama through scale, gold/blue outlines, shadows, halos, ribbons, and nearby abstract art; keep the actual result card interior light.
- For multi-figure sections, use a shared light cluster panel with thin pale separators and subtle shadows rather than separate dark tiles.
- Keep decorative texture out of figure mats; use only a quiet solid or near-solid light fill inside any chart/plot/diagram block.

TYPOGRAPHY SYSTEM:
- Preserve HEP notation: √s, pT, pTmiss, mN, VμN, Δφμμ, mjj, HT/pT(μ1), CLs.
- Use compact fact badges for √s = 13 TeV, 138 fb⁻¹, CMS, same-sign μμ, and VBF.
- Keep bullets short enough for a professional audience to scan from a distance.

COLOR AND MATERIAL SYSTEM:
- Observed limits use high-contrast black or CMS-blue emphasis; expected limits and uncertainty bands retain plot-native styling.
- Signal hypotheses are visually separated from SM backgrounds by stable accent colors and line styles.
- Decorative geometry remains abstract and must not resemble unverified data.

Canvas/layout:
- Portrait poster, approximately A0 vertical / 2:3 ratio.
- Top band: strong title banner with concise identity text, CMS/LHC badges, and abstract VBF-inspired particle-field artwork.
- Main body: Five large numbered modules on a light background with one dominant central result region, generous gutters, varied card shapes, and light paper-like figure cards for every chart or diagram.
- Color grammar: deep indigo/graphite outer atmosphere; primary cyan-blue accent for observed CMS result; secondary warm amber/green accents for expected bands and Weinberg-operator contrast; all scientific figure surfaces warm-white or pearl.
- Avoid old poster rectangular-crop feeling. Make it feel designed from scratch.
````

````yaml
  \ Letters as \\\\href{http://dx.doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.131.011803}{\\\\doi{10.1103/PhysRevLett.131.011803}.}}\\\
  n\\\\begin{document}\\\\cmsNoteHeader{EXO-21-003}\\n\\\\cmsNoteHeader{EXO-21-003}\\\

  n\\\\newcommand{\\\\mN}{m_{N}\\\\xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\\WO}{Weinberg operator\\\
  \\xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\\mjj}{m_{jj}}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\\Vln}{V_{\\\\ell\
  \ N}\\\\xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\\Vlnprime}{V_{\\\\ell' N}\\\\xspace}\\n\\\\\
  newcommand{\\\\Vmn}{V_{\\\\PGm N}\\\\xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\\pT}{p_{T}\\\\\
  xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\\pTmiss}{p_{T}^{\\\\mathrm{miss}}\\\\xspace}\\n\\\\\
  newcommand{\\\\pTvecmiss}{\\\\ensuremath{{\\\\vec p}_{T}^{\\\\kern1pt\\\\text{miss}}}\\\
  \\xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\\hT}{\\\\ensuremath{H_{T}}\\\\xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\
  \\lag}{\\\\ensuremath{\\\\mathcal{L}}\\\\xspace}\\n\\\\title{Probing heavy Majorana\
  \ neutrinos and the Weinberg operator through vector boson fusion processes in proton-proton\
  \ collisions at \\\\texorpdfstring{$\\\\sqrt{s}~=~13~\\\\TeV$}{sqrt(s) = 13 TeV}}\\\
  n\\\\date{\\\\today}\\n\\\\abstract{The first search exploiting the vector boson\
  \ fusion process to probe heavy Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator at\
  \ the LHC is presented. The search is performed in the same-sign dimuon final state\
  \ using a proton-proton collision dataset recorded at $\\\\sqrt{s}=13\\\\TeV$, collected\
  \ with the CMS detector and corresponding to a total integrated luminosity of 138\\\
  \\fbinv. The results are found to agree with the predictions of the standard model.\
  \ For heavy Majorana neutrinos, constraints on the squared mixing element between\
  \ the muon and the heavy neutrino are derived in the heavy neutrino mass range $50\\\
  \\GeV$--$25\\\\TeV$; for masses above 650\\\\GeV these are the most stringent constraints\
  \ from searches at the LHC to date. A first test of the Weinberg operator at colliders\
  \ provides an observed upper limit at 95\\\\% confidence level on the effective\
  \ $\\\\PGm\\\\PGm$ Majorana neutrino mass of 10.8\\\\GeV.}\\n\\\\hypersetup{\\npdfauthor={CMS\
  \ Collaboration},\\npdftitle={Probing Majorana neutrinos and Weinberg operator in\
  \ di-muon channel through vector boson fusion processes in proton-proton collisions\
  \ at 13 TeV},\\npdfsubject={CMS},\\npdfkeywords={CMS, Majorana neutrino, Weinberg\
  \ operator, vector boson fusion}}\\n\\\\maketitle\\nDespite the enormous success\
  \ of the standard model (SM) of particle physics over the last fifty years, the\
  \ observation of neutrino oscillations~\\\\cite{SNO:2002tuh,Super-Kamiokande:2005mbp}\
  \ has confirmed that at least two SM neutrinos have small, but nonzero, masses.\
  \ This provides a compelling hint of physics beyond the SM. Efforts to determine\
  \ each neutrino mass are being pursued by many experiments within different research\
  \ fields, including cosmology and tritium beta decay~\\\\cite{Loureiro:2018pdz,eBOSS:2020yzd,KATRIN:2021uub},\
  \ and various theoretical explanations of these observations have been proposed~\\\
  \\cite{seesaw1,seesaw2,seesaw3,seesaw4,Weinberg79,Das:2015toa,Das:2016hof,Das:2017nvm}.\\\
  nA natural formalism for generating neutrino masses is through a dimension-five\
  \ operator, proposed by Weinberg~\\\\cite{Weinberg79}, which extends the SM Lagrangian\
  \ with\\n\\\\begin{linenomath}\\n\\\\begin{equation}\\n\\\\lag_5 = \\\\frac{\\\\\
  mathrm{C}_5^{\\\\ell\\\\ell'}}{\\\\Lambda} \\\\big[\\\\Phi\\\\!~\\\\cdot~\\\\! \\\
  \\overline{L}^c_{\\\\ell }\\\\big] \\\\big[L_{\\\\ell'}\\\\!\\\\!~\\\\cdot~\\\\\
  !\\\\Phi\\\\big],\\n\\\\label{eqn:Lag_5}\\n\\\\end{equation}\\n\\\\end{linenomath}\\\
  nwhere $\\\\ell ,~\\\\ell'$ are the flavors of the leptons, which can be electrons,\
  \ muons, or taus; $\\\\Lambda$ is the scale at which the particles responsible for\
  \ neutrino masses become relevant degrees of freedom; $\\\\mathrm{C}_5^{\\\\ell\\\
  \\ell'}$ is a flavor-dependent Wilson coefficient; $L_\\\\ell=(\\\\nu_\\\\ell,\\\
  \\ell)$ is the left-handed lepton doublet; and $\\\\Phi$ is the SM Higgs doublet\
  \ with a vacuum expectation value $v=\\\\sqrt{2}\\\\langle\\\\Phi\\\\rangle\\\\\
  approx246\\\\GeV$. This operator, known as the Weinberg operator, generates the\
  \ Majorana neutrino masses as\\n\\\\begin{linenomath}\\n\\\\begin{equation}\\nm_{\\\
  \\ell\\\\ell'} = C_5^{\\\\ell\\\\ell'} v^2/\\\\Lambda,\\n\\\\label{eqn:Majorana_N_mass}\\\
  n\\\\end{equation}\\n\\\\end{linenomath}\\nand introduces lepton number violation\
  \ (LNV), as the Majorana neutrino is its own antiparticle. The LNV processes have\
  \ been tested extensively in searches for neutrinoless double beta decays of heavy\
  \ nuclei. These experiments search for events with two same-sign (SS) charge electrons\
  \ and the absence of neutrinos in the final state, and set stringent upper limits\
  \ on the associated Majorana neutrino mass ($ \\\\abs{m_{ee}}$) at 90\\\\% confidence\
  \ level (\\\\CL) in the ranges 61--165\\\\unit{meV}~\\\\cite{KamLAND-Zen:2016pfg}\
  \ and 79--180\\\\unit{meV}~\\\\cite{Agostini:2020xta}.\\nSince muons and tau leptons\
  \ are much heavier than electrons, SS final states involving these heavier leptons\
  \ are kinematically forbidden in low-energy nuclear experiments and can only be\
  \ studied at colliders~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm}. As the study of tau leptons is experimentally\
  \ more challenging, the final state with SS muons is investigated in this search.\
  \ The observed upper limit on the effective $\\\\PGm\\\\PGm$ Majorana neutrino mass\
  \ ($\\\\abs{m_{\\\\PGm\\\\PGm}}$), translated from the searches for LNV decays of\
  \ charged kaons at the NA62 experiment~\\\\cite{NA62:2019eax}, is around 55\\\\\
  GeV at 90\\\\% \\\\CL~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm}.\\nThe Weinberg operator can be realized\
  \ in the context of ``seesaw'' models~\\\\cite{seesaw1,seesaw2,seesaw3,seesaw4},\
  \ assuming the existence of hypothetical heavy states, for example a heavy Majorana\
  \ neutrino ($\\\\mathit{N}$) in the type-I seesaw model. The small mass of the SM\
  \ neutrinos can thus be explained by a suppression due to the high mass of new particles,\
  \ because $ m_\\\\nu\\\\sim y_\\\\nu^2v^2/ \\\\mN$. In this expression, $m_\\\\\
  nu$ is the SM neutrino mass, $ \\\\mN$ is the mass of the heavy Majorana neutrino,\
  \ and $y_\\\\nu$ is the Yukawa coupling. This ability to explain the small mass\
  \ of the SM neutrinos motivates the search for heavy Majorana neutrinos. Heavy Majorana\
  \ neutrinos can only couple to the SM through mixing with SM neutrinos, which is\
  \ characterized by the mixing element, $\\\\Vln$, between a SM neutrino in its left-handed\
  \ interaction state and a \\\\hmn in its mass eigenstate. The searches that have\
  \ set limits on $\\\\Vln$ were based on the production of a \\\\hmn through either\
  \ quark-antiquark annihilation or $W\\\\PGg$, with different analysis strategies\
  \ based on various decay modes, such as many leptons in the final state~\\\\cite{Sirunyan:2018mtv,Aad:2019kiz,Sirunyan:2019bgz},\
  \ and in final states containing LNV lepton pairs~\\\\cite{Sirunyan:2018xiv,Aaboud:2018spl}.\
  \ For $ \\\\mN$ at a few \\\\GeVns{}, the constraints on $\\\\abs{\\\\Vln}^{2}$,\
  \ where $\\\\ell=\\\\left\\\\{e, \\\\Pgm \\\\right\\\\}$, are around $10^{-7}$--$10^{-5}$,\
  \ while at around 1\\\\TeV, the constraints approach unity.\\nThis Letter reports\
  \ the first search probing Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator in vector\
  \ boson fusion (VBF) processes~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm,Fuks:2020att} at the CERN LHC,\
  \ studying events with SS muon pairs.\\nAs shown in Fig.~\\\\ref{fig:diagram} by\
  \ the two representative Feynman diagrams, in the $t$ channel, SS $W$ boson pairs\
  \ may convert to SS lepton pairs via a \\\\TeVns{}-scale Majorana neutrino or through\
  \ a Weinberg operator process. Because the cross section of $t$-channel processes\
  \ is less sensitive to the mass of the intermediate particle compared with $s$-channel\
  \ quark-antiquark annihilation processes, the VBF process can complement searches\
  \ for heavy Majorana neutrinos at the \\\\TeVns{} mass scale as its cross section\
  \ decreases more slowly with increasing $N$ mass compared with the values from $s$-channel\
  \ production. Although the various seesaw mechanisms can be considered as realizations\
  \ of the Weinberg operator, an alternative implementation is considered in this\
  \ Letter, as shown in Fig.~\\\\ref{fig:diagram} (right). The two VBF processes considered\
  \ in this work differ primarily in that the Majorana process is assumed to be mediated\
  \ by a heavy $t$-channel neutrino whereas the Weinberg operator process is mediated\
  \ by a lighter $t$-channel neutrino.\\n\\\\begin{figure}[h!]\\\\centering\\n\\\\\
  includegraphics[width=0.40\\\\linewidth]{Figure_001-a.pdf}\\n\\\\hspace{13pt}\\\
  n\\\\includegraphics[width=0.40\\\\linewidth]{Figure_001-b.pdf}\\n\\\\caption{Example\
  \ Feynman diagrams of VBF processes with heavy Majorana neutrino production (left)\
  \ and processes mediated by the Weinberg operator (right) at the LHC.}\\\\label{fig:diagram}\\\
  n\\\\end{figure}\\nThis analysis is based on proton-proton ($pp$) collision data\
  \ collected at $\\\\sqrt{s} = 13\\\\TeV$ by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC during\
  \ 2016--2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $138\\\\fbinv$.\\nTabulated\
  \ results are provided in the HEPData record for this analysis~\\\\cite{hepdata}.\\\
  nThe CMS apparatus~\\\\cite{CMS:2008xjf} is a multipurpose, nearly hermetic detector,\
  \ designed to trigger on~\\\\cite{CMS:2020cmk,CMS:2016ngn}\\nand identify electrons,\
  \ muons, photons, and hadrons~\\\\cite{CMS:2020uim,CMS:2018rym,CMS:2014pgm}. A global\
  \ ``particle-flow'' algorithm~\\\\cite{CMS:2017yfk} aims to reconstruct all individual\
  \ particles in an event, combining information provided by the all-silicon inner\
  \ tracker and by the crystal electromagnetic and brass-scintillator hadron calorimeters,\
  \ operating inside a 3.8\\\\unit{T} superconducting solenoid, with data from gas-ionization\
  \ muon detectors embedded in the flux-return yoke outside the solenoid. The reconstructed\
  \ particles are used to build charged leptons, jets, and missing transverse momentum\
  \ ($\\\\pTvecmiss$)~\\\\cite{CMS:2018jrd,CMS:2016lmd,CMS:2019ctu}.\\nSamples of\
  \ signal events are simulated with next-to-leading order (NLO) precision using the\
  \ \\\\MGvATNLO 2.6.5 generator~\\\\cite{Alwall:2014hca}, based on model implementations\
  \ from Refs.~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm,Alva:2014gxa,Degrande:2016aje,Fuks:2020att}.\
  \ For the heavy Majorana neutrino, we assume only one heavy state and scan its mass\
  \ in a range from 50\\\\GeV to 25\\\\TeV. The process induced by the Weinberg operator\
  \ is simulated using a novel approach, established in Ref.~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm},\
  \ which approximates the internal neutrino lines and vertex insertion with an effective\
  \ light Majorana neutrino. The Wilson coefficient $\\\\mathrm{C}_5^{\\\\ell\\\\\
  ell'}$ is set to 1, and the energy scale $\\\\Lambda$ to 200\\\\TeV. The production\
  \ cross sections scale with $\\\\Vln ^{2} \\\\Vlnprime^{2}$ and $\\\\abs{\\\\mathrm{C}_5^{\\\
  \\ell\\\\ell'}/\\\\Lambda }^{2}$ for the VBF processes with heavy Majorana neutrinos~\\\
  \\cite{Fuks:2020att} and the Weinberg operator~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm}, respectively.\
  \ Since the kinematic shape of the signal is independent of $\\\\abs{ \\\\Vmn }$,\
  \ we set $\\\\abs{ \\\\Vmn } = 1$ for the signal simulation to ensure efficient\
  \ generation of signal events.\\nThe SM electroweak $\\\\WW$ and $W^{\\\\pm} Z$\
  \ processes, where both bosons decay leptonically, are simulated using \\\\MGvATNLO\
  \ 2.4.2~\\\\cite{Alwall:2014hca} at leading order (LO) with six electroweak $\\\\\
  left[ \\\\mathcal{O}(\\\\alpha^6) \\\\right]$ and zero quantum chromodynamics (QCD)\
  \ vertices. The QCD-induced $\\\\WW$ process is also simulated using \\\\MGvATNLO\
  \ 2.4.2 at LO. Contributions with an initial-state $b$ quark are excluded from the\
  \ electroweak $W^{\\\\pm} Z$ simulation because they are included in the production\
  \ of a $Z$ boson in association with a single top quark, known as the $tZq$ process,\
  \ which is simulated at NLO using \\\\MGvATNLO 2.3.3.\\nThe $ZZ \\\\to 4 \\\\ell$\
  \ and $gg \\\\to ZZ$ processes are simulated with the $\\\\POWHEG$ v2~\\\\cite{Nason:2013ydw}\
  \ and $\\\\MCFM$ 7.0.1~\\\\cite{Campbell:2011bn} generators, respectively. The production\
  \ of $\\\\TTBar W^{\\\\pm}$, $\\\\TTBar Z$, and triple vector boson ($VVV$) background\
  \ events is simulated at NLO in QCD using the \\\\MGvATNLO 2.2.2 (2.4.2) generator~\\\
  \\cite{Alwall:2014hca,MadGraph,Frederix:2012ps} for the samples corresponding to\
  \ the 2016 (2017--2018) data-taking period. The production of $\\\\WW$ even...\"\
  \n}"
````

````yaml
  \ physics symbols with ambiguous prose when equations or standard variables are\
  \ clearer..\n- For a professional HEP audience, make dataset/selection and analysis-strategy\
  \ sections analysis-specific, not generic.\n- Extract concrete luminosity/energy/channel,\
  \ object thresholds, SR/CR definitions, binning variables, fit observable, likelihood/CLs\
  \ method, normalization factors, nuisance/systematic treatment, and dominant uncertainties\
  \ when present.\n- Preserve HEP notation with unambiguous glyphs: γ must remain\
  \ Greek gamma, never Latin y; in compact public labels, prefer the word gamma when\
  \ a rendered glyph would be ambiguous.\n- Do not use a generic workflow like 'pp\
  \ collisions → candidates → topology → SR/CR → fit' as the main analysis graphic.\n\
  - If a flowchart is useful, make it a compact HEP region/fit schematic with concrete\
  \ SR bins, CR labels, fitted observables, and nuisance/systematic blocks.\n- When\
  \ a section gets a 'flowchart' field, treat each node as a concrete information\
  \ capsule, not a generic stage label.\n- Each flowchart node should contain at least\
  \ one paper-specific number, variable, threshold, region label, fitted observable,\
  \ uncertainty label, or statistical-method detail.\n- Bad node: 'preselection'.\
  \ Good node: '>=2 same-sign muons: pT>30 GeV, |eta|<2.4; >=2 jets pT>30 GeV'.\n\
  - Bad node: 'signal region'. Good node: 'HMN SR binned in Delta phi(ll) | Weinberg\
  \ SR binned in pTmiss, split at 50 GeV'.\n- Bad node: 'fit'. Good node: 'Simultaneous\
  \ SR/CR fit; WZ/top/fake norms constrained; profile-likelihood CLs'.\n- Use a '|'\
  \ character inside a node label only when the analysis genuinely branches into parallel\
  \ SR/CR/category paths.\n- Order nodes in true data-flow order: dataset -> object/event\
  \ selection -> categorization -> SR/CR definition -> fit/model -> output result.\n\
  - Keep each node under 22 words; use the paper's own symbols and unit suffixes when\
  \ explicitly present.\n- Produce 4-5 nodes total; fewer is fine. Do not pad with\
  \ generic stages.\n- Skip the flowchart entirely or leave it empty if the source\
  \ text does not provide concrete data-flow details.\n- Keep rendered text compact\
  \ but information-rich: prefer short public bullets, data badges, and one-line claims\
  \ over paragraphs.\n- Do not make a sparse cover image. Aim for 14-24 public information\
  \ units across the poster: section claims, badges, concise bullets, and conclusion\
  \ takeaways.\n- Each section should have at most one short body sentence plus 2-4\
  \ high-value bullets unless the source requires otherwise; use more sections or\
  \ badges rather than long paragraphs.\n- Each placeholder must have id, section,\
  \ label, aspect, and asset filename.\n- Plan one hero placeholder for the headline\
  \ result/limit/cross-section plot and 2-3 supporting placeholders for strategy/background/context.\n\
  - Captions must be public-facing scientific descriptions, not design instructions;\
  \ avoid wording like 'Use...', 'Draw...', 'Place...', or 'Bottom strip should...'.\n\
  - Do not leak workflow notes, TODOs, or internal replacement language into public\

  \ reserve a wide method section for them before adding extra text-only sections.\n\
````
