  : []\n    }\n  ],\n  \"source_text_excerpt\": \"\\\\pdfoutput=1\\n\\\\documentclass[11pt,twoside,a4paper,cmspaper,final,collab]{cms-tdr}\\\
  n\\\\def\\\\svnVersion{0481bee}\\\\def\\\\svnDate{2023/07/11}\\\\def\\\\cmsCernNoTag{CERN-EP-2022-105}\\\
  \\def\\\\cmsCernDate{\\\\today}\\\\def\\\\cmsMessage{Published in Physical Review\
  \ Letters as \\\\href{http://dx.doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.131.011803}{\\\\doi{10.1103/PhysRevLett.131.011803}.}}\\\
  n\\\\begin{document}\\\\cmsNoteHeader{EXO-21-003}\\n\\\\cmsNoteHeader{EXO-21-003}\\\
  n\\\\newcommand{\\\\dphill}{\\\\ensuremath{\\\\Delta\\\\phi_{\\\\ell\\\\ell}}\\\\\
  xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\\WW}{\\\\ensuremath{W^{\\\\pm} W^{\\\\pm}}\\\\xspace}\\\
  n\\\\newcommand{\\\\WZ}{\\\\ensuremath{W^{\\\\pm} Z}\\\\xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\
  \\ZZ}{\\\\ensuremath{Z Z}\\\\xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\\TTBar}{\\\\ensuremath{t\\\
  \\bar{t}}\\\\xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\\hmn}{heavy Majorana neutrino\\\\xspace}\\\
  n\\\\newcommand{\\\\mN}{m_{N}\\\\xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\\WO}{Weinberg operator\\\
  \\xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\\mjj}{m_{jj}}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\\Vln}{V_{\\\\ell\
  \ N}\\\\xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\\Vlnprime}{V_{\\\\ell' N}\\\\xspace}\\n\\\\\
  newcommand{\\\\Vmn}{V_{\\\\PGm N}\\\\xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\\pT}{p_{T}\\\\\
  xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\\pTmiss}{p_{T}^{\\\\mathrm{miss}}\\\\xspace}\\n\\\\\
  newcommand{\\\\pTvecmiss}{\\\\ensuremath{{\\\\vec p}_{T}^{\\\\kern1pt\\\\text{miss}}}\\\
  \\xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\\hT}{\\\\ensuremath{H_{T}}\\\\xspace}\\n\\\\newcommand{\\\
  \\lag}{\\\\ensuremath{\\\\mathcal{L}}\\\\xspace}\\n\\\\title{Probing heavy Majorana\
  \ neutrinos and the Weinberg operator through vector boson fusion processes in proton-proton\
  \ collisions at \\\\texorpdfstring{$\\\\sqrt{s}~=~13~\\\\TeV$}{sqrt(s) = 13 TeV}}\\\
  n\\\\date{\\\\today}\\n\\\\abstract{The first search exploiting the vector boson\
  \ fusion process to probe heavy Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator at\
  \ the LHC is presented. The search is performed in the same-sign dimuon final state\
  \ using a proton-proton collision dataset recorded at $\\\\sqrt{s}=13\\\\TeV$, collected\
  \ with the CMS detector and corresponding to a total integrated luminosity of 138\\\
  \\fbinv. The results are found to agree with the predictions of the standard model.\
  \ For heavy Majorana neutrinos, constraints on the squared mixing element between\
  \ the muon and the heavy neutrino are derived in the heavy neutrino mass range $50\\\
  \\GeV$--$25\\\\TeV$; for masses above 650\\\\GeV these are the most stringent constraints\
  \ from searches at the LHC to date. A first test of the Weinberg operator at colliders\
  \ provides an observed upper limit at 95\\\\% confidence level on the effective\
  \ $\\\\PGm\\\\PGm$ Majorana neutrino mass of 10.8\\\\GeV.}\\n\\\\hypersetup{\\npdfauthor={CMS\
  \ Collaboration},\\npdftitle={Probing Majorana neutrinos and Weinberg operator in\
  \ di-muon channel through vector boson fusion processes in proton-proton collisions\
  \ at 13 TeV},\\npdfsubject={CMS},\\npdfkeywords={CMS, Majorana neutrino, Weinberg\
  \ operator, vector boson fusion}}\\n\\\\maketitle\\nDespite the enormous success\
  \ of the standard model (SM) of particle physics over the last fifty years, the\
  \ observation of neutrino oscillations~\\\\cite{SNO:2002tuh,Super-Kamiokande:2005mbp}\
  \ has confirmed that at least two SM neutrinos have small, but nonzero, masses.\
  \ This provides a compelling hint of physics beyond the SM. Efforts to determine\
  \ each neutrino mass are being pursued by many experiments within different research\
  \ fields, including cosmology and tritium beta decay~\\\\cite{Loureiro:2018pdz,eBOSS:2020yzd,KATRIN:2021uub},\
  \ and various theoretical explanations of these observations have been proposed~\\\
  \\cite{seesaw1,seesaw2,seesaw3,seesaw4,Weinberg79,Das:2015toa,Das:2016hof,Das:2017nvm}.\\\
  nA natural formalism for generating neutrino masses is through a dimension-five\
  \ operator, proposed by Weinberg~\\\\cite{Weinberg79}, which extends the SM Lagrangian\
  \ with\\n\\\\begin{linenomath}\\n\\\\begin{equation}\\n\\\\lag_5 = \\\\frac{\\\\\
  mathrm{C}_5^{\\\\ell\\\\ell'}}{\\\\Lambda} \\\\big[\\\\Phi\\\\!~\\\\cdot~\\\\! \\\
  \\overline{L}^c_{\\\\ell }\\\\big] \\\\big[L_{\\\\ell'}\\\\!\\\\!~\\\\cdot~\\\\\
  !\\\\Phi\\\\big],\\n\\\\label{eqn:Lag_5}\\n\\\\end{equation}\\n\\\\end{linenomath}\\\
  nwhere $\\\\ell ,~\\\\ell'$ are the flavors of the leptons, which can be electrons,\
  \ muons, or taus; $\\\\Lambda$ is the scale at which the particles responsible for\
  \ neutrino masses become relevant degrees of freedom; $\\\\mathrm{C}_5^{\\\\ell\\\
  \\ell'}$ is a flavor-dependent Wilson coefficient; $L_\\\\ell=(\\\\nu_\\\\ell,\\\
  \\ell)$ is the left-handed lepton doublet; and $\\\\Phi$ is the SM Higgs doublet\
  \ with a vacuum expectation value $v=\\\\sqrt{2}\\\\langle\\\\Phi\\\\rangle\\\\\
  approx246\\\\GeV$. This operator, known as the Weinberg operator, generates the\
  \ Majorana neutrino masses as\\n\\\\begin{linenomath}\\n\\\\begin{equation}\\nm_{\\\
  \\ell\\\\ell'} = C_5^{\\\\ell\\\\ell'} v^2/\\\\Lambda,\\n\\\\label{eqn:Majorana_N_mass}\\\
  n\\\\end{equation}\\n\\\\end{linenomath}\\nand introduces lepton number violation\
  \ (LNV), as the Majorana neutrino is its own antiparticle. The LNV processes have\
  \ been tested extensively in searches for neutrinoless double beta decays of heavy\
  \ nuclei. These experiments search for events with two same-sign (SS) charge electrons\
  \ and the absence of neutrinos in the final state, and set stringent upper limits\
  \ on the associated Majorana neutrino mass ($ \\\\abs{m_{ee}}$) at 90\\\\% confidence\
  \ level (\\\\CL) in the ranges 61--165\\\\unit{meV}~\\\\cite{KamLAND-Zen:2016pfg}\
  \ and 79--180\\\\unit{meV}~\\\\cite{Agostini:2020xta}.\\nSince muons and tau leptons\
  \ are much heavier than electrons, SS final states involving these heavier leptons\
  \ are kinematically forbidden in low-energy nuclear experiments and can only be\
  \ studied at colliders~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm}. As the study of tau leptons is experimentally\
  \ more challenging, the final state with SS muons is investigated in this search.\
  \ The observed upper limit on the effective $\\\\PGm\\\\PGm$ Majorana neutrino mass\
  \ ($\\\\abs{m_{\\\\PGm\\\\PGm}}$), translated from the searches for LNV decays of\
  \ charged kaons at the NA62 experiment~\\\\cite{NA62:2019eax}, is around 55\\\\\
  GeV at 90\\\\% \\\\CL~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm}.\\nThe Weinberg operator can be realized\
  \ in the context of ``seesaw'' models~\\\\cite{seesaw1,seesaw2,seesaw3,seesaw4},\
  \ assuming the existence of hypothetical heavy states, for example a heavy Majorana\
  \ neutrino ($\\\\mathit{N}$) in the type-I seesaw model. The small mass of the SM\
  \ neutrinos can thus be explained by a suppression due to the high mass of new particles,\
  \ because $ m_\\\\nu\\\\sim y_\\\\nu^2v^2/ \\\\mN$. In this expression, $m_\\\\\
  nu$ is the SM neutrino mass, $ \\\\mN$ is the mass of the heavy Majorana neutrino,\
  \ and $y_\\\\nu$ is the Yukawa coupling. This ability to explain the small mass\
  \ of the SM neutrinos motivates the search for heavy Majorana neutrinos. Heavy Majorana\
  \ neutrinos can only couple to the SM through mixing with SM neutrinos, which is\
  \ characterized by the mixing element, $\\\\Vln$, between a SM neutrino in its left-handed\
  \ interaction state and a \\\\hmn in its mass eigenstate. The searches that have\
  \ set limits on $\\\\Vln$ were based on the production of a \\\\hmn through either\
  \ quark-antiquark annihilation or $W\\\\PGg$, with different analysis strategies\
  \ based on various decay modes, such as many leptons in the final state~\\\\cite{Sirunyan:2018mtv,Aad:2019kiz,Sirunyan:2019bgz},\
  \ and in final states containing LNV lepton pairs~\\\\cite{Sirunyan:2018xiv,Aaboud:2018spl}.\
  \ For $ \\\\mN$ at a few \\\\GeVns{}, the constraints on $\\\\abs{\\\\Vln}^{2}$,\
  \ where $\\\\ell=\\\\left\\\\{e, \\\\Pgm \\\\right\\\\}$, are around $10^{-7}$--$10^{-5}$,\
  \ while at around 1\\\\TeV, the constraints approach unity.\\nThis Letter reports\
  \ the first search probing Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator in vector\
  \ boson fusion (VBF) processes~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm,Fuks:2020att} at the CERN LHC,\
  \ studying events with SS muon pairs.\\nAs shown in Fig.~\\\\ref{fig:diagram} by\
  \ the two representative Feynman diagrams, in the $t$ channel, SS $W$ boson pairs\
  \ may convert to SS lepton pairs via a \\\\TeVns{}-scale Majorana neutrino or through\
  \ a Weinberg operator process. Because the cross section of $t$-channel processes\
  \ is less sensitive to the mass of the intermediate particle compared with $s$-channel\
  \ quark-antiquark annihilation processes, the VBF process can complement searches\
  \ for heavy Majorana neutrinos at the \\\\TeVns{} mass scale as its cross section\
  \ decreases more slowly with increasing $N$ mass compared with the values from $s$-channel\
  \ production. Although the various seesaw mechanisms can be considered as realizations\
  \ of the Weinberg operator, an alternative implementation is considered in this\
  \ Letter, as shown in Fig.~\\\\ref{fig:diagram} (right). The two VBF processes considered\
  \ in this work differ primarily in that the Majorana process is assumed to be mediated\
  \ by a heavy $t$-channel neutrino whereas the Weinberg operator process is mediated\
  \ by a lighter $t$-channel neutrino.\\n\\\\begin{figure}[h!]\\\\centering\\n\\\\\
  includegraphics[width=0.40\\\\linewidth]{Figure_001-a.pdf}\\n\\\\hspace{13pt}\\\
  n\\\\includegraphics[width=0.40\\\\linewidth]{Figure_001-b.pdf}\\n\\\\caption{Example\
  \ Feynman diagrams of VBF processes with heavy Majorana neutrino production (left)\
  \ and processes mediated by the Weinberg operator (right) at the LHC.}\\\\label{fig:diagram}\\\
  n\\\\end{figure}\\nThis analysis is based on proton-proton ($pp$) collision data\
  \ collected at $\\\\sqrt{s} = 13\\\\TeV$ by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC during\
  \ 2016--2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $138\\\\fbinv$.\\nTabulated\
  \ results are provided in the HEPData record for this analysis~\\\\cite{hepdata}.\\\
  nThe CMS apparatus~\\\\cite{CMS:2008xjf} is a multipurpose, nearly hermetic detector,\
  \ designed to trigger on~\\\\cite{CMS:2020cmk,CMS:2016ngn}\\nand identify electrons,\
  \ muons, photons, and hadrons~\\\\cite{CMS:2020uim,CMS:2018rym,CMS:2014pgm}. A global\
  \ ``particle-flow'' algorithm~\\\\cite{CMS:2017yfk} aims to reconstruct all individual\
  \ particles in an event, combining information provided by the all-silicon inner\
  \ tracker and by the crystal electromagnetic and brass-scintillator hadron calorimeters,\
  \ operating inside a 3.8\\\\unit{T} superconducting solenoid, with data from gas-ionization\
  \ muon detectors embedded in the flux-return yoke outside the solenoid. The reconstructed\
  \ particles are used to build charged leptons, jets, and missing transverse momentum\
  \ ($\\\\pTvecmiss$)~\\\\cite{CMS:2018jrd,CMS:2016lmd,CMS:2019ctu}.\\nSamples of\
  \ signal events are simulated with next-to-leading order (NLO) precision using the\
  \ \\\\MGvATNLO 2.6.5 generator~\\\\cite{Alwall:2014hca}, based on model implementations\
  \ from Refs.~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm,Alva:2014gxa,Degrande:2016aje,Fuks:2020att}.\
  \ For the heavy Majorana neutrino, we assume only one heavy state and scan its mass\
  \ in a range from 50\\\\GeV to 25\\\\TeV. The process induced by the Weinberg operator\
  \ is simulated using a novel approach, established in Ref.~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm},\
  \ which approximates the internal neutrino lines and vertex insertion with an effective\
  \ light Majorana neutrino. The Wilson coefficient $\\\\mathrm{C}_5^{\\\\ell\\\\\
  ell'}$ is set to 1, and the energy scale $\\\\Lambda$ to 200\\\\TeV. The production\
  \ cross sections scale with $\\\\Vln ^{2} \\\\Vlnprime^{2}$ and $\\\\abs{\\\\mathrm{C}_5^{\\\
  \\ell\\\\ell'}/\\\\Lambda }^{2}$ for the VBF processes with heavy Majorana neutrinos~\\\
  \\cite{Fuks:2020att} and the Weinberg operator~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm}, respectively.\
  \ Since the kinematic shape of the signal is independent of $\\\\abs{ \\\\Vmn }$,\
  \ we set $\\\\abs{ \\\\Vmn } = 1$ for the signal simulation to ensure efficient\
  \ generation of signal events.\\nThe SM electroweak $\\\\WW$ and $W^{\\\\pm} Z$\
  \ processes, where both bosons decay leptonically, are simulated using \\\\MGvATNLO\
  \ 2.4.2~\\\\cite{Alwall:2014hca} at leading order (LO) with six electroweak $\\\\\
  left[ \\\\mathcal{O}(\\\\alpha^6) \\\\right]$ and zero quantum chromodynamics (QCD)\
  \ vertices. The QCD-induced $\\\\WW$ process is also simulated using \\\\MGvATNLO\
  \ 2.4.2 at LO. Contributions with an initial-state $b$ quark are excluded from the\
  \ electroweak $W^{\\\\pm} Z$ simulation because they are included in the production\
  \ of a $Z$ boson in association with a single top quark, known as the $tZq$ process,\
  \ which is simulated at NLO using \\\\MGvATNLO 2.3.3.\\nThe $ZZ \\\\to 4 \\\\ell$\
  \ and $gg \\\\to ZZ$ processes are simulated with the $\\\\POWHEG$ v2~\\\\cite{Nason:2013ydw}\
  \ and $\\\\MCFM$ 7.0.1~\\\\cite{Campbell:2011bn} generators, respectively. The production\
  \ of $\\\\TTBar W^{\\\\pm}$, $\\\\TTBar Z$, and triple vector boson ($VVV$) background\
  \ events is simulated at NLO in QCD using the \\\\MGvATNLO 2.2.2 (2.4.2) generator~\\\
  \\cite{Alwall:2014hca,MadGraph,Frederix:2012ps} for the samples corresponding to\
  \ the 2016 (2017--2018) data-taking period. The production of $\\\\WW$ events through\
  \ double-parton scattering is generated at LO using \\\\PYTHIA 8.226 (8.230)~\\\\\
  cite{Sjostrand:2014zea} for 2016 (2017--2018).\\nThe simulated samples for the 2016\
  \ (2017--2018) data-taking period use the NNPDF 3.0 (3.1) parton distribution functions~\\\
  \\cite{Ball:2014uwa,Ball:2017nwa}, and are interfaced with \\\\PYTHIA to model the\
  \ fragmentation and hadronization of partons in the initial and final states, along\
  \ with the underlying event. The CUETP8M1 (CP5) tune~\\\\cite{Khachatryan:2015pea,Sirunyan:2019dfx}\
  \ is used in the simulation for the 2016 (2017--2018) data-taking period. In LO\
  \ (NLO) simulations performed with \\\\MGvATNLO, jets are matched to the parton\
  \ shower produced by \\\\PYTHIA 8.2 following the MLM~\\\\cite{Alwall:2007fs} (FxFx~\\\
  \\cite{Frederix:2012ps}) prescription. The interactions of all final-state particles\
  \ with the CMS detector are simulated using \\\\GEANTfour~\\\\cite{Agostinelli:2002hh}.\
  \ Simulated events are mixed with the contribution of particles from additional\
  \ $pp$ interactions within the same or nearby bunch crossings (pileup); the pileup\
  \ distribution in the simulated samples matches that observed in data.\\nCollision\
  \ events are collected using single-muon triggers~\\\\cite{CMS:2016ngn} that require\
  \ the presence of an isolated muon with transverse momentum $\\\\pT > 24$ or 27\\\
  \\GeV, depending on the data-taking period. In addition, a set of dimuon triggers~\\\
  \\cite{CMS:2016ngn} with lower $\\\\pT$ thresholds is used to ensure a trigger efficiency\
  \ above 90\\\\% for events with muons. Depending on the subsequent off-line selection,\
  \ the dimuon triggers increase the event acceptance by up to 4\\\\%. The primary\
  \ vertex (PV) is taken to be the vertex corresponding to the hardest scattering\
  \ in the event, evaluated using tracking information alone, as described in Section\
  \ 9.4.1 of Ref.~\\\\cite{CMS-TDR-15-02}.\\nThe jets are clustered using the anti-\\\
  \\kt algorithm~\\\\cite{Cacciari:2011ma,Cacciari:2008gp} with a distance parameter\
  \ of 0.4, with the tracks assigned to the candidate vertices as inputs. To mitigate\
  \ the impact from pileup, tracks identified to be originating from pileup vertices\
  \ are discarded and calorimeter energies are corrected to account for charged and\
  \ neutral particles originating from those vertices. The $\\\\pTvecmiss$ is then\
  \ defined as the negative vector $\\\\pT$ sum of all reconstructed particles in\
  \ an event. Its magnitude is referred to as $\\\\pTmiss$. Jets arising from $b$\
  \ quark hadronization and decay ($b$ jets) are identified using a deep neural network\
  \ algorithm, termed \\\\textsc{DeepCSV}, whose inputs are tracks displaced from\
  \ the primary interaction vertex, details of secondary vertices, and the kinematical\
  \ variables of jets~\\\\cite{Sirunyan:2017ezt}. To classify jets as $b$ tagged,\
  \ we use a requirement on the score of the \\\\textsc{DeepCSV} algorithm for which\
  \ the $b$ jet identification efficiency ranges from 65 to 75\\\\% and the rate at\
  \ which gluon or light-flavor jets are misidentified as $b$ jets is around 1\\\\\
  %. The fraction of jets originating from the hadronization of $c$ quarks that are\
  \ incorrectly identified as $b$ jets is about 10\\\\%.\\nStarting from the constituents\
  \ of reconstructed jets, hadronically decaying $\\\\tau$ leptons are identified\
  \ via the ``hadrons-plus-strips'' algorithm~\\\\cite{CMS:2018jrd}.\\nThe final states\
  \ analyzed contain two well-identified SS muons with $\\\\pT > 30\\\\GeV$ and pseudorapidity\
  \ $\\\\abs{\\\\eta} < 2.4$, and at least two jets with $\\\\pT > 30\\\\GeV$ and\
  \ $\\\\abs{\\\\eta} < 4.7$. The two selected jets with the largest $\\\\pT$ are\
  \ considered as the VBF jet candidates, which must satisfy a large pseudorapidity\
  \ separation $\\\\abs{\\\\Delta\\\\eta_{jj}} > 2.5$ and a large dijet invariant\
  \ mass $m_{jj} > 750 \\\\GeV$. Events produced via VBF are expected to contain rapidity\
  \ gaps between the muons and the VBF jets. To utilize this signature, we require\
  \ max$\\\\left ( \\\\mathcal{Z}_{\\\\ell} \\\\right ) < 0.75$, where $\\\\mathcal{Z}_{\\\
  \\ell}$ is the Zeppenfeld variable~\\\\cite{zepp1996} of a lepton $\\\\ell$: $\\\
  \\mathcal{Z}_{\\\\ell} = \\\\abs{ \\\\eta_{\\\\ell} -(\\\\eta_{j1}+\\\\eta_{j2})/2\
  \ }/ \\\\abs{ \\\\Delta \\\\eta_{jj} }$, where $\\\\eta_{\\\\ell}$ is the pseudorapidity\
  \ of the lepton, and $\\\\eta_{j1}$ and $\\\\eta_{j2}$ are of the two VBF jets.\
  \ Events with an additional loosely identified muon (electron) with $\\\\pT > 10\
  \ \\\\GeV$ and $\\\\abs{\\\\eta} < 2.5 (2.4)$ or an identified hadronically decaying\
  \ tau lepton with $\\\\pT > 20 \\\\GeV$ and $\\\\abs{\\\\eta}<2.3$ are rejected\
  \ to suppress backgrounds such as $W^{\\\\pm} Z$ production. Because the signal\
  \ processes do not produce final state neutrinos other than those produced in hadron\
  \ decays, $\\\\pTmiss$ is a useful discriminant to separate the signal and backgrounds.\
  \ For the analysis targeting processes with heavy Majorana neutrinos, the azimuthal\
  \ separation variable $\\\\dphill$ is better for improving the sensitivity to the\
  \ signal than $\\\\pTmiss$ because the two muons in the final state tend to be more\
  \ back-to-back than in background processes~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020att}. However, $\\\
  \\pTmiss$ is more discriminating than azimuthal separation for the Weinberg operator\
  \ process because of the different event topology resulting from the discrepancy\
  \ between the two $t$-channel propagators. To separate the signal and the SM electroweak\
  \ $\\\\WW$ events, signal regions (SRs) for the \\\\hmn and Weinberg operator analyses\
  \ are defined in bins of $\\\\dphill$ and $\\\\pTmiss$, respectively. For the \\\
  \\hmn analysis, we define a high-$\\\\dphill$ bin ($\\\\dphill > 2$) and a low-$\\\
  \\dphill$ bin ($\\\\dphill < 2$) in the SR. For the Weinberg operator analysis,\
  \ a low-$\\\\pTmiss$ bin ($<~$50\\\\GeV) and a high-$\\\\pTmiss$ bin ($>~$50\\\\\
  GeV) are defined in the SR.\\nThe background from opposite-sign dilepton events\
  \ where one of the lepton charges is misidentified is negligible for events with\
  \ muon pairs~\\\\cite{CMS:2009fdy,CMS:2019ied}. The so-called nonprompt-lepton backgrounds,\
  \ originating from leptonic decays of heavy quarks or hadrons misidentified as leptons,\
  \ are suppressed by identification and isolation requirements.\\nEvents from a $\\\
  \\TTBar$ pair where only one $W$ boson decays leptonically are the main source of\
  \ nonprompt-lepton backgrounds. To reduce this contribution, events with at least\
  \ one $b$-tagged jet with $\\\\pT > 20\\\\GeV$ and $\\\\abs{\\\\eta}<2.4$ are rejected.\
  \ The remaining contribution of the nonprompt-lepton background is estimated directly\
  \ from a data sample by applying weights to events containing muon candidates that\
  \ fail the nominal selection criteria while passing a less stringent isolation requirement.\
  \ These weights, called fake-lepton factors, are obtained from the probability of\
  \ a jet being misidentified as a lepton and the efficiency of correctly reconstructing\
  \ and identifying a lepton. More details about this method are given in Refs.~\\\
  \\cite{Sirunyan:2018egh,CMS:2020dvg}.\\nTo constrain the reducible background contributions,\
  \ which include $W^{\\\\pm} Z$ production and backgrounds from nonprompt leptons,\
  \ several control regions (CRs) in data are used. These CRs are defined to select\
  \ samples of events enriched in those background processes, following the procedure\
  \ described in Refs.~\\\\cite{Sirunyan:2017ret,Sirunyan:2020gyx,Sirunyan:2020gvn}.\\\
  nA $WZ$ CR, requiring the presence of three muons in an event, is used to estimate\
  \ $W^{\\\\pm} Z$ background contributions. The opposite-sign dimuon combination\
  \ with invariant mass closest to the $Z$ boson mass ($m_{Z}$) is considered as the\
  \ $Z$ boson decay product, whereas the remaining muon is assumed to originate from\
  \ the decay of the $W$ boson. The selection criteria defining the SR and the $WZ$\
  \ CR are summarized in Table~\\\\ref{tab:regions}.\\nTo select event samples enriched\
  \ in nonprompt leptons, a $b$-tagged CR is defined by using the same selection as\
  \ for the SR, however requiring the presence of a $b$-tagged jet. Similarly, the\
  \ $WZb$ CR is defined by requiring the same selection as for the WZ CR, but requiring\
  \ at least one $b$-tagged jet. The dominant backgrounds in the SR are SM electroweak\
  \ $\\\\WW$ production and the contribution from nonprompt leptons.\\n\\\\begin{table*}[htbp]\\\
  n\\\\centering\\n\\\\topcaption{Signal region and $WZ$ control region definitions.\
  \ The signal region is binned differently for the heavy Majorana neutrino and Weinberg\
  \ operator analyses. A $b$-tagged CR is defined by using the same selection as for\
  \ the SR, however requiring the presence of a $b$-tagged jet. A $WZb$ CR is defined\
  \ by requiring the same selection as for the $WZ$ CR, but requiring at least one\
  \ $b$-tagged jet.}\\n\\\\begin{scotch}{l c c}\\nVariable & SR & $WZ$ CR \\\\\\\\\
  \\n\\\\hline\\nNumber of leptons & Exactly 2 same-sign muons & Exactly 3 muons \\\
  \\\\\\\\nLepton $\\\\pT$ & $>~$30/30~\\\\GeV & $>~$25/25/10~\\\\GeV \\\\\\\\\\nLepton\
  \ \\\\abs{\\\\eta} & $<~$2.4 & $<~$2.4 \\\\\\\\\\nJet $\\\\pT$ & $>~$30~\\\\GeV\
  \ & $>~$30~\\\\GeV \\\\\\\\\\nJet \\\\abs{\\\\eta} & $<~$4.7 & $<~$4.7 \\\\\\\\\\\
  nDilepton mass $m_{\\\\ell \\\\ell}$ & $>~$20~\\\\GeV & \\\\NA \\\\\\\\\\n$\\\\\
  abs{m_{\\\\ell \\\\ell}-m_{Z}}$ & \\\\NA & $<~$15~\\\\GeV (for one $\\\\PGmp\\\\\
  PGmm$ pair) \\\\\\\\\\nTrilepton mass $m_{\\\\ell \\\\ell \\\\ell}$ & \\\\NA & $>~$100~\\\
  \\GeV \\\\\\\\\\nMax $\\\\left ( \\\\mathcal{Z}_{\\\\ell} \\\\right )$ & $<~$0.75\
  \ & $<~$1.0 \\\\\\\\\\n$\\\\pTmiss$ & \\\\NA & $>~$30~\\\\GeV \\\\\\\\\\n$b$-tagged\
  \ jet veto & Required & Required \\\\\\\\\\nHadronic $\\\\tau$ veto & Required &\
  \ Required \\\\\\\\\\n$\\\\mjj$ & $>~$750~\\\\GeV & $>~$750~\\\\GeV \\\\\\\\\\n$\\\
  \\abs{\\\\Delta\\\\eta_{jj}}$ & $>~$2.5 & $>~$2.5 \\\\\\\\\\n\\\\end{scotch}\\n\\\
  \\label{tab:regions}\\n\\\\end{table*}\\nThe discriminating variable used to search\
  \ for a signal for both analyses is $\\\\hT/\\\\pT^{\\\\PGm_1}$. Here, $\\\\hT$\
  \ is the scalar sum of jet $\\\\pT$ for all jets with $\\\\pT>30\\\\GeV$ and $\\\
  \\abs{\\\\eta} < 4.7$, $\\\\PGm_1$ indicates the highest $\\\\pT$ muon.\\nThis discriminating\
  \ variable measures the amount of hadronic activity relative to leptonic activity\
  \ in a given event, and is sensitive to the color structure of the hard scattering\
  \ processes as discussed in Ref.~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm}. As hadronic activity is\
  \ typically suppressed in VBF production processes, $\\\\hT/\\\\pT^{\\\\PGm_1}$\
  \ tends to be smaller for signal events than for background events~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm,Fuks:2020att}.\\\
  nThe statistical analysis is performed with a profile likelihood ratio test statistic\
  \ in which systematic uncertainties are modeled as constrained nuisance parameters.\
  \ Limits are set using the modified frequentist \\\\CLs criterion~\\\\cite{CLS2,CLS1},\
  \ and the asymptotic approximation~\\\\cite{Cowan:2010js} is used in the limit setting\
  \ procedure. The integrated luminosities of the 2016, 2017, and 2018 data-taking\
  \ periods are individually known with uncertainties in the range 1.2--2.5\\\\%~\\\
  \\cite{CMS:2021xjt,CMS:2018elu,CMS:2019jhq}, while the uncertainty in the total\
  \ integrated luminosity in 2016--2018 is 1.6\\\\%. The simulation of pileup events\
  \ assumes a total inelastic $pp$ cross section of 69.2\\\\unit{mb}, with an associated\
  \ uncertainty of 5\\\\%~\\\\cite{ATLAS:2016pu,Sirunyan:2018nqx}, which has an impact\
  \ of approximately 1\\\\% on the expected signal and background yields. Discrepancies\
  \ in the lepton reconstruction and identification efficiencies between data and\
  \ simulation are corrected for by applying scale factors to all simulated samples,\
  \ and the associated uncertainty is around 2\\\\%. Uncertainties in both the muon\
  \ momentum scale and resolution individually amount to about 0.2\\\\%. The simulated\
  \ muon momentum resolution is corrected by applying a 15\\\\% Gaussian smearing\
  \ to muons with $\\\\pT > 200\\\\GeV$~\\\\cite{CMS:2019ied}.\\nThe resolution uncertainty\
  \ and the momentum scale uncertainty for high-$\\\\pT$ muons are less than 1\\\\\
  %. The uncertainty in the calibration of the jet energy scale (JES) directly affects\
  \ the acceptance of the jet multiplicity requirement and the $\\\\pTmiss$ measurement.\
  \ These effects are estimated by shifting the JES in the simulation up and down\
  \ by 1 standard deviation. The uncertainty in the JES is 2\\\\%--5\\\\%, depending\
  \ on the jet $\\\\pT$ and $\\\\eta$~\\\\cite{CMS:2016lmd,CMS-DP-2020-019}. Uncertainties\
  \ in the $b$ tagging algorithm are introduced by various sources~\\\\cite{Sirunyan:2017ezt},\
  \ and the overall impact on the simulated samples is less than 1\\\\%. Theoretical\
  \ uncertainties arising from the choice of the renormalization and factorization\
  \ scales are estimated by varying these scales independently up and down by a factor\
  \ of 2 from their nominal values, excluding the two extreme variations~\\\\cite{Biedermann:2017bss}.\
  \ The largest cross section variations from this procedure are taken as the uncertainty~\\\
  \\cite{Ballestrero:2018anz}, which is about 6\\\\%, and which is applied to both\
  \ the signal and the SM electroweak $\\\\WW$ processes. The parton distribution\
  \ function uncertainty of the signal and the SM electroweak $\\\\WW$ processes is\
  \ evaluated according to the procedure described in Ref.~\\\\cite{PDFLHC}, and is\
  \ found to be about 1\\\\%. These uncertainties are not applied to the subdominant\
  \ $\\\\WZ$ background, where they are not significant compared to other uncertainties\
  \ considered. For the nonprompt-lepton background prediction, systematic uncertainties\
  \ arise from the limited size of the sample used to measure the efficiency and from\
  \ the difference in the flavor composition of the jets that are misidentified as\
  \ leptons between the measured sample and the signal region, estimated to amount\
  \ to at most 5 and 7\\\\%, respectively. An additional normalization uncertainty\
  \ of 30\\\\% is assigned to the nonprompt-lepton background, based on studies of\
  \ simulated events~\\\\cite{CMS:2020dvg}.\\nThe statistical uncertainty in the signal\
  \ and background templates is introduced as a systematic uncertainty via the Barlow-Beeston-lite\
  \ approach~\\\\cite{Barlow:1993dm}. This is the systematic uncertainty that has\
  \ the largest impact on the results derived from the simultaneous fits described\
  \ below. Uncertainties related to pileup, theoretical calculations, and the muon\
  \ trigger and identification are correlated across the three data-taking years.\
  \ The luminosity and $b$ tagging uncertainties are partially correlated through\
  \ some of the individual uncertainty sources, and the remaining uncertainties are\
  \ uncorrelated across the three datasets. The total uncertainties on the results\
  \ are dominated by the statistical uncertainties.\\nTwo separate fits are performed,\
  \ based on the SR and the $b$-tagged, $WZ$, and $WZb$ CRs: one for the heavy Majorana\
  \ neutrino analysis using $\\\\dphill$ bins in the SR, and a second for the Weinberg\
  \ operator analysis with the $\\\\pTmiss$ bins in the SR. The normalization factors\
  \ for the $\\\\WW$, $\\\\WZ$, and $tZq$ background processes, affecting both the\
  \ SRs and CRs, are included as free parameters in the fit together with the signal\
  \ strength. The predicted yields are shown in Fig.~\\\\ref{fig:signal_region} with\
  \ their best fit normalizations from the simultaneous fits for the background-only\
  \ hypothesis, \\\\ie assuming no contributions from processes involving heavy Majorana\
  \ neutrinos and the Weinberg operator. The bin boundaries are chosen to optimize\
  \ the signal sensitivity while leaving the major background contributions in each\
  \ bin at a reasonable level.\\n\\\\begin{figure*}[htb!]\\n\\\\centering\\n\\\\includegraphics[width=1\\\
  \\textwidth]{Figure_002.pdf}\\n\\\\caption{The $\\\\hT/\\\\pT^{\\\\PGm_{1}}$ distribution\
  \ in the SRs and CRs. The horizontal axis indicates the bin width. The predicted\
  \ yields of the backgrounds are shown with their best fit normalizations from the\
  \ simultaneous fits for the background-only hypothesis. The lines indicate the scaled\
  \ expected distributions of the \\\\hmn process with $\\\\mN = 750\\\\GeV$ (solid\
  \ red line), 1.5\\\\TeV (dashed red line), 5.0\\\\TeV (dotted red line), and of\
  \ the \\\\WO process (dash-dotted green line). The \\\\hmn processes are characterized\
  \ by the azimuthal separation variable $\\\\dphill$, while the \\\\WO process features\
  \ in low missing transverse momentum.}\\n\\\\label{fig:signal_region}\\n\\\\end{figure*}\\\
  nThe data are found to be consistent with the background expectation. Using the\
  \ relationship between the cross section and the mixing elements for the \\\\hmn\
  \ analysis, upper limits at the 95\\\\% \\\\CL are derived on $\\\\abs{ \\\\Vmn\
  \ }^{2}$ as shown in Fig.~\\\\ref{fig:upper_limits}. These results surpass those\
  \ obtained in previous searches by the ATLAS and CMS Collaborations~\\\\cite{Sirunyan:2018mtv,Sirunyan:2018xiv,Aad:2019kiz}\
  \ for $\\\\mN \\\\gtrsim 650\\\\GeV$, and set the first direct limits for $\\\\\
  mN > 2 \\\\TeV$. Previous upper limits on the mixing elements from the CMS Collaboration~\\\
  \\cite{Sirunyan:2018mtv,Sirunyan:2018xiv} are plotted in Fig.~\\\\ref{fig:upper_limits}\
  \ for comparison. These limits on $\\\\abs{ \\\\Vmn }^{2}$ approach unity at around\
  \ 1\\\\TeV. As the mixing element describes the oscillation probability between\
  \ the SM neutrinos and the heavy Majorana neutrino, results with $\\\\abs{ \\\\\
  Vmn }^{2} > 1$ are not physically meaningful.\\nEquation~(\\\\ref{eqn:Majorana_N_mass})\
  \ is used to convert the limit on $\\\\abs{\\\\mathrm{C}_5^{\\\\ell\\\\ell'}/\\\\\
  Lambda }^{2}$ extracted from the Weinberg operator analysis into a limit on $\\\\\
  abs{m_{\\\\PGm\\\\PGm}}$. The observed (expected) 95\\\\% \\\\CL upper limit on\
  \ $\\\\abs{m_{\\\\PGm\\\\PGm}}$ is found to be $10.8 ~ (12.8)\\\\GeV$. This is the\
  \ first upper limit from a collider experiment, and it improves upon a previous\
  \ limit set in Ref.~\\\\cite{Fuks:2020zbm} using the results from the NA62 experiment~\\\
  \\cite{NA62:2019eax}.\\n\\\\ifthenelse{\\\\boolean{cms@external}}{\\\\clearpage}{}\\\
  n\\\\begin{figure}[htbp!]\\n\\\\centering\\n\\\\includegraphics[width=0.50\\\\textwidth]{Figure_003.pdf}\\\
  n\\\\caption{Upper limits on the heavy neutrino mixing element $\\\\abs{ \\\\Vmn\
  \ }^{2}$ at the 95\\\\% C.L. as a function of the heavy neutrino mass $\\\\mN$.\
  \ The black dashed curve shows the expected upper limit, with the 1 and 2 standard\
  \ deviation bands are indicated in lime green and light yellow, respectively. The\
  \ solid black curve is the observed upper limit. The red dashed curve indicates\
  \ observed upper limits from Ref.~\\\\cite{Sirunyan:2018mtv}, while the blue dashed\
  \ curve shows the observed upper limits from Ref.~\\\\cite{Sirunyan:2018xiv}. The\
  \ result from Ref.~\\\\cite{Aad:2019kiz} is not shown since it focuses on low $\\\
  \\mN$. Starting from $\\\\mN$ around 650\\\\GeV, the analysis presented in this\
  \ Letter improves upon the upper limits from those references.}\\n\\\\label{fig:upper_limits}\\\
  n\\\\end{figure}\\nIn summary, this Letter presents the first search for Majorana\
  \ neutrinos at several \\\\TeVns{} and a first probe of the Weinberg operator at\
  \ the LHC. These achievements...\"\n}"

result:
  meta:
    title: Probing Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator through VBF at √s
      = 13 TeV
    authors: CMS Collaboration
    audience: High-energy physics conference audience
    one_sentence_takeaway: A CMS search in 138 fb⁻¹ of pp collisions at √s = 13 TeV
      finds no deviation from Standard Model predictions and sets 95% CL constraints
      on same-sign dimuon VBF lepton-number violation through heavy Majorana neutrinos
      and the Weinberg operator.
  core_message: Same-sign μμ production in a VBF topology provides a collider test
    of lepton-number violation in the muon channel; CMS data agree with SM backgrounds,
    yielding limits on |V_{μN}|² for m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV and an observed 95% CL limit
    |m_{μμ}| < 10.8 GeV for the Weinberg-operator interpretation.
  sections:
  - id: 1
    title: 'Physics target: LNV in VBF same-sign dimuons'
    role: motivation
    synopsis: Same-sign W bosons in VBF can probe lepton-number violation through
      either a heavy t-channel Majorana neutrino N or the dimension-five Weinberg
      operator. The final state is two same-sign muons plus two VBF jets, targeting
      a μμ collider channel not accessible to low-energy ee-focused LNV searches.
    key_claims:
    - The search targets LNV in VBF pp processes producing same-sign μμ pairs.
    - 'Heavy Majorana neutrino interpretation: a single heavy state N coupled through
      V_{μN}, scanned over m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV.'
    - 'Weinberg operator: C5^{μμ}/Λ generates an effective μμ Majorana mass m_{μμ}
      = C5^{μμ}v²/Λ.'
    - VBF t-channel production complements other LHC heavy-neutrino searches at TeV-scale
      masses.
    text_budget: title + one-sentence motivation + 4 short bullets + 2 equation chips
    preferred_visual: Two adjacent Feynman diagrams with compact equation chips for
      L_5 and m_{μμ}; use CMS-style particle labels and high-contrast signal coloring.
    visual_keywords:
    - Feynman diagram
    - VBF
    - same-sign W bosons
    - heavy Majorana neutrino
    - Weinberg operator
    - LNV
    - m_{μμ}
    - V_{μN}
  - id: 2
    title: Dataset, objects, and VBF event selection
    role: dataset
    synopsis: The analysis uses CMS pp collision data collected in 2016–2018 at √s
      = 13 TeV, corresponding to 138 fb⁻¹. Events are selected with exactly two same-sign
      muons and at least two high-mass, well-separated VBF jets, with lepton, b-jet,
      and τ vetoes to suppress backgrounds.
    key_claims:
    - 'Dataset: CMS pp collisions at √s = 13 TeV with integrated luminosity 138 fb⁻¹.'
    - 'Triggers: isolated single-muon p_T > 24 or 27 GeV; dimuon triggers improve
      acceptance by up to 4%.'
    - 'Signal-region muons: exactly two same-sign μ with p_T > 30 GeV, |η| < 2.4,
      and m_{μμ} > 20 GeV.'
    - 'VBF jets: at least two jets with p_T > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7; m_{jj} > 750 GeV
      and |Δη_{jj}| > 2.5.'
    - 'VBF topology requirement: max(Z_ℓ) < 0.75; additional loose leptons, hadronic
      τ candidates, and b-tagged jets are vetoed.'
    text_budget: fact badges + 5 compact selection bullets
    preferred_visual: 'Compact HEP selection-flow schematic with concrete thresholds:
      138 fb⁻¹ √s=13 TeV → 2 SS μ → ≥2 VBF jets → topology/vetoes.'
    visual_keywords:
    - 138 fb⁻¹
    - √s = 13 TeV
    - same-sign dimuons
    - p_T > 30 GeV
    - m_{jj} > 750 GeV
    - '|Δη_{jj}| > 2.5'
    - Zeppenfeld variable
    - b veto
  - id: 3
    title: Regions, backgrounds, and fit observables
    role: method
    synopsis: 'Two signal interpretations share the H_T/p_T(μ₁) discriminant but use
      interpretation-specific SR binning: Δφ_{μμ} for heavy Majorana neutrinos and
      p_T^{miss} for the Weinberg operator. A simultaneous fit includes SRs and CRs
      enriched in WZ and nonprompt-lepton backgrounds.'
    key_claims:
    - Heavy Majorana neutrino SRs are split into Δφ_{μμ} > 2 and Δφ_{μμ} < 2 bins.
    - Weinberg-operator SRs are split into p_T^{miss} < 50 GeV and p_T^{miss} > 50
      GeV bins.
    - Control regions include a 3μ WZ CR, a b-tagged CR, and a WZb CR with at least
      one b-tagged jet.
    - Dominant SR backgrounds are SM electroweak W^{±}W^{±} production and nonprompt
      leptons.
    - 'Fit observable: H_T/p_T(μ₁), where H_T is the scalar sum of jet p_T for jets
      with p_T > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7.'
    text_budget: section title + 2 mini-blocks, each with 3–4 bullets
    preferred_visual: Wide post-fit H_T/p_T(μ₁) distribution panel across SR/CR bins,
      plus a small region/fit schematic with paper-specific labels.
    visual_keywords:
