  : \"Create a complete vertical academic conference poster as one finished design.\\\
  n\\nTopic: CMS search for lepton-number violation in same-sign dimuon vector boson\
  \ fusion processes.\\nAudience: high-energy physics conference audience.\\nOverall\
  \ style: premium domain-adaptive scientific conference poster, modern editorial\
  \ design, artistic but readable, not a collage.\\n\\nTITLE SPELLING LOCK:\\n- Render\
  \ the top main title exactly as: \\\"Probing Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg\
  \ operator through VBF at √s = 13 TeV\\\".\\n- Do not paraphrase, abbreviate, or\
  \ visually autocorrect any title word. The word 'for' must be spelled f-o-r, never\
  \ 'fon'.\\n- Keep Greek letters unambiguous in the title; if γ would look like Latin\
  \ y, use clearer glyph spacing rather than a corrupted y.\\n\\nPLACEHOLDER GEOMETRY\
  \ PRIORITY (highest priority; outranks art, symmetry, text density, and decoration):\\\
  n- The visible dashed rectangle for every [FIG NN] placeholder must match its listed\
  \ width/height aspect ratio. This is the most important instruction in the whole\
  \ prompt.\\n- Generation order: first reserve and draw the blank [FIG NN] placeholder\
  \ rectangles as hard geometric anchors on light mats; only then arrange text, flowcharts,\
  \ badges, and decoration around those anchors.\\n- Do not stretch a placeholder\
  \ to fill a card. If a card is too wide, shorten the dashed rectangle or make the\
  \ card taller; compute height = width / listed ratio before rendering.\\n- If a\
  \ placeholder shape conflicts with prose, flowcharts, badges, cards, or background\
  \ art, reconstruct the surrounding text/design: reflow copy into compact legible\
  \ tiers, merge labels, move badges/ornaments, and preserve the information target;\
  \ never distort the placeholder.\\n- The light figure mat/card immediately behind\
  \ a placeholder must support the same shape; do not hide a wrong large card by drawing\
  \ a smaller correct-looking dashed inset.\\n- A generated template with an incorrect\
  \ placeholder shape will be rejected before real-figure insertion.\\n- [FIG 01]:\
  \ width/height ≈ 1.00; aspect \\\"1:1 square\\\"; label \\\"95% CL limits on |VμN|²\
  \ versus mN\\\"; true square; width and height should look equal.\\n- [FIG 02]:\
  \ width/height ≈ 2.50; aspect \\\"2.5:1 wide\\\"; label \\\"Post-fit H_T/p_T(μ1)\
  \ distributions in SRs and CRs\\\"; substantial wide panel with width:height about\
  \ 2.5:1; not 3.5:1, 4:1, or a thin ribbon.\\n- [FIG 03]: width/height ≈ 1.20; aspect\
  \ \\\"1.2:1\\\"; label \\\"VBF heavy Majorana neutrino diagram\\\"; near-square\
  \ panel with width:height about 1.20:1; only slightly wider than tall, not a 1.5:1\
  \ landscape card or banner.\\n- [FIG 04]: width/height ≈ 1.20; aspect \\\"1.2:1\\\
  \"; label \\\"VBF Weinberg-operator diagram\\\"; near-square panel with width:height\
  \ about 1.20:1; only slightly wider than tall, not a 1.5:1 landscape card or banner.\\\
  n- Ruler check before rendering: 2.5:1 is 2.5× wider than tall, so height is 40%\
  \ of its width; 1.22:1 is only slightly wider than tall; 1:1.47 is portrait with\
  \ width about 68% of height; 1:1.99 is portrait with width about 50% of height.\\\
  n- Wide placeholders need enough height to remain readable; portrait placeholders\
  \ need enough vertical space; near-square placeholders must not become banners.\\\
  n\\nPOSITIVE ART DIRECTION:\\n- Art direction: Editorial scientific-magazine design\
  \ with layered abstract geometry and luminous gradients. Use atmospheric depth,\
  \ subtle glow, frosted-glass surfaces, and carefully balanced negative space. Create\
  \ a cover-story feeling: authoritative, beautiful, contemporary, and clearly scientific.\
  \ Let abstract scientific forms sweep across the canvas to connect sections without\
  \ becoming fake data. Use refined typography, micro-shadows, metallic accents, and\
  \ soft depth cues to avoid a PPT-like template. Decorative artwork remains abstract;\
  \ real plots, diagrams, tables, and images appear only in placeholders.\\n- Layout\
  \ rhythm: Editorial scientific-poster rhythm with a strong header and a clear diagonal\
  \ or Z-shaped scan path. Anchor one hero result in the visual center of gravity,\
  \ with supporting method and context modules around it. Use section ribbons, numbered\
  \ tabs, circular callouts, pill headers, wide bands, tall sidebars, and staggered\
  \ panels. Break the grid intentionally while keeping alignment disciplined and readable.\
  \ Vary card proportions and scale so the poster has hierarchy rather than a uniform\
  \ matrix of boxes. Generous gutters and overlapping translucent connector elements\
  \ should create flow without clutter.\\n- Background texture: Soft abstract scientific\
  \ network and field texture behind content cards, kept low contrast and atmospheric.\
  \ Use faint radial gradients, subtle particle trails, ghosted geometric forms, and\
  \ margin-only network hints. Texture should add depth and motion while never reading\
  \ as a plot, table, equation, or data visualization. Keep card interiors calm enough\
  \ for text and placeholders to stay legible. Let color temperature shift gently\
  \ across the poster to support the reading path.\\n- Typography: Modern editorial\
  \ sans-serif system: Helvetica/Inter/Source-Sans-like, with a bold condensed title,\
  \ crisp section headers, compact readable bullets, and restrained scientific notation.\
  \ Use two weights and one accent style rather than many decorative fonts. Create\
  \ hierarchy through scale, weight, color, spacing, and numbered tabs.\\n- Color/material\
  \ palette: Premium HEP palette: deep indigo and graphite margins, CMS-like blue\
  \ accent, muted teal/green for Weinberg-operator elements, warm amber for uncertainty-band\
  \ highlights, and warm-white content cards. Text cards and figure cards remain light\
  \ and calm; dark surfaces are reserved for the header, margins, frames, or accent\
  \ rails.\\n- Figure-card surface: Every scientific figure placeholder sits on a\
  \ warm-white, pearl, or very pale blue paper-like card with subtle shadow and fine\
  \ outline. Plots and Feynman diagrams are never placed on dark navy, black, purple,\
  \ or saturated blocks.\\n- Start from a beautiful editorial composition, not from\
  \ a slide deck or wireframe.\\n- Use abstract, non-data artwork outside placeholders:\
  \ gradients, light trails, field-appropriate geometry, atmospheric glow, soft depth,\
  \ and subtle material texture.\\n- Decorative icons/badges outside placeholders\
  \ must be generic only (stars, checks, arrows, abstract circles). Do not put physics\
  \ symbols, particle labels, equations, ΔL=2, μ/ν/q/W/N, axes, vertices, or event-display\
  \ schematics in decorative badges.\\n- Flowcharts, summary pills, and callout badges\
  \ must not turn scientific shorthand into icons. Use plain words in normal text\
  \ (for example 'dimuon' or 'muon-sector limit'), never standalone μμ/ν/W/N/ΔL/equation\
  \ badges or pictograms.\\n- Give the poster varied visual mass: one dominant hero\
  \ region, secondary supporting modules, small badges, shaped callouts, and breathing\
  \ room.\\n- Section blocks may be rounded rectangles, capsules, circular badges,\
  \ vertical sidebars, L-shaped wraps, staggered panels, or translucent overlays when\
  \ this improves hierarchy.\\n- Keep every scientific figure placeholder itself a\
  \ clean rectangle on a light paper-like figure card, but make the surrounding poster\
  \ expressive and premium.\\n- Use official-looking identity as plain text badges\
  \ only; do not hallucinate complex collaboration or institute logos unless explicitly\
  \ supplied as assets.\\n\\nDOMAIN-ADAPTIVE GUIDANCE (internal design brief; do not\
  \ render this heading):\\n- Detected domain profile: hep\\n- Domain detection summary:\
  \ The paper is a CMS Collaboration search in proton-proton collisions at the CERN\
  \ LHC at sqrt(s)=13 TeV, probing heavy Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator\
  \ via vector boson fusion in same-sign dimuon final states. The excerpt contains\
  \ HEP-specific terminology and methods including integrated luminosity, Feynman\
  \ diagrams, VBF, lepton-number violation, Wilson coefficients, detector reconstr...\\\
  n- Domain text guidance: Prioritize concrete luminosity/energy/channel, object selections,\
  \ SR/CR labels, binning variables, fitted observables, likelihood/CLs strategy,\
  \ floating normalizations, and dominant uncertainties when present.\\n- Detected\
  \ visual grammar: Use a collider-physics visual style with clean axes, compact legends,\
  \ and explicit units such as GeV, TeV, fb^{-1}, and confidence level.; Prioritize\
  \ Feynman diagrams, event-selection flow, signal-versus-background distributions,\
  \ and limit curves over decorative visuals.; Use CMS/LHC-appropriate terminology\
  \ and notation consistently, including pp collisions, sqrt(s), pT, missing transverse\
  \ momentum, same-sign dimuons, VBF jets, and integrated lum...; Distinguish signal\
  \ hypotheses from Standard Model backgrounds with stable, high-contrast colors and\
  \ clear line styles.; When showing constraints, emphasize log-scale axes where appropriate\
  \ for masses, cross sections, or mixing elements..\\n- Detected layout priorities:\
  \ Lead with the physics question: lepton-number violation, Majorana neutrinos, and\
  \ collider tests of the Weinberg operator.; Place the Feynman diagrams near the\
  \ motivation section to make the signal topology immediately understandable.; Use\
  \ a central results panel for observed/expected limits and the key quantitative\
  \ outcome stated in the abstract.; Separate detector/data, event selection, backgrounds,\
  \ and statistical interpretation into concise blocks.; Reserve space for collision\
  \ energy and luminosity, since sqrt(s)=13 TeV and 138 fb^{-1} are essential context.;\
  \ Use equation snippets sparingly, highlighting only the Weinberg operator, Majorana\
  \ mass relation, and scaling of relevant couplings if needed..\\n- Detected text\
  \ priorities: State that the analysis uses CMS pp collision data at sqrt(s)=13 TeV\
  \ corresponding to 138 fb^{-1}.; Identify the final state as same-sign dimuons in\
  \ vector boson fusion processes.; Explain that the search targets lepton-number\
  \ violation through heavy Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator.; Report\
  \ only grounded results: agreement with Standard Model predictions, constraints\
  \ on the muon-heavy-neutrino mixing element over 50 GeV to 25 TeV, and the 95% CL\
  \ observed upp...; Define specialized quantities such as V_{mu N}, m_N, C5/Lambda,\
  \ and m_{mumu} when used.; Use concise language for backgrounds and simulation,\
  \ avoiding excessive generator details unless they support the poster narrative..\\\
  n- HEP notation legibility: Greek gamma must look like γ, never Latin y; if a compact\
  \ label risks glyph ambiguity, use the word gamma.\\n\\nNARRATIVE STORYBOARD (internal\
  \ design brief; do not render this heading or the word storyboard):\\n- Core message\
  \ to make visually obvious: Same-sign dimuon production in a VBF topology provides\
  \ a collider test of lepton-number violation in the muon channel; CMS data agree\
  \ with SM backgrounds, yielding limits on muon-heavy-neutrino mixing squared for\
  \ m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV and an observed 95% CL limit |m_{dimuon}| < 10.8 GeV for the\
  \ Weinberg-operator interpretation.\\n- Reading order should follow section ids:\
  \ 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.\\n- Hero section id: 4; hero visual role: Observed and expected\
  \ 95% CL |V_{μN}|² limit curve versus m_N, paired with a prominent Weinberg-operator\
  \ |m_{μμ}| limit callout..\\n- Layout intent: Lead with the LNV physics question\
  \ and Feynman diagrams, anchor the upper-right with dataset and concrete VBF selection,\
  \ use the middle band for region/fit strategy and post-fit distributions, then center\
  \ the poster on the limit results and close with scope and interpretation.\\n- Section\
  \ 1: role=motivation; text budget=title + one-sentence motivation + 4 short bullets\
  \ + 2 equation chips; preferred visual=Two adjacent Feynman diagrams with compact\
  \ equation chips for L_5 and m_{dimuon}; use CMS-style particle labels and high-contrast\
  \ signal coloring.; key claims=The search targets LNV in VBF pp processes producing\
  \ same-sign dimuon pairs.; Heavy Majorana neutrino interpretation: a single heavy\
  \ state N coupled through V_{μN}, scanned over m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV.; Weinberg operator:\
  \ C5^{dimuon}/Λ generates an effective dimuon Majorana mass m_{dimuon} = C5^{dimuon}v²/Λ.\\\
  n- Section 2: role=dataset; text budget=fact badges + 5 compact selection bullets;\
  \ preferred visual=Compact HEP selection-flow schematic with concrete thresholds:\
  \ 138 fb⁻¹ √s=13 TeV → 2 SS μ → ≥2 VBF jets → topology/vetoes.; key claims=Dataset:\
  \ CMS pp collisions at √s = 13 TeV with integrated luminosity 138 fb⁻¹.; Triggers:\
  \ isolated single-muon p_T > 24 or 27 GeV; dimuon triggers improve acceptance by\
  \ up to 4%.; Signal-region muons: exactly two same-sign μ with p_T > 30 GeV, |η|\
  \ < 2.4, and m_{dimuon} > 20 GeV.\\n- Section 3: role=method; text budget=section\
  \ title + 2 mini-blocks, each with 3–4 bullets; preferred visual=Wide post-fit H_T/p_T(μ₁)\
  \ distribution panel across SR/CR bins, plus a small region/fit schematic with paper-specific\
  \ labels.; key claims=Heavy Majorana neutrino SRs are split into Δφ_{dimuon} > 2\
  \ and Δφ_{dimuon} < 2 bins.; Weinberg-operator SRs are split into p_T^{miss} < 50\
  \ GeV and p_T^{miss} > 50 GeV bins.; Control regions include a 3μ WZ CR, a b-tagged\
  \ CR, and a WZb CR with at least one b-tagged jet.\\n- Section 4: role=result; text\
  \ budget=large result callout + 4 bullets + one small Weinberg result badge; preferred\
  \ visual=Hero square limit plot: observed and expected 95% CL upper limits on muon-heavy-neutrino\
  \ mixing squared vs m_N, with uncertainty bands and previous CMS comparison curves;\
  \ include log-scale axes if shown in source figure.; key claims=No deviation from\
  \ Standard Model expectations is observed.; Heavy-neutrino limits constrain muon-heavy-neutrino\
  \ mixing squared over m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV.; For m_N ≳ 650 GeV, the constraints are\
  \ reported as the most stringent from LHC searches to date in the paper.\\n- Section\
  \ 5: role=interpretation; text budget=one-sentence takeaway + 4 compact scope bullets;\
  \ preferred visual=Summary strip with definition cards for V_{μN}, m_N, C5^{dimuon}/Λ,\
  \ and m_{dimuon}; no new quantitative plots.; key claims=The search finds agreement\
  \ with SM predictions, not discovery or evidence of LNV.; Heavy-neutrino interpretation\
  \ assumes one heavy state coupled through V_{μN}.; The heavy-neutrino mass scan\
  \ is limited to m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV.\\n- Use this storyboard only to guide hierarchy,\
  \ reading path, and text compression; render only the public section text specified\
  \ below.\\n- Storyboard science terms are semantic guidance only: never render them\
  \ as standalone icons, circular badges, particle-symbol marks, fake diagrams, or\
  \ flowchart pictograms outside [FIG NN] placeholders.\\n\\nINFORMATION DENSITY TARGET:\\\
  n- Target: Paper2Poster-rich editorial density: 14-24 concise public information\
  \ units across the poster, 3-6 grounded fact badges, 4-6 section modules, and one\
  \ compact conclusion strip. Prefer short claims and fact chips over paragraphs;\
  \ reconstruct lower-priority facts into compact legible chips before changing placeholder\
  \ geometry..\\n- Do not make the poster a sparse cover illustration. It should communicate\
  \ enough public content for a conference viewer to understand the paper's motivation,\
  \ method, key figures, and conclusion.\\n- Prefer compact information architecture:\
  \ 4-6 section modules, 18-30 total short bullets/fact chips, 4-8 small badges, and\
  \ a concise conclusion strip.\\n- Keep the current generous whitespace/gutters;\
  \ increase information density with smaller text tiers and shorter copy, not by\
  \ flattening the layout or shrinking placeholders.\\n- Keep public facts legible\
  \ and truthful. If the image model cannot fit a fact clearly, rewrite it as a shorter\
  \ public chip or move it to a smaller but legible text tier; never use unreadable\
  \ text or invented abbreviations.\\n- Numeric badges are allowed only for numbers\
  \ explicitly present in the supplied public text/assets; never invent luminosities,\
  \ energies, masses, limits, years, or confidence levels.\\n- Use figure placeholders\
  \ as information anchors: each figure card should have a short nearby public headline\
  \ explaining why the future real figure matters, without describing fake drawn contents.\\\
  n- Candidate public data/fact badges to render when space allows:\\n  • √s = 13\
  \ TeV\\n  • 138 fb⁻¹\\n  • CMS 2016–2018\\n  • same-sign dimuon + VBF jets\\n  •\
  \ m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV\\n  • 95% CL\\n  • observed |m_{dimuon}| < 10.8 GeV\\n  •\
  \ expected |m_{dimuon}| < 12.8 GeV\\n- Candidate high-value public facts/claims\
  \ to distribute across modules:\\n  • Final state: exactly two same-sign μ plus\
  \ at least two VBF jets.\\n  • Muon selection: p_T > 30 GeV and |η| < 2.4.\\n  •\
  \ Jet selection: p_T > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7.\\n  • VBF topology: m_{jj} > 750 GeV,\
  \ |Δη_{jj}| > 2.5, max(Z_ℓ) < 0.75.\\n  • HMN SR split: Δφ_{dimuon} > 2 and Δφ_{dimuon}\
  \ < 2.\\n  • Weinberg SR split: p_T^{miss} < 50 GeV and p_T^{miss} > 50 GeV.\\n\
  \  • Fit observable: H_T/p_T(μ₁).\\n  • Dominant SR backgrounds: SM electroweak\
  \ W^{±}W^{±} and nonprompt leptons.\\n  • Statistical method: profile likelihood\
  \ with constrained nuisance parameters; modified frequentist CL_s with asymptotic\
  \ approximation.\\n  • Data agree with SM predictions.\\n- Visual story units to\
  \ make obvious through hierarchy, not fake scientific drawings:\\n  • Side-by-side\
  \ Feynman diagrams: heavy N vs Weinberg operator VBF LNV.\\n  • Selection thresholds\
  \ as concrete badges and a compact region-flow schematic.\\n  • Post-fit H_T/p_T(μ₁)\
  \ distribution showing data-background agreement and signal hypotheses.\\n  • Observed/expected\
  \ muon-heavy-neutrino mixing squared limit curve vs m_N with uncertainty bands.\\\
  n  • Definition/scope strip clarifying V_{μN}, m_N, C5^{dimuon}/Λ, m_{dimuon}, and\
  \ dimuon collider context.\\n- A viewer should be able to answer these from the\
  \ final poster; use them to prioritize content, not as rendered questions:\\n  •\
  \ What lepton-number-violating processes are tested in the same-sign dimuon VBF\
  \ channel?\\n  • What CMS dataset, collision energy, and integrated luminosity are\
  \ used?\\n  • What object and VBF topology requirements define the signal region?\\\
  n  • How do the heavy-neutrino and Weinberg-operator SR binnings differ?\\n  • Which\
  \ backgrounds dominate, and how are control regions used?\\n  • What discriminant\
  \ and statistical method are used to set limits?\\n\\nPHYSICS QUIZ COVERAGE TARGET\
  \ (internal; do not render this heading, Q IDs, questions, or answers verbatim unless\
  \ also present in COPY DECK):\\n- These questions define what a viewer should be\
  \ able to understand after reading the poster.\\n- Use them to prioritize public\
  \ copy and figure hierarchy. Do not draw quiz cards, exam questions, answer keys,\
  \ or Q-number labels.\\n- priority=must, aspect=physics_motivation: viewer question\
  \ \\\"What lepton-number-violating mechanisms are tested in the VBF same-sign dimuon\
  \ channel?\\\"; expected answer target \\\"Heavy Majorana neutrino exchange and\
  \ the dimension-five Weinberg operator.\\\".\\n- priority=must, aspect=signal_topology:\
  \ viewer question \\\"What final state defines the core collider signature of the\
  \ search?\\\"; expected answer target \\\"Two same-sign muons plus at least two\
  \ VBF jets in pp collisions.\\\".\\n- priority=must, aspect=dataset_channel: viewer\
  \ question \\\"What collision energy and integrated luminosity are used?\\\"; expected\
  \ answer target \\\"CMS pp collision data at √s = 13 TeV corresponding to 138 fb⁻¹,\
  \ collected during 2016–2018.\\\".\\n- priority=should, aspect=trigger_and_acceptance:\
  \ viewer question \\\"Which triggers are used, and what acceptance gain do dimuon\
  \ triggers provide?\\\"; expected answer target \\\"Single-muon triggers requiring\
  \ isolated muons with pT > 24 or 27 GeV are used; dimuon triggers improve event\
  \ acceptance by up to 4%.\\\".\\n- priority=must, aspect=object_selection: viewer\
  \ question \\\"What are the signal-region muon requirements?\\\"; expected answer\
  \ target \\\"Exactly two same-sign muons with pT > 30 GeV and |η| < 2.4; the SR\
  \ also requires mdimuon > 20 GeV.\\\".\\n- priority=must, aspect=vbf_selection:\
  \ viewer question \\\"Which VBF jet and topology requirements define the signal\
  \ region?\\\"; expected answer target \\\"At least two jets with pT > 30 GeV and\
  \ |η| < 4.7; VBF candidates must satisfy mjj > 750 GeV, |Δηjj| > 2.5, and max(Zℓ)\
  \ < 0.75.\\\".\\n- priority=must, aspect=region_definitions: viewer question \\\"\
  How are the signal regions split for the two interpretations?\\\"; expected answer\
  \ target \\\"The heavy Majorana neutrino SR is split by Δφdimuon > 2 and Δφdimuon\
  \ < 2; the Weinberg-operator SR is split by pTmiss < 50 GeV and pTmiss > 50 GeV.\\\
  \".\\n- priority=must, aspect=backgrounds_and_control_regions: viewer question \\\
  \"Which backgrounds dominate the SR, and which control regions help constrain reducible\
  \ backgrounds?\\\"; expected answer target \\\"Dominant SR backgrounds are SM electroweak\
  \ W±W± production and nonprompt leptons; WZ, b-tagged, and WZb control regions constrain\
  \ reducible backgrounds.\\\".\\n- priority=must, aspect=fit_observable: viewer question\
  \ \\\"What discriminating variable is fitted in the SRs and CRs, and what does it\
  \ measure?\\\"; expected answer target \\\"The fitted discriminant is HT/pT(μ1),\
  \ measuring hadronic activity relative to the leading muon pT; HT is the scalar\
  \ sum of jet pT for jets with pT > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7.\\\".\\n- priority=must,\
  \ aspect=statistical_interpretation: viewer question \\\"Which statistical method\
  \ is used to set limits?\\\"; expected answer target \\\"Limits are set using a\
  \ profile-likelihood ratio test statistic with constrained nuisance parameters and\
  \ the modified frequentist CLs criterion with asymptotic approximation.\\\".\\n-\
  \ priority=must, aspect=heavy_neutrino_result: viewer question \\\"What does the\
  \ analysis conclude for the heavy Majorana neutrino mixing element muon-heavy-neutrino\

  \ scientific notation. Use two weights and one accent style rather than many decorative\
  \ fonts. Create hierarchy through scale, weight, color, spacing, and numbered tabs.\"\
  ,\n      \"color_palette\": \"Premium HEP palette: deep indigo and graphite margins,\
  \ CMS-like blue accent, muted teal/green for Weinberg-operator elements, warm amber\
  \ for uncertainty-band highlights, and warm-white content cards. Text cards and\
  \ figure cards remain light and calm; dark surfaces are reserved for the header,\
  \ margins, frames, or accent rails.\",\n      \"figure_surface\": \"Every scientific\
  \ figure placeholder sits on a warm-white, pearl, or very pale blue paper-like card\
  \ with subtle shadow and fine outline. Plots and Feynman diagrams are never placed\
  \ on dark navy, black, purple, or saturated blocks.\",\n      \"art_direction\"\
  : \"Editorial scientific-magazine design with layered abstract geometry and luminous\
  \ gradients. Use atmospheric depth, subtle glow, frosted-glass surfaces, and carefully\
  \ balanced negative space. Create a cover-story feeling: authoritative, beautiful,\
  \ contemporary, and clearly scientific. Let abstract scientific forms sweep across\
  \ the canvas to connect sections without becoming fake data. Use refined typography,\
  \ micro-shadows, metallic accents, and soft depth cues to avoid a PPT-like template.\
  \ Decorative artwork remains abstract; real plots, diagrams, tables, and images\
  \ appear only in placeholders.\",\n      \"layout_rhythm\": \"Editorial scientific-poster\
  \ rhythm with a strong header and a clear diagonal or Z-shaped scan path. Anchor\
  \ one hero result in the visual center of gravity, with supporting method and context\
  \ modules around it. Use section ribbons, numbered tabs, circular callouts, pill\
  \ headers, wide bands, tall sidebars, and staggered panels. Break the grid intentionally\
  \ while keeping alignment disciplined and readable. Vary card proportions and scale\
  \ so the poster has hierarchy rather than a uniform matrix of boxes. Generous gutters\
  \ and overlapping translucent connector elements should create flow without clutter.\"\
  ,\n      \"background_texture\": \"Soft abstract scientific network and field texture\
  \ behind content cards, kept low contrast and atmospheric. Use faint radial gradients,\
  \ subtle particle trails, ghosted geometric forms, and margin-only network hints.\
  \ Texture should add depth and motion while never reading as a plot, table, equation,\
  \ or data visualization. Keep card interiors calm enough for text and placeholders\
  \ to stay legible. Let color temperature shift gently across the poster to support\
  \ the reading path.\",\n      \"information_density\": \"Paper2Poster-rich editorial\
  \ density: 14-24 concise public information units across the poster, 3-6 grounded\
  \ fact badges, 4-6 section modules, and one compact conclusion strip. Prefer short\
  \ claims and fact chips over paragraphs; reconstruct lower-priority facts into compact\
  \ legible chips before changing placeholder geometry.\",\n      \"domain_label\"\
  : \"high_energy_physics\",\n      \"domain_grammar_heading\": \"HEP POSTER DESIGN\
  \ GRAMMAR\",\n      \"domain_poster_grammar\": [\n        \"Use a CERN/LHCC-style\

  \ key result → interpretation/summary.\",\n        \"Use colored section ribbons\
  \ or numbered tabs so the viewer can scan the poster from 2 meters away.\",\n  \
  \      \"Create one dominant hero region for the headline result; do not divide\
  \ the body into many equal tiny boxes.\",\n        \"Cards/blocks do not need to\
  \ be square: use wide bands, tall sidebars, pill headers, circular callouts, curved\
  \ connectors, and staggered panels when it improves hierarchy.\",\n        \"Let\
  \ 40-55% of the body be reserved for figure placeholders; HEP posters are figure-led,\
  \ not paragraph-led.\",\n        \"Use small badges for dataset, collision energy,\
  \ luminosity, channel, or experiment only when present in the supplied text; never\

  \ the largest placeholder to the main result/limit/cross-section/significance plot.\"\

  : \"Create a complete vertical academic conference poster as one finished design.\\\
  n\\nTopic: CMS search for lepton-number violation in same-sign dimuon vector boson\
  \ fusion processes.\\nAudience: high-energy physics conference audience.\\nOverall\
  \ style: premium domain-adaptive scientific conference poster, modern editorial\
  \ design, artistic but readable, not a collage.\\n\\nTITLE SPELLING LOCK:\\n- Render\
  \ the top main title exactly as: \\\"Probing Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg\
  \ operator through VBF at √s = 13 TeV\\\".\\n- Do not paraphrase, abbreviate, or\
  \ visually autocorrect any title word. The word 'for' must be spelled f-o-r, never\
  \ 'fon'.\\n- Keep Greek letters unambiguous in the title; if γ would look like Latin\
  \ y, use clearer glyph spacing rather than a corrupted y.\\n\\nPLACEHOLDER GEOMETRY\
  \ PRIORITY (highest priority; outranks art, symmetry, text density, and decoration):\\\
  n- The visible dashed rectangle for every [FIG NN] placeholder must match its listed\
  \ width/height aspect ratio. This is the most important instruction in the whole\
  \ prompt.\\n- Generation order: first reserve and draw the blank [FIG NN] placeholder\
  \ rectangles as hard geometric anchors on light mats; only then arrange text, flowcharts,\
  \ badges, and decoration around those anchors.\\n- Do not stretch a placeholder\
  \ to fill a card. If a card is too wide, shorten the dashed rectangle or make the\
  \ card taller; compute height = width / listed ratio before rendering.\\n- If a\
  \ placeholder shape conflicts with prose, flowcharts, badges, cards, or background\
  \ art, reconstruct the surrounding text/design: reflow copy into compact legible\
  \ tiers, merge labels, move badges/ornaments, and preserve the information target;\
  \ never distort the placeholder.\\n- The light figure mat/card immediately behind\
  \ a placeholder must support the same shape; do not hide a wrong large card by drawing\
  \ a smaller correct-looking dashed inset.\\n- A generated template with an incorrect\
  \ placeholder shape will be rejected before real-figure insertion.\\n- [FIG 01]:\
  \ width/height ≈ 1.00; aspect \\\"1:1 square\\\"; label \\\"95% CL limits on |VμN|²\
  \ versus mN\\\"; true square; width and height should look equal.\\n- [FIG 02]:\
  \ width/height ≈ 2.50; aspect \\\"2.5:1 wide\\\"; label \\\"Post-fit H_T/p_T(μ1)\
  \ distributions in SRs and CRs\\\"; substantial wide panel with width:height about\
  \ 2.5:1; not 3.5:1, 4:1, or a thin ribbon.\\n- [FIG 03]: width/height ≈ 1.20; aspect\
  \ \\\"1.2:1\\\"; label \\\"VBF heavy Majorana neutrino diagram\\\"; near-square\
  \ panel with width:height about 1.20:1; only slightly wider than tall, not a 1.5:1\
  \ landscape card or banner.\\n- [FIG 04]: width/height ≈ 1.20; aspect \\\"1.2:1\\\
  \"; label \\\"VBF Weinberg-operator diagram\\\"; near-square panel with width:height\
  \ about 1.20:1; only slightly wider than tall, not a 1.5:1 landscape card or banner.\\\
  n- Ruler check before rendering: 2.5:1 is 2.5× wider than tall, so height is 40%\
  \ of its width; 1.22:1 is only slightly wider than tall; 1:1.47 is portrait with\
  \ width about 68% of height; 1:1.99 is portrait with width about 50% of height.\\\
  n- Wide placeholders need enough height to remain readable; portrait placeholders\
  \ need enough vertical space; near-square placeholders must not become banners.\\\
  n\\nPOSITIVE ART DIRECTION:\\n- Art direction: Editorial scientific-magazine design\
  \ with layered abstract geometry and luminous gradients. Use atmospheric depth,\
  \ subtle glow, frosted-glass surfaces, and carefully balanced negative space. Create\
  \ a cover-story feeling: authoritative, beautiful, contemporary, and clearly scientific.\
  \ Let abstract scientific forms sweep across the canvas to connect sections without\
  \ becoming fake data. Use refined typography, micro-shadows, metallic accents, and\
  \ soft depth cues to avoid a PPT-like template. Decorative artwork remains abstract;\
  \ real plots, diagrams, tables, and images appear only in placeholders.\\n- Layout\
  \ rhythm: Editorial scientific-poster rhythm with a strong header and a clear diagonal\
  \ or Z-shaped scan path. Anchor one hero result in the visual center of gravity,\
  \ with supporting method and context modules around it. Use section ribbons, numbered\
  \ tabs, circular callouts, pill headers, wide bands, tall sidebars, and staggered\
  \ panels. Break the grid intentionally while keeping alignment disciplined and readable.\
  \ Vary card proportions and scale so the poster has hierarchy rather than a uniform\
  \ matrix of boxes. Generous gutters and overlapping translucent connector elements\
  \ should create flow without clutter.\\n- Background texture: Soft abstract scientific\
  \ network and field texture behind content cards, kept low contrast and atmospheric.\
  \ Use faint radial gradients, subtle particle trails, ghosted geometric forms, and\
  \ margin-only network hints. Texture should add depth and motion while never reading\
  \ as a plot, table, equation, or data visualization. Keep card interiors calm enough\
  \ for text and placeholders to stay legible. Let color temperature shift gently\
  \ across the poster to support the reading path.\\n- Typography: Modern editorial\
  \ sans-serif system: Helvetica/Inter/Source-Sans-like, with a bold condensed title,\
  \ crisp section headers, compact readable bullets, and restrained scientific notation.\
  \ Use two weights and one accent style rather than many decorative fonts. Create\
  \ hierarchy through scale, weight, color, spacing, and numbered tabs.\\n- Color/material\
  \ palette: Premium HEP palette: deep indigo and graphite margins, CMS-like blue\
  \ accent, muted teal/green for Weinberg-operator elements, warm amber for uncertainty-band\
  \ highlights, and warm-white content cards. Text cards and figure cards remain light\
  \ and calm; dark surfaces are reserved for the header, margins, frames, or accent\
  \ rails.\\n- Figure-card surface: Every scientific figure placeholder sits on a\
  \ warm-white, pearl, or very pale blue paper-like card with subtle shadow and fine\
  \ outline. Plots and Feynman diagrams are never placed on dark navy, black, purple,\
  \ or saturated blocks.\\n- Start from a beautiful editorial composition, not from\
  \ a slide deck or wireframe.\\n- Use abstract, non-data artwork outside placeholders:\
  \ gradients, light trails, field-appropriate geometry, atmospheric glow, soft depth,\
  \ and subtle material texture.\\n- Decorative icons/badges outside placeholders\
  \ must be generic only (stars, checks, arrows, abstract circles). Do not put physics\
  \ symbols, particle labels, equations, ΔL=2, μ/ν/q/W/N, axes, vertices, or event-display\
  \ schematics in decorative badges.\\n- Flowcharts, summary pills, and callout badges\
  \ must not turn scientific shorthand into icons. Use plain words in normal text\
  \ (for example 'dimuon' or 'muon-sector limit'), never standalone μμ/ν/W/N/ΔL/equation\
  \ badges or pictograms.\\n- Give the poster varied visual mass: one dominant hero\
  \ region, secondary supporting modules, small badges, shaped callouts, and breathing\
  \ room.\\n- Section blocks may be rounded rectangles, capsules, circular badges,\
  \ vertical sidebars, L-shaped wraps, staggered panels, or translucent overlays when\
  \ this improves hierarchy.\\n- Keep every scientific figure placeholder itself a\
  \ clean rectangle on a light paper-like figure card, but make the surrounding poster\
  \ expressive and premium.\\n- Use official-looking identity as plain text badges\
  \ only; do not hallucinate complex collaboration or institute logos unless explicitly\
  \ supplied as assets.\\n\\nDOMAIN-ADAPTIVE GUIDANCE (internal design brief; do not\
  \ render this heading):\\n- Detected domain profile: hep\\n- Domain detection summary:\
  \ The paper is a CMS Collaboration search in proton-proton collisions at the CERN\
  \ LHC at sqrt(s)=13 TeV, probing heavy Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator\
  \ via vector boson fusion in same-sign dimuon final states. The excerpt contains\
  \ HEP-specific terminology and methods including integrated luminosity, Feynman\
  \ diagrams, VBF, lepton-number violation, Wilson coefficients, detector reconstr...\\\
  n- Domain text guidance: Prioritize concrete luminosity/energy/channel, object selections,\
  \ SR/CR labels, binning variables, fitted observables, likelihood/CLs strategy,\
  \ floating normalizations, and dominant uncertainties when present.\\n- Detected\
  \ visual grammar: Use a collider-physics visual style with clean axes, compact legends,\
  \ and explicit units such as GeV, TeV, fb^{-1}, and confidence level.; Prioritize\
  \ Feynman diagrams, event-selection flow, signal-versus-background distributions,\
  \ and limit curves over decorative visuals.; Use CMS/LHC-appropriate terminology\
  \ and notation consistently, including pp collisions, sqrt(s), pT, missing transverse\
  \ momentum, same-sign dimuons, VBF jets, and integrated lum...; Distinguish signal\
  \ hypotheses from Standard Model backgrounds with stable, high-contrast colors and\
  \ clear line styles.; When showing constraints, emphasize log-scale axes where appropriate\
  \ for masses, cross sections, or mixing elements..\\n- Detected layout priorities:\
  \ Lead with the physics question: lepton-number violation, Majorana neutrinos, and\
  \ collider tests of the Weinberg operator.; Place the Feynman diagrams near the\
  \ motivation section to make the signal topology immediately understandable.; Use\
  \ a central results panel for observed/expected limits and the key quantitative\
  \ outcome stated in the abstract.; Separate detector/data, event selection, backgrounds,\
  \ and statistical interpretation into concise blocks.; Reserve space for collision\
  \ energy and luminosity, since sqrt(s)=13 TeV and 138 fb^{-1} are essential context.;\
  \ Use equation snippets sparingly, highlighting only the Weinberg operator, Majorana\
  \ mass relation, and scaling of relevant couplings if needed..\\n- Detected text\
  \ priorities: State that the analysis uses CMS pp collision data at sqrt(s)=13 TeV\
  \ corresponding to 138 fb^{-1}.; Identify the final state as same-sign dimuons in\
  \ vector boson fusion processes.; Explain that the search targets lepton-number\
  \ violation through heavy Majorana neutrinos and the Weinberg operator.; Report\
  \ only grounded results: agreement with Standard Model predictions, constraints\
  \ on the muon-heavy-neutrino mixing element over 50 GeV to 25 TeV, and the 95% CL\
  \ observed upp...; Define specialized quantities such as V_{mu N}, m_N, C5/Lambda,\
  \ and m_{mumu} when used.; Use concise language for backgrounds and simulation,\
  \ avoiding excessive generator details unless they support the poster narrative..\\\
  n- HEP notation legibility: Greek gamma must look like γ, never Latin y; if a compact\
  \ label risks glyph ambiguity, use the word gamma.\\n\\nNARRATIVE STORYBOARD (internal\
  \ design brief; do not render this heading or the word storyboard):\\n- Core message\
  \ to make visually obvious: Same-sign dimuon production in a VBF topology provides\
  \ a collider test of lepton-number violation in the muon channel; CMS data agree\
  \ with SM backgrounds, yielding limits on muon-heavy-neutrino mixing squared for\
  \ m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV and an observed 95% CL limit |m_{dimuon}| < 10.8 GeV for the\
  \ Weinberg-operator interpretation.\\n- Reading order should follow section ids:\
  \ 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.\\n- Hero section id: 4; hero visual role: Observed and expected\
  \ 95% CL |V_{μN}|² limit curve versus m_N, paired with a prominent Weinberg-operator\
  \ |m_{μμ}| limit callout..\\n- Layout intent: Lead with the LNV physics question\
  \ and Feynman diagrams, anchor the upper-right with dataset and concrete VBF selection,\
  \ use the middle band for region/fit strategy and post-fit distributions, then center\
  \ the poster on the limit results and close with scope and interpretation.\\n- Section\
  \ 1: role=motivation; text budget=title + one-sentence motivation + 4 short bullets\
  \ + 2 equation chips; preferred visual=Two adjacent Feynman diagrams with compact\
  \ equation chips for L_5 and m_{dimuon}; use CMS-style particle labels and high-contrast\
  \ signal coloring.; key claims=The search targets LNV in VBF pp processes producing\
  \ same-sign dimuon pairs.; Heavy Majorana neutrino interpretation: a single heavy\
  \ state N coupled through V_{μN}, scanned over m_N = 50 GeV–25 TeV.; Weinberg operator:\
  \ C5^{dimuon}/Λ generates an effective dimuon Majorana mass m_{dimuon} = C5^{dimuon}v²/Λ.\\\
  n- Section 2: role=dataset; text budget=fact badges + 5 compact selection bullets;\
  \ preferred visual=Compact HEP selection-flow schematic with concrete thresholds:\
  \ 138 fb⁻¹ √s=13 TeV → 2 SS μ → ≥2 VBF jets → topology/vetoes.; key claims=Dataset:\

  n\\nHEP POSTER DESIGN GRAMMAR:\\n- Use a CERN/LHCC-style scientific story spine:\
  \ motivation → dataset/selection → strategy/background → key result → interpretation/summary.\\\
  n- Use colored section ribbons or numbered tabs so the viewer can scan the poster\
  \ from 2 meters away.\\n- Create one dominant hero region for the headline result;\
  \ do not divide the body into many equal tiny boxes.\\n- Cards/blocks do not need\
  \ to be square: use wide bands, tall sidebars, pill headers, circular callouts,\
  \ curved connectors, and staggered panels when it improves hierarchy.\\n- Let 40-55%\
  \ of the body be reserved for figure placeholders; HEP posters are figure-led, not\
  \ paragraph-led.\\n- Use small badges for dataset, collision energy, luminosity,\
  \ channel, or experiment only when present in the supplied text; never invent numbers.\\\
  n\\nTEXT DENSITY AND READABILITY:\\n- Compress prose into poster bullets: short\
  \ noun phrases, ideally under 11 words each.\\n- Maintain Paper2Poster-style information\
  \ richness through smaller but still legible text tiers, not by removing whitespace\
  \ or shrinking figure placeholders.\\n- Use three text scales: large must-level\
  \ claims, compact body bullets for specialist detail, and micro-badges for optional\
  \ should/could facts.\\n- Preserve the current generous editorial whitespace; add\
  \ information by making copy shorter and typesetting secondary facts smaller, not\
  \ by packing cards edge-to-edge.\\n- Avoid microscopic paragraphs, footnote blocks,\
  \ dense equations, and reference lists in the rendered poster.\\n- Prefer 2-5 bullets/fact\
  \ chips per non-hero card and at most one short sentence per text block; preserve\
  \ meaning without adding new science.\\n- Use public fact chips and numeric badges\
  \ for explicitly grounded dataset/result facts; do not invent numbers.\\n- If text\
  \ competes with a result figure, reconstruct the text layout: split it into shorter\
  \ legible chips/sidebars and preserve the information target while enlarging/preserving\
  \ the figure placeholder.\\n\\nFIGURE-LED COMPOSITION:\\n- Allocate the largest\
  \ placeholder to the main result/limit/cross-section/significance plot.\\n- Every\

  \ and strategy cards should show analysis-specific SR/CR, fit, and uncertainty details\
  \ rather than a generic data-processing pipeline.\\n- All figure-containing cards\
  \ must use a light paper/lab-white surface around the placeholder; dark or saturated\
  \ fills may be outer accents only.\\n\\nFIGURE CARD SURFACE POLICY (mandatory for\
  \ visual integration):\\n- Mandatory: every [FIG NN] placeholder sits inside a light\

  \ actual result card interior light.\\n- For multi-figure sections, use a shared\

  \ or near-solid light fill inside any chart/plot/diagram block.\\n\\nTYPOGRAPHY\

  \ item. Draw a blank placeholder only.\\n- Every location where a plot/diagram/table/image\
  \ should go must be a clean rectangular placeholder panel.\\n- Use ONLY the placeholder\
  \ IDs explicitly listed in this prompt. Do not invent, add, skip ahead to, or render\
  \ any extra placeholder such as [FIG 06] unless it is listed in the PLACEHOLDER\
  \ REFERENCE LIST.\\n- Each placeholder panel must contain ONLY three text elements:\
  \ the exact ID such as [FIG 01], the intended content label, and the requested aspect\
  \ ratio.\\n- Placeholder IDs [FIG 01], [FIG 02], etc. must be large, legible, and\
  \ visually centered or top-left inside the box.\\n- Placeholder boxes must be light\
  \ neutral panels with dashed borders or subtle tint; inside must remain empty except\
  \ the required ID/label/aspect text.\\n- The whole figure-containing block/card\
  \ behind each placeholder must also be light neutral or paper-like. Do not put a\
  \ chart placeholder inside a dark navy, purple, black, or saturated card.\\n- Placeholder\
  \ geometry is audited after generation. A box labeled 1:1 must be visibly square;\
  \ a box labeled 2.5:1 must be about 2.5 times wider than tall.\\n- A box labeled\
  \ 1.2:1 must be near-square: only about 20% wider than tall. Do not draw it as a\
  \ generic 1.5:1 landscape card.\\n- Do not draw a generic 1.6:1 landscape rectangle\
  \ for every placeholder. Each placeholder must use its own declared ratio.\\n- Rejected\
  \ geometry examples: a 2.5:1 plot as a 950×90 ribbon, a 1:1 result as a 300×190\
  \ landscape card, or any placeholder whose text cluster is detected instead of the\
  \ whole figure panel.\\n- No fake data and no real-looking scientific content may\
  \ appear inside placeholders. Faint abstract grid texture is allowed only if it\
  \ cannot be mistaken for data.\\n- Outside placeholders, do not draw particle-labeled\
  \ icons, equation badges, process badges, or symbolic physics diagrams. Use public\
  \ text only for scientific claims and generic abstract icons for decoration.\\n-\
  \ Later, these placeholders will be replaced with real figures. Therefore they must\
  \ be rectangular, unobstructed, and have enough padding.\\n- Never add captions\
  \ under placeholders that describe drawn content as if the figure were already present;\
  \ captions may describe the future intended content only.\\n\\nDECORATIVE ART GUIDANCE:\\\
  n- Decorative artwork must remain abstract.\\n- Focus decorative art on abstract\
  \ atmosphere, geometry, light, and texture; all plots, tables, and scientific diagrams\
  \ belong only in labeled placeholders.\\n- The title/header artwork must be abstract\
  \ detector or beamline art only.\\n- Keep decorative art abstract; reserve Feynman\
  \ diagrams for [FIG NN] placeholders only.\\n- Use abstract geometric motifs rather\
  \ than specific particle notation in header artwork.\\n- Reserve process diagrams,\

  \ poster spec.\\n- Only [FIG 01]-style placeholders may contain source-figure diagram\
  \ slots.\\n- Use abstract decorative design instead; imply discovery, evidence for\

  \ Model predictions.\\n- Use abstract decorative design instead; generalize the\

  \ exclusions, p-values, event yields, efficiencies, or background compositions not\

  \ as directly comparable to neutrinoless double beta decay limits without explaining\
  \ the different lepton flavor and collider context.\\n- Keep confidence-level terminology\
  \ precise, especially for observed versus expected limits.\\n- Use HEP notation\
  \ accurately and avoid replacing physics symbols with ambiguous prose when equations\
  \ or standard variables are clearer.\\n\\nPLACEHOLDER REFERENCE LIST (aspect ratios\
  \ are mandatory; no pixel-level target is required):\\n- [FIG 01]: label \\\"95%\
  \ CL limits on |VμN|² versus mN\\\"; aspect ratio \\\"1:1 square\\\"; visible dashed\
  \ width/height ≈ 1.00; visual shape: true square; width and height should look equal.\\\
  n- [FIG 02]: label \\\"Post-fit H_T/p_T(μ1) distributions in SRs and CRs\\\"; aspect\

  \ wide panel with width:height about 2.5:1; not 3.5:1, 4:1, or a thin ribbon.\\\
  n- [FIG 03]: label \\\"VBF heavy Majorana neutrino diagram\\\"; aspect ratio \\\"\
  1.2:1\\\"; visible dashed width/height ≈ 1.20; visual shape: near-square panel with\
  \ width:height about 1.20:1; only slightly wider than tall, not a 1.5:1 landscape\
  \ card or banner.\\n- [FIG 04]: label \\\"VBF Weinberg-operator diagram\\\"; aspect\
  \ ratio \\\"1.2:1\\\"; visible dashed width/height ≈ 1.20; visual shape: near-square\
  \ panel with width:height about 1.20:1; only slightly wider than tall, not a 1.5:1\
  \ landscape card or banner.\\n- Aspect ratios describe the visible dashed placeholder\
  \ rectangle, not the surrounding decorative card. The dashed rectangle itself is\
  \ what will be audited.\\n- Exact allowed placeholder IDs: [FIG 01], [FIG 02], [FIG\
  \ 03], [FIG 04]. Do not render any other [FIG NN] box.\\n- Interpret X:Y literally\
  \ as width:height = X:Y. For example, 2.5:1 means the width is about two and a half\
  \ heights, not three, four, or seven heights.\\n- A square placeholder should look\
  \ square; a wide placeholder should have real vertical presence and should not become\
  \ a thin banner.\\n- A moderate landscape placeholder such as 1.49:1 should look\
  \ only about one and a half times wider than tall; never stretch it into a panoramic\
  \ 2.5:1 or 3:1 banner.\\n- A true portrait placeholder such as 1:1.99 should be\

  n- For portrait placeholders, compare the visible width/height against the printed\
  \ number: 1:1.99≈0.50, 1:1.54≈0.65, 1:1.47≈0.68.\\n- A near-portrait placeholder\
  \ such as 1:1.16 should look only slightly taller than wide; do not exaggerate it\
  \ into a narrow tall column.\\n- A square headline-result placeholder should be\
  \ prominent but not oversized: keep its side around 30-34% of the canvas width,\
  \ visibly larger than supporting scientific placeholders, never a giant sticker\
  \ covering most of the result card.\\n- For square placeholders, the visible light/white\
  \ placeholder fill itself must also be square; do not put the [FIG NN] label inside\
  \ a wide white rounded rectangle and only draw a square-ish dashed fragment inside\
  \ it.\\n- Keep the square headline-result placeholder clearly above the bottom summary/conclusion\
  \ modules; its bottom edge should sit before the lower fifth of the poster begins,\
  \ with an obvious gutter below it.\\n- If a wide placeholder would become too thin\
  \ at full poster width, make it narrower or make its section taller rather than\
  \ stretching it into a ribbon.\\n- If prose, badges, or flowcharts compete with\
  \ a placeholder, reconstruct their layout around the figure: shorter equivalent\
  \ copy, side chips, stacked labels, or moved ornaments; do not make the poster sparse\
  \ just to protect geometry.\\n- Every dashed placeholder must be an interior figure\
  \ slot, not the outer border of a whole section card.\\n- Keep a clearly visible\
  \ gutter between every pair of dashed placeholders; placeholder rectangles must\
  \ never touch, overlap, or share a border.\\n- Each placeholder's surrounding figure\
  \ mat/card must be light and quiet; if a section has a dramatic dark background,\
  \ place the figure in a large warm-white inset card with padding.\\n\\nINTER-PLACEHOLDER\
  \ GUTTER RULE:\\n- The wide placeholder(s) [FIG 02] and square result placeholder(s)\
  \ [FIG 01] must be in separate non-overlapping modules with an obvious blank/card\
  \ gutter between them.\\n- Do not stack a wide distribution placeholder so close\
  \ to a square result placeholder that a replacement figure could intrude into the\
  \ next module.\\n\\nSection 1, layout: upper-left wide motivation card with two\
  \ adjacent Feynman-diagram mats and equation chips; paired near-square figure layout:\
  \ reserve separate light mats for [FIG 03], [FIG 04], each dashed rectangle only\
  \ slightly wider than tall (about 1.2:1), never a horizontal banner; place text\
  \ in side chips or a row below the pair, title: \\\"01 Physics target: LNV in VBF\
  \ same-sign dimuons\\\"\\nVisible section heading is taken from the copy deck section_title\
  \ unit above; do not repeat that heading again as a body bullet, badge, or callout.\\\
  nStory role: motivation\\nStory synopsis for layout emphasis (do not render verbatim):\
  \ Same-sign W bosons in VBF can probe lepton-number violation through either a heavy\
  \ t-channel Majorana neutrino N or the dimension-five Weinberg operator. The final\
  \ state is two same-sign muons plus two VBF jets, targeting a μμ collider channel\
  \ not accessible to low-energy ee-focused LNV searches.\\nStory text budget: title\
  \ + one-sentence motivation + 4 short bullets + 2 equation chips\\nAuthoritative\
  \ copy deck text for this section (render public text from these units; do not render\
  \ C/Q IDs or evidence):\\n- badge, priority=must, max≈32 chars; style=primary badge:\
  \ \\\"same-sign μμ + VBF jets\\\"\\n- figure_headline, priority=must, max≈28 chars;\
  \ near [FIG 03]; style=figure-side headline: \\\"Heavy-N VBF topology\\\"\\n- figure_headline,\
  \ priority=must, max≈36 chars; near [FIG 04]; style=figure-side headline: \\\"Weinberg-operator\
  \ VBF topology\\\"\\n- bullet, priority=must, max≈66 chars; style=mini bullet: \\\
  \"Heavy Majorana N: t-channel exchange with mixing VμN\\\"\\n- bullet, priority=must,\
  \ max≈62 chars; style=mini bullet: \\\"Weinberg operator: C5^{μμ}/Λ gives effective\
  \ mμμ\\\"\\n- callout, priority=must, max≈68 chars; style=primary callout: \\\"\
  VBF tests heavy N and the dimension-five Weinberg operator\\\"\\n- callout, priority=should,\
  \ max≈28 chars; style=tiny formula chip: \\\"mμμ = C5^{μμ}v²/Λ\\\"\\nCopy-deck density\
  \ rule for this figure-containing section: render must-priority units first and\
  \ at most 3 ordinary bullets; rewrite should/could units as compact chips or side\
  \ labels before shrinking placeholders, while preserving the target information\
  \ density.\\nNear-square placeholder section design: [FIG 03]=~1.2:1, [FIG 04]=~1.2:1;\
  \ each dashed rectangle should look almost square, only slightly wider than tall.\
  \ For paired near-square placeholders, each visible dashed box must be wider than\
  \ tall (for 1.2:1, height is about 83% of width), not portrait or square-tall. Do\
  \ not use 1.5:1, 16:10, portrait, or generic landscape tiles for these placeholders.\\\
  nUse these blank placeholders in this section (do not draw their content):\\n- [FIG\
  \ 03]: blank rectangular placeholder only; label \\\"VBF heavy Majorana neutrino\
  \ diagram\\\"; aspect ratio \\\"1.2:1\\\"; inside the box write only the exact ID,\
  \ label, and aspect ratio.\\n- [FIG 04]: blank rectangular placeholder only; label\
  \ \\\"VBF Weinberg-operator diagram\\\"; aspect ratio \\\"1.2:1\\\"; inside the\
  \ box write only the exact ID, label, and aspect ratio.\\nDo not render separate\
  \ captions directly above or below these placeholder boxes; keep their replacement\
  \ area visually clear.\\nKeep bullets/text, flowcharts, badges, and decorative artwork\
  \ outside every placeholder rectangle with a clear visual gutter.\\nUse a light\
  \ neutral figure-card surface for this whole figure area; dark or saturated colors\
  \ are allowed only as thin framing accents outside the light card.\\n\\nSection\
  \ 2, layout: upper-right tall analysis card with fact badges and compact selection\
  \ bullets, title: \\\"02 Dataset, objects, and VBF event selection\\\"\\nVisible\
  \ section heading is taken from the copy deck section_title unit above; do not repeat\
  \ that heading again as a body bullet, badge, or callout.\\nStory role: dataset\\\
  nStory synopsis for layout emphasis (do not render verbatim): The analysis uses\
  \ CMS pp collision data collected in 2016–2018 at √s = 13 TeV, corresponding to\
  \ 138 fb⁻¹. Events are selected with exactly two same-sign muons and at least two\
  \ high-mass, well-separated VBF jets, with lepton, b-jet, and τ vetoes to suppress\
  \ backgrounds.\\nStory text budget: fact badges + 5 compact selection bullets\\\
  nAuthoritative copy deck text for this section (render public text from these units;\
  \ do not render C/Q IDs or evidence):\\n- badge, priority=must, max≈20 chars; style=primary\
  \ badge: \\\"CMS 2016–2018\\\"\\n- badge, priority=must, max≈18 chars; style=primary\
  \ badge: \\\"√s = 13 TeV\\\"\\n- badge, priority=must, max≈16 chars; style=primary\
  \ badge: \\\"138 fb⁻¹\\\"\\nDraw this as a polished public text-only HEP analysis\
  \ schematic, not a source-figure placeholder:\\n- Render only the listed node labels\
  \ and short directional arrows; do NOT render instruction sentences verbatim and\
  \ do NOT add generic stage labels.\\n- Use equal-sized rounded rectangular nodes,\
  \ light node interiors, accent-color borders/arrows, subtle shadows, and readable\
  \ compact typography.\\n- If a node label contains '|', show it as a clean branch\
  \ or split node with parallel sub-flow labels; otherwise keep a simple left-to-right\
  \ or top-to-bottom chain.\\n- Preserve explicit analysis symbols, subscripts, units,\
  \ and region names in node text when supplied; do not convert them into standalone\
  \ icons.\\n- No circular node icons, pictograms, mini charts, fake axes, particle/equation-symbol\
  \ badges, or decorative Feynman/process diagrams.\\n- This schematic should look\
  \ like a professional SR/CR/fit summary for HEP readers, with concrete cuts, regions,\
  \ observables, uncertainties, or statistical methods visible in the nodes.\\n- Node\
  \ label: \\\"2016--2018 pp data: sqrt{s}=13 TeV, 138 fb^-1\\\"\\n- Node label: \\\
  \"Single-muon triggers pT>24 or 27 GeV; dimuon triggers add up to 4% acceptance\\\
  \"\\n- Node label: \\\"Two SS muons: pT>30 GeV, |eta|<2.4\\\"\\n- Node label: \\\
  \">=2 jets: pT>30 GeV, |eta|<4.7; leading-pT pair defines VBF candidates\\\"\\n-\
  \ Node label: \\\"VBF jets: |Delta eta_jj|>2.5, mjj>750 GeV, max(Z_l)<0.75\\\"\\\
  nCaption: \\\"Selection emphasizes a VBF topology with two same-sign muons and large-mass,\
  \ well-separated jets.\\\"\\n\\nSection 3, layout: middle full-width strategy band\
  \ with wide post-fit distribution figure and side notes, title: \\\"03 Regions,\
  \ backgrounds, and fit observables\\\"\\nVisible section heading is taken from the\
  \ copy deck section_title unit above; do not repeat that heading again as a body\
  \ bullet, badge, or callout.\\nStory role: method\\nStory synopsis for layout emphasis\
  \ (do not render verbatim): Two signal interpretations share the H_T/p_T(μ₁) discriminant\
  \ but use interpretation-specific SR binning: Δφ_{μμ} for heavy Majorana neutrinos\
  \ and p_T^{miss} for the Weinberg operator. A simultaneous fit includes SRs and\
  \ CRs enriched in WZ and nonprompt-lepton backgrounds.\\nStory text budget: section\
  \ title + 2 mini-blocks, each with 3–4 bullets\\nAuthoritative copy deck text for\
  \ this section (render public text from these units; do not render C/Q IDs or evidence):\\\
  n- fit_strategy, priority=must, max≈64 chars; style=normal-small node; render as\
  \ a fit-model callout connected to the result/fit figure: \\\"Profile likelihood\
  \ + constrained nuisances; modified CLs\\\"\\n- figure_headline, priority=must,\
  \ max≈64 chars; near [FIG 02]; style=figure-side headline: \\\"Post-fit HT/pT(μ1)\
  \ distributions across SRs and CRs\\\"\\n- uncertainty, priority=should, max≈58\
  \ chars; style=micro callout; render as a small nuisance/uncertainty chip for HEP\
  \ experts: \\\"WW, WZ, and tZq normalizations float in the fit\\\"\\n- uncertainty,\
  \ priority=should, max≈48 chars; style=micro badge; render as a small nuisance/uncertainty\
  \ chip for HEP experts: \\\"Total uncertainties are statistically dominated\\\"\\\
  nCopy-deck density rule for this figure-containing section: render must-priority\
  \ units first and at most 2 ordinary bullets; rewrite should/could units as compact\
  \ chips or side labels before shrinking placeholders, while preserving the target\
  \ information density.\\nWide-figure section design: draw the dashed placeholder\
  \ as width:height about 2.5:1; give it a substantial, readable light figure zone;\
  \ reflow nearby prose into compact side/bottom tiers before making it look like\
  \ a thin ribbon.\\nUse these blank placeholders in this section (do not draw their\
  \ content):\\n- [FIG 02]: blank rectangular placeholder only; label \\\"Post-fit\
  \ H_T/p_T(μ1) distributions in SRs and CRs\\\"; aspect ratio \\\"2.5:1 wide\\\"\
  ; inside the box write only the exact ID, label, and aspect ratio.\\nDo not render\
  \ separate captions directly above or below these placeholder boxes; keep their\
  \ replacement area visually clear.\\nKeep bullets/text, flowcharts, badges, and\
  \ decorative artwork outside every placeholder rectangle with a clear visual gutter.\\\
  nUse a light neutral figure-card surface for this whole figure area; dark or saturated\
  \ colors are allowed only as thin framing accents outside the light card.\\nOptional\
  \ compact public text-only analysis flowchart: draw it only if the wide placeholder\
  \ remains visually substantial; simplify the flowchart before shrinking or distorting\
  \ any placeholder.\\n- Render only the listed node labels and short directional\
  \ arrows; do NOT render instruction sentences verbatim and do NOT add generic stage\
  \ labels.\\n- Use equal-sized rounded rectangular nodes, light node interiors, accent-color\
  \ borders/arrows, subtle shadows, and readable compact typography.\\n- If a node\
  \ label contains '|', show it as a clean branch or split node with parallel sub-flow\
  \ labels; otherwise keep a simple left-to-right or top-to-bottom chain.\\n- Preserve\
  \ explicit analysis symbols, subscripts, units, and region names in node text when\
  \ supplied; do not convert them into standalone icons.\\n- No circular node icons,\
  \ pictograms, mini charts, fake axes, particle/equation-symbol badges, or decorative\
  \ Feynman/process diagrams.\\n- This schematic should look like a professional SR/CR/fit\
  \ summary for HEP readers, with concrete cuts, regions, observables, uncertainties,\
  \ or statistical methods visible in the nodes.\\n- Node label: \\\"Heavy Majorana\
  \ signal: MGvATNLO 2.6.5 NLO; m_N scan 50 GeV--25 TeV\\\"\\n- Node label: \\\"Weinberg\
  \ signal: C_5^{ll'}=1, Lambda=200 TeV; cross section scales as |C_5^{ll'}/Lambda|^2\\\
  \"\\n- Node label: \\\"EW WW and W^{pm}Z leptonic backgrounds: MGvATNLO 2.4.2 LO,\
  \ O(alpha^6), zero QCD vertices\\\"\\n- Node label: \\\"tZq background: initial-state\
  \ b removed from W^{pm}Z; simulated NLO with MGvATNLO 2.3.3\\\"\\n- Node label:\
  \ \\\"WW double-parton scattering: LO PYTHIA 8.226 for 2016; 8.230 for 2017--2018\\\
  \"\\n\\nSection 4, layout: central hero result card with largest square limit plot\
  \ and prominent result callouts; square-first hero layout: reserve a true square\
  \ dashed result placeholder above the bottom conclusion zone, then place compact\
  \ result text beside it, title: \\\"04 Headline constraints at 95% confidence level\\\
  \"\\nVisible section heading is taken from the copy deck section_title unit above;\
  \ do not repeat that heading again as a body bullet, badge, or callout.\\nStory\
  \ role: result\\nStory synopsis for layout emphasis (do not render verbatim): The\
  \ observed data are consistent with Standard Model predictions. The analysis sets\
  \ 95% CL upper limits on |V_{μN}|² versus m_N and an observed 95% CL upper limit\
  \ |m_{μμ}| < 10.8 GeV for the Weinberg-operator interpretation.\\nStory text budget:\
  \ large result callout + 4 bullets + one small Weinberg result badge\\nAuthoritative\
  \ copy deck text for this section (render public text from these units; do not render\
  \ C/Q IDs or evidence):\\n- figure_headline, priority=must, max≈46 chars; near [FIG\
  \ 01]; style=figure-side headline: \\\"95% CL limits on |VμN|² versus mN\\\"\\n-\
  \ bullet, priority=must, max≈66 chars; style=mini bullet: \\\"For mN ≳ 650 GeV:\
  \ strongest LHC constraints reported\\\"\\n- callout, priority=must, max≈52 chars;\
  \ style=primary callout: \\\"Data agree with Standard Model predictions\\\"\\n-\
  \ callout, priority=must, max≈58 chars; style=primary badge: \\\"|VμN|² constrained\
  \ for mN = 50 GeV–25 TeV\\\"\\nCopy-deck density rule for this figure-containing\
  \ section: render must-priority units first and at most 2 ordinary bullets; rewrite\
  \ should/could units as compact chips or side labels before shrinking placeholders,\
  \ while preserving the target information density.\\nHero visual priority: make\
  \ this section's hero placeholder visibly dominant within its card while preserving\
  \ the exact placeholder aspect ratio and light figure surface.\\nSquare-placeholder\
  \ section design: reserve a true square dashed rectangle with square light/white\
  \ fill; the surrounding figure card/mat must also be light, although it may have\
  \ dramatic outer outlines, halos, ribbons, or side accents. The placeholder itself\
  \ cannot be a landscape box or wide white rounded rectangle. For a headline result,\
  \ make the square substantial yet moderate, visibly larger than supporting placeholders,\
  \ with visible surrounding light-card breathing room; do not let it descend into\
  \ the bottom summary/conclusion zone.\\nUse these blank placeholders in this section\
  \ (do not draw their content):\\n- [FIG 01]: blank rectangular placeholder only;\
  \ label \\\"95% CL limits on |VμN|² versus mN\\\"; aspect ratio \\\"1:1 square\\\
  \"; inside the box write only the exact ID, label, and aspect ratio.\\nDo not render\
  \ separate captions directly above or below these placeholder boxes; keep their\
  \ replacement area visually clear.\\nKeep bullets/text, flowcharts, badges, and\
  \ decorative artwork outside every placeholder rectangle with a clear visual gutter.\\\
  nUse a light neutral figure-card surface for this whole figure area; dark or saturated\
  \ colors are allowed only as thin framing accents outside the light card.\\n\\nSection\
  \ 5, layout: lower full-width summary strip with compact cards and no additional\
  \ figures, title: \\\"05 Interpretation and scope\\\"\\nStory role: interpretation\\\
  nStory synopsis for layout emphasis (do not render verbatim): This VBF same-sign\
  \ dimuon search probes LNV in the muon channel and reports constraints under specific\
  \ heavy-neutrino and Weinberg-operator assumptions. The results should be read as\
  \ collider μμ constraints, not as evidence for LNV or as direct ee neutrinoless-double-beta-decay\
  \ comparisons.\\nStory text budget: one-sentence takeaway + 4 compact scope bullets\\\
  nNo copy-deck units assigned to this section; keep rendered prose minimal and do\
  \ not invent extra science copy.\\n\\nConclusion box titled \\\"Conclusion and prospects\\\
  \" with public bullets:\\n- \\\"CMS observes agreement with Standard Model predictions\
  \ in VBF same-sign dimuon events at √s = 13 TeV using 138 fb⁻¹.\\\"\\n- \\\"The\
  \ search constrains |VμN|² for mN = 50 GeV–25 TeV and improves LHC constraints for\
  \ mN ≳ 650 GeV as stated in the analysis.\\\"\\n- \\\"The Weinberg-operator interpretation\
  \ gives an observed 95% CL upper limit |mμμ| < 10.8 GeV in the collider μμ channel.\\\
  \"\\nClosing line: \\\"Questions welcome • CMS EXO-21-003 • HEPData record available\\\
  \"\\nConclusion hard constraint: the conclusion box must contain ONLY the public\
  \ bullets and closing line listed above. Do not add any workflow, placeholder, replacement,\
  \ validation, TODO, or production-process bullet.\\n\\nLayout quality constraints:\\\
  n- Copy all section titles, placeholder labels, and public conclusion bullets exactly\
  \ as supplied; do not misspell or paraphrase headings.\\n- Do not invent extra placeholder\
  \ IDs. Render exactly the listed [FIG NN] placeholders and no additional figure\
  \ boxes.\\n- Make placeholder boxes geometrically clean and easy to detect for replacement:\
  \ blank interior, dashed/subtle border, exact [FIG NN] text, label, and aspect-ratio\
  \ text.\\n- Match each placeholder's declared aspect ratio closely; width/height\
  \ should visibly agree with the source ratio, not just the label text.\\n- Keep\
  \ all section cards aligned to a coherent grid, but avoid a monotonous tiled template;\
  \ use editorial hierarchy, varied card scale, non-square cards, and shaped callouts.\\\
  n- The poster must not look like a simple wireframe; it should feel like a finished\
  \ premium visual design with placeholders ready for production replacement.\\n-\
  \ Use modern rounded cards, subtle shadows, scientific background art, glow/depth\
  \ effects, and coherent accent colors.\\n- Use sophisticated typography and palette:\
  \ editorial sans-serif type, disciplined type scale, deep atmospheric background,\
  \ cobalt/violet/gold accents, and warm-white content cards.\\n- Never use dark-filled\
  \ blocks for chart/plot/diagram sections; if the surrounding poster is dark, put\
  \ every figure on a large light paper card or mat.\\n- If you use summary pills\
  \ or badges, keep their icons generic and their labels word-based; do not use standalone\
  \ physics-symbol badges such as μμ, ν, W, N, ΔL, or equation fragments.\\n- Preserve\
  \ enough whitespace for later replacement; no decorative artwork may overlap a placeholder\
  \ rectangle.\\n- Keep placeholder-to-placeholder gutters obvious; final real figures\
  \ must fit inside their own dashed boxes without protruding into neighboring modules.\\\
  n- Visually group many placeholders into one hero result, supporting analysis figures,\
  \ and smaller diagnostics rather than equal tiles.\\n\",\n  \"detected_placeholders\"\
  : {\n    \"image_size\": {\n      \"width\": 1024,\n      \"height\": 1536\n   \

sections:
- id: 1
  title: 'Physics target: LNV in VBF same-sign dimuons'
  layout: upper-left wide motivation card with two adjacent Feynman-diagram mats and
    equation chips
  text:
  - title: Why this channel?
    body:
    - Same-sign W bosons in VBF can probe lepton-number violation through either a
      heavy Majorana neutrino or the dimension-five Weinberg operator.
    bullets:
    - 'Final state: two same-sign muons plus two VBF jets.'
    - 'Majorana-neutrino hypothesis: heavy t-channel N with mass mN.'
    - 'Weinberg operator: C5μμ/Λ generates an effective μμ Majorana mass mμμ.'
    - Collider μμ searches complement low-energy ee-focused LNV probes.
  caption: Representative VBF diagrams for same-sign dimuon production mediated by
    a heavy Majorana neutrino and by the Weinberg operator.
- id: 2
  title: Dataset, objects, and VBF event selection
  layout: upper-right tall analysis card with fact badges and compact selection bullets
  text:
  - title: CMS pp collision sample
    body:
    - The analysis uses CMS data collected in 2016–2018 at √s = 13 TeV, corresponding
      to 138 fb⁻¹.
    bullets:
    - 'Triggers: single-muon pT > 24 or 27 GeV, with dimuon triggers improving acceptance
      by up to 4%.'
    - 'Signal-region muons: exactly two same-sign μ, pT > 30 GeV and |η| < 2.4.'
    - 'VBF jets: at least two jets with pT > 30 GeV and |η| < 4.7.'
    - 'VBF topology: mjj > 750 GeV, |Δηjj| > 2.5, max(Zℓ) < 0.75.'
  flowchart: &id001
  - '2016--2018 pp data: sqrt{s}=13 TeV, 138 fb^-1'
  - Single-muon triggers pT>24 or 27 GeV; dimuon triggers add up to 4% acceptance
  - 'Two SS muons: pT>30 GeV, |eta|<2.4'
  - '>=2 jets: pT>30 GeV, |eta|<4.7; leading-pT pair defines VBF candidates'
  - 'VBF jets: |Delta eta_jj|>2.5, mjj>750 GeV, max(Z_l)<0.75'
  caption: Selection emphasizes a VBF topology with two same-sign muons and large-mass,
    well-separated jets.
- id: 3
  title: Regions, backgrounds, and fit observables
  layout: middle full-width strategy band with wide post-fit distribution figure and
    side notes
  text:
  - title: Analysis strategy
    body:
    - Two signal interpretations use the same HT/pT(μ1) discriminant, with different
      SR binning chosen for the heavy-neutrino and Weinberg-operator topologies.
    bullets:
    - 'Heavy Majorana neutrino SR: Δφμμ > 2 and Δφμμ < 2 bins.'
    - 'Weinberg-operator SR: pTmiss < 50 GeV and pTmiss > 50 GeV bins.'
    - 'Control regions: WZ, b-tagged, and WZb samples constrain reducible backgrounds.'
    - 'Dominant SR backgrounds: SM electroweak W±W± production and nonprompt leptons.'
  - title: Statistical model
    body: []
    bullets:
    - Profile-likelihood ratio with constrained nuisance parameters.
    - Modified frequentist CLs with asymptotic approximation.
    - WW, WZ, and tZq normalization factors float with signal strength.
    - 'Largest impact: statistical uncertainty in signal/background templates; total
      uncertainties are statistically dominated.'
  flowchart: &id002
  - 'Heavy Majorana signal: MGvATNLO 2.6.5 NLO; m_N scan 50 GeV--25 TeV'
  - 'Weinberg signal: C_5^{ll''}=1, Lambda=200 TeV; cross section scales as |C_5^{ll''}/Lambda|^2'
  - 'EW WW and W^{pm}Z leptonic backgrounds: MGvATNLO 2.4.2 LO, O(alpha^6), zero QCD
    vertices'
  - 'tZq background: initial-state b removed from W^{pm}Z; simulated NLO with MGvATNLO
    2.3.3'
  - 'WW double-parton scattering: LO PYTHIA 8.226 for 2016; 8.230 for 2017--2018'
  caption: Post-fit HT/pT(μ1) distributions compare data, SM backgrounds, and scaled
    signal hypotheses across signal and control regions.
- id: 4
  title: Headline constraints at 95% confidence level
  layout: central hero result card with largest square limit plot and prominent result
    callouts
  text:
  - title: Heavy Majorana neutrino limits
    body:
    - The data agree with Standard Model predictions, leading to upper limits on |VμN|²
      over mN = 50 GeV–25 TeV.
    bullets:
    - For mN ≳ 650 GeV, the constraints are the most stringent from LHC searches reported
      in the paper.
    - The analysis sets first direct limits for mN > 2 TeV in this VBF approach.
    - Limits with |VμN|² > 1 are not physically meaningful and are interpreted accordingly.
  - title: Weinberg-operator result
    body: []
    bullets:
    - 'Observed 95% CL upper limit: |mμμ| < 10.8 GeV.'
    - 'Expected 95% CL upper limit: |mμμ| < 12.8 GeV.'
    - This is the first collider test of the μμ Weinberg-operator scenario reported
      by the analysis.
  caption: Observed and expected 95% CL upper limits on |VμN|² as a function of heavy-neutrino
    mass mN, compared with earlier CMS limits shown in the paper.
- id: 5
  title: Interpretation and scope
  layout: lower full-width summary strip with compact cards and no additional figures
  text:
  - title: What is constrained
    body:
    - This VBF same-sign dimuon search probes LNV in the muon channel without observing
      a deviation from the Standard Model.
    bullets:
    - 'Heavy-neutrino interpretation: one heavy state coupled through the muon mixing
      element VμN.'
    - 'Signal mass scan: mN from 50 GeV to 25 TeV.'
    - 'Weinberg interpretation: limit expressed through |C5μμ/Λ|² and converted to
      |mμμ|.'
    - Results are specific to the collider μμ channel and should not be conflated
      with ee neutrinoless double beta decay limits.
